> *bhuvanyathā no viśve vṛdhāsaḥ karantuṣāhā vidhuraṃ na śavaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 118

*Running head: [118 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 186].*

*[A stray line in the supplied text before the Pada: १ हदिनाल्कु १ (*1 hadinālku 1*); not part of the printed Pada.]*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । नः । विश्वे । आस्क्र्याः । गमंतु । देवाः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । वरुणः । सजोषाः ।
> भुवन् । यथा । नः । विश्वे । वृधासः । करन् । सुसहा । विधुरं । न । शवः ॥ २ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> वैश्वदेवे पशावा नो विश्व इत्येषा हविषः पुरोनुवाक्या । आ नो देवाना-
> मुपवेतु शंस आ नो विश्व आस्त्वा गमंतु देवाः । आ ३-७ । इति ॥
> नोऽस्माकं यज्ञं विश्वे सर्वॆ देवा आस्माः शत्रूणामास्कंदयितार आक्र-
> मितारो वा आ गमंतु । आगच्छंतु । के ते । मित्रोऽर्यमा वरुणश्च त्रयोऽपि
> सजोषाः समानप्रीतयः संत आगच्छंतु । किंतु विश्वे देवा नोस्माकं वृधासो
> वर्धयितारो यथा भुवन् भवेयुः तथा सुषाहा सुष्टु शत्रूणामभिभवेन नोs-
> स्मदीयं शपोऽन्नं विथुरं हीनं यथा न करन् न कुर्युः तथागच्छंतु ॥

*Gist:* May all the gods, with Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa united in affection, come to our sacrifice, overcoming foes, and not leave our food diminished.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

विश्वे (देवाः) (*viśve (devāḥ)*) — the Viśve Devāḥ. नः (*naḥ*) — to us. वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*) — as increasers. भुवन् (*bhuvan*) — as they became (and). सुषाहा (*suṣāhā*) — by defeating and destroying the enemies. नः (*naḥ*) — of us. शवः (*śavaḥ*) — the food. विधुरं (*vidhuraṃ*) — diminished. न करन् (*na karan*) — as they do not make (so). मित्रः (*mitraḥ*) — Mitra. आर्यमा (*āryamā*) — Aryaman (printed "ಆರಮ್ಯ"). वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) — Varuṇa. विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*) — all these gods. सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — of one equal affection. आस्क्राः (*āskrāḥ*) — resisting (our enemies). नः (*naḥ*) — to our sacrifice. आ गमंतु (*ā gamaṃtu*) — may they come.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May the Viśve Devāḥ become increasers for us, and, by defeating and destroying our enemies, not make our food nothing but augment it; and may Mitra, Aryaman (printed "ಅರಮ್ಯ") and Varuṇa, and all these gods too, united in equal affection and resisting our enemies, come to our sacrifice.

**Printed English translation**

May all the triumphant gods, Mitra, Aryaman, Varuna equally well pleased, come (to our rite) : may they all be propitious to us: may they not leave us in want of food, after overcoming (our foes).

### Printed p. 119

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 119 (as supplied, "ಅ. ೨ ಅ. ೫. ವ. ೪").*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

When the oblation addressed to the Viśve Devāḥ is offered in the animal sacrifice, this ṛk beginning आ नो विश्वे (*ā no viśve*) is to be used as the *puro-'nuvākyā* mantra; this is set out in the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra नो देवानामुपवेतु शंस आ नो विश्व आस्प्रागमंतु देवाः ऎंब सूत्रदिंद।(आ. (*no devānāmupavetu śaṃsa ā no viśva āsprāgamaṃtu devāḥ èṃba sūtradiṃda|(ā.*) (as printed).

आस्क्रा:-शत्रुगळन्नु (*āskrā:-śatrugaḷannu*) — those who defeat or attack the enemies. It is prayed that the gods, having defeated our enemies, come to our sacrificial ground and bestow on us food and other nourishment.

विश्वे देवाः—ऎल्ला देवतॆगळू (*viśve devāḥ—èllā devatègaḷū*) — all the gods are here prayed to come together with the deities Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa. If it is asked whether, when "all the gods" is said, the deities Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa are not already included among them, the answer is: although they are included, the names of these three are mentioned separately in order to stress that these three must come without fail.

मित्र: अर्यमा, वरुण:—ई मूरुदेवतॆगळू प्रत्येकदेवतॆगळॆंदु भाविसल्पट्टिद्दरू (*mitra: aryamā, varuṇa:—ī mūrudevatègaḷū pratyekadevatègaḷèṃdu bhāvisalpaṭṭiddarū*) — although these three deities are regarded as separate deities, it appears from what is explained here that they are the part-deities of that name among the many forms of the Sun, that is, among the twelve Ādityas. Besides, in some places it is said that these three deities are other forms of Agni:

त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः । (*tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro bhavasi yatsamiddhaḥ |*)
(((पु. सं ५-३-१) (*((pu. saṃ 5-3-1)*), as printed with a doubled parenthesis; the book prints "ಪು. ಸಂ")
त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन् गुह्यं बिभर्षि । (*tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ nāma svadhāvan guhyaṃ bibharṣi |*)
((मि. सं. ५-३-२) (*(mi. saṃ. 5-3-2)*), as printed; the book prints "ಮಿ. ಸಂ.")

in these ṛks it is said that Agni has these three names: Varuṇa when he is born, Mitra when he is well kindled and blazing, and Aryaman in the offerings connected with the maiden (marriage rites). Moreover, in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:

मित्रोऽसि वरुणोऽसीत्याह । मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः । अहोरात्रा- भ्यामेवैनमुपावहरति (*mitro 'si varuṇo 'sītyāha | maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ | ahorātrā- bhyāmevainamupāvaharati*)
((कै. ब्रा, १-७-१०-१) (*(kai. brā, 1-7-10-1)*), as printed; the book prints "ಕೈ. ಬ್ರಾ,")

it is said that Mitra is the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night. It should therefore be noted that these three deities are in some places said to be part-deities of the Sun and in some places different names of Agni.

### Printed p. 120

*Running head: [120 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186]. The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 of Sūkta 186 (Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa) from p. 119; no new ṛk begins in this window.*

In the Purāṇas and elsewhere Mitra is one of the twelve Ādityas. In the Ṛgveda, though Mitra is another name of the Sun, Mitra has a distinct individuality, that is, a personal importance of his own. In the Ṛgveda Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are said to be sons of Aditi, and so they are in many places called Ādityas. That these Ādityas, that is, the sons of Aditi, are six in number:

इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो धृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि । (*imā gira ādityebhyo dhṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi |*)
शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥ (*śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*)

((म सं. २-२७-१) (*(ma saṃ. 2-27-1)*), as printed; the book prints "ಮ ಸಂ.")

that is, only six names are given: Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa and Aṃśa.

देवा आदित्या ये सप्त तेभिः सोमाभि रक्ष न इंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव । (*devā ādityā ye sapta tebhiḥ somābhi rakṣa na iṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava |*)
((पु. सं ९-११४-३) (*(pu. saṃ 9-114-3)*), as printed; the book prints "ಪು. ಸಂ")

in this मक्किनल्लि (*makkinalli*) [as printed] it is said that the sons of Aditi are seven.

अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्व १ स्परि । (*aṣṭau putrāso aditerye jātāstanva 1 spari |*)
देवा उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः परा मार्तंडमास्यत् । (*devā upapraitsaptabhiḥ parā mārtaṃḍamāsyat |*)
सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुप प्रैत्तूर्व्यं युगं । (*saptabhiḥ putrairaditirupa praittūrvyaṃ yugaṃ |*)
प्रजायै मृत्यवे त्वत्पुनर्मार्तंडमाभरत् ॥ (*prajāyai mṛtyave tvatpunarmārtaṃḍamābharat ‖*)
((म. सं. १०-७२-८, ९) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-72-8, 9)*))

in these ṛks it is said that Aditi had first seven and then Mārtaṇḍa, eight sons in all. (The supplied text has जातास्तन्व १ स्परि (*jātāstanva 1 spari*) in the first line, with a stray "೧".) Besides, in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka:

अष्टा पुत्रासो आदितेः । ये जातास्तन्वः परि । देवा उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः । परामार्तंडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उपप्रैत्सूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्यवे तत् । परामार्तंडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्- श्चेत्येते । (*aṣṭā putrāso āditeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥ pari | devā upapraitsaptabhiḥ | parāmārtaṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upapraitsūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyave tat | parāmārtaṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāg- ścetyete |*)
((कृ. आ. १-१३-३) (*(kṛ. ā. 1-13-3)*), "ಕೃ. ಆ." as printed)

the names of the eight sons of Aditi are also given: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryaman, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān are said to be those eight. The same matter is stated in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:

अदिति पुत्रकामा । साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मौदनमपचत् । तस्या उच्चे- षणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्यै धाता चार्यमा चाजा- (*aditi putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmaudanamapacat | tasyā ucce- ṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyai dhātā cāryamā cājā-*)

### Printed p. 121

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 121 (as supplied).*

येतां । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्यॆ मित्रश्च वरुणश्चाजायेतां । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या अगंशश्च भगश्चाजायेतां । सा चतुर्थमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्ंश्चाजायेतां (*yetāṃ | sā dvitīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyè mitraśca varuṇaścājāyetāṃ | sā tṛtīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā agaṃśaśca bhagaścājāyetāṃ | sā caturthamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā iṃdraśca vivasvāgṃścājāyetāṃ*)
((तै. ब्रा. १-१-९-१, २, ३.) (*(tai. brā. 1-1-9-1, 2, 3.)*))

The matter that Aditi obtained eight sons is clearly set out here. Of these eight, the three Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are especially famous in the Ṛgveda. In the sūkta २-२७ने (*2-27ne*) of the Ṛg. Saṃ. there is a detailed description of the beneficent heroic deeds of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman.

मित्रः—मित्रशब्दद (*mitraḥ—mitraśabdada*) — Yāska in his Nirukta has stated the derivation of the word *mitra* in this way:

मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते । संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा । मेदयतेर्वा । (*mitraḥ pramītestrāyate | saṃminvāno dravatīti vā | medayatervā |*)
((नि. १०-२१) (*(ni. 10-21)*))

What is the meaning of the word *mitra*? ऎंदरॆ—मित्रः कस्मात् । स हि प्रमीतेः त्रायते । प्रमीतिः मरणं । (*èṃdarè—mitraḥ kasmāt | sa hi pramīteḥ trāyate | pramītiḥ maraṇaṃ |*) — *pramīti* means death. Because this deity gives rain to the people in the world, and thereby provides food and so on, and saves and protects them from the fear of death that may come from hunger, he is called Mitra.

समंततो मिन्वानः उदकेन द्रवति अंतरिक्षलोके । (*samaṃtato minvānaḥ udakena dravati aṃtarikṣaloke |*) — because this deity, being lord of water and staying in the atmosphere, makes, through the clouds, all around, that is, the whole region, drenched, that is, wet with water, he is called Mitra. Or: अथवा-स्नेहनार्थस्य (*athavā-snehanārthasya*) सर्वं ह्यसावुदकेन स्नेहयति । (*sarvaṃ hyasāvudakena snehayati |*) — because this deity makes everything cling together with water, that is, join together in one, he is called Mitra. Having given the derivation in three ways, in order to support it he has quoted the ṛk

मित्रो जनान् यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां । (*mitro janān yātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ |*)
मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं धृतवज्जु होत ॥ (*mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ dhṛtavajju hota ‖*)
((ऋ. सं. ३-५९-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 3-59-1)*))

as an example. In this ṛk Mitra, helping agricultural and other works, pouring rain and so on, providing people with food and the like, supports, that is, nourishes, the people of the earth and the dwellers of heaven. "O men, offer to this Mitra the deity

### Printed p. 122

*Running head: [122 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186].*

oblations and the like mixed with ghee": thus the unique qualities of Mitra and his beneficence to the world are very well described. The only sūkta in the Ṛgveda addressed to Mitra is this sūkta of 9 ṛks ((ऋ सं. ३-५९) (*(ṛ saṃ. 3-59)*)); elsewhere Mitra is praised together with Varuṇa and other deities.

Since the association of Mitra and Varuṇa is very close, the sūkta with Mitra alone as deity is, as said before, only one in the Ṛgveda ((ऋ. सं. ३-५९) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 3-59)*)); even there the praise of the deity is unclear. But in the first ṛk only the distinctive quality of Mitra is well stated. In the fifth ṛk of the same sūkta:

महा आदित्यो नमसोपसद्यो यातयज्जनो गृणते सुशेवः । (*mahā ādityo namasopasadyo yātayajjano gṛṇate suśevaḥ |*)
((म. सं. ३-५९-५) (*(ma. saṃ. 3-59-5)*))

this Mitra is called the great Āditya who gathers all men together. The word यातयज्ञन (*yātayajñana*) ("one who brings the people together") which gives this meaning,

व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातॆयज्जना । (*vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātèyajjanā |*)
((ऋ. सं. ५-७२-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 5-72-2)*))

in this ṛk is applied to the pair Mitra and Varuṇa, and

मित्रस्तयोर्वरुणो यातयज्जनोऽर्यमा यातयज्जनः । (*mitrastayorvaruṇo yātayajjano 'ryamā yātayajjanaḥ |*)
((म. सं. १-१३६-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-136-3)*))

in this ṛk to the three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. According to the sūkta ऋ. सं ३-५९ नॆय (*ṛ. saṃ 3-59 nèya*) [as above], Mitra is the support of heaven and earth; the five tribes of men (*pañcajanāḥ*) are obedient to him; he is the support of the life of all the other gods: so the qualities of Mitra are described. In ऋ सं. ५-८१-४ रल्लि (*ṛ saṃ. 5-81-4 ralli*) Savitṛ and Mitra are said to be one; in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā ((वा. सं. ४-३ ) (*(vā. saṃ. 4-3 )*)) Viṣṇu is said to have taken three steps following the rules of Mitra; in ऋ. सं. १०-८-४ रल्लि (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-8-4 ralli*) Agni, established before the dawn, is said to produce Mitra for himself; in ऋ. सं. ३-५-४ रल्लि (*ṛ. saṃ. 3-5-4 ralli*) the blazing Agni is said to be Mitra; in ऋ सं. ५-३-१ रल्लि (*ṛ saṃ. 5-3-1 ralli*) it is said that Agni is Varuṇa when born and Mitra when kindled;

मित्रो अग्निर्भवति यत्समिद्दो मित्रो होता वरुणो जातवेदाः । (*mitro agnirbhavati yatsamiddo mitro hotā varuṇo jātavedāḥ |*)
मित्रो अध्वर्युरिषिरो दमूना मित्रः सिंधूनामुत पर्वतानां ॥ (*mitro adhvaryuriṣiro damūnā mitraḥ siṃdhūnāmuta parvatānāṃ ‖*)
((ऋ. सं. ३-५-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 3-5-4)*))

in this ṛk the well-kindled Agni is described as Mitra, who is the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu in the sacrifice, and Varuṇa, and the Agni called Jātavedas, and the friend (benefactor) of rivers and mountains: so the qualities of Mitra are described.

### Printed p. 123

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 123 (as supplied, "ವ. .೪"). The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 of Sūkta 186 (Mitra and Varuṇa) from p. 122; no new ṛk begins in this window.*

वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) — Yāska's derivation: वरुणो वृणोतीति सतः (*varuṇo vṛṇotīti sataḥ*) ((नि. १०-२) (*(ni. 10-2)*)): because he is covered by masses of cloud this deity is called Varuṇa.

Varuṇa is a most eminent deity, equal to Indra in power and the like. The number of mantras addressed to Varuṇa is very small. There are twelve sūktas in the Ṛgveda addressed to Varuṇa, but there are twenty-four sūktas that praise Mitra and Varuṇa together.

Varuṇa has a human body and human actions; but rather than his physical body and actions the description of his moral actions and deeds is more prominent. He has a face, eyes, arms, hands and feet; he drives a chariot. This is stated plainly in the ṛks

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । (*citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-११५-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-115-1)*)
उदु त्यच्यक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धं । (*udu tyacyakṣurmahi mitrayorā eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdhaṃ |*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-५१-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 6-51-1)*)
उद्वां चक्षुर्वरुण सुप्रतीकं देवयोरेति सूर्यस्ततन्वान् । (*udvāṃ cakṣurvaruṇa supratīkaṃ devayoreti sūryastatanvān |*)
(ऋ सं. ७-६१-१) (*(ṛ saṃ. 7-61-1)*)
चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य देवश्चर्मेव यः समविव्यक् तमांसि । (*cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasya devaścarmeva yaḥ samavivyak tamāṃsi |*)
(ऋ. सं. ७-६३-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 7-63-1)*)
नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तदृतं सपर्यत । (*namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣase maho devāya tadṛtaṃ saparyata |*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-३७-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-37-1)*)

That the Sun is, as it were, his eye is found in the very first ṛk of the sūktas addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa, so it seems that this is the aspect that first comes into view whenever Mitra and Varuṇa are mentioned. And in the ṛk ७-६६-१० (*7-66-10*) it is said that Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa have the Sun as eye. That Varuṇa is far-seeing (चक्षसं (*cakṣasaṃ*)) is said in the ṛks १-२५-५ (*1-25-5*), १-२५-१६ (*1-25-16*) and others.

आ नो बर्हि रिशादसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा। सीदंतु मनुषो यथा॥ (*ā no barhi riśādaso varuṇo mitro aryamā| sīdaṃtu manuṣo yathā‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-२६-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-26-4)*)
प्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातॆयज्जना । नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोम- (*pratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātèyajjanā | ni barhiṣi sadataṃ soma-*)
पीतये ॥ (*pītaye ‖*)
(म. सं. ५-२-२) (*(ma. saṃ. 5-2-2)*)

### Printed p. 124

*[Page break of the print; the supplied text prints the header as "124 ಸಾಯಿಣಭಾವ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೪. ಸೂ. ೧೮೬" in the middle of the text, with no page marker.]*

In these and similar ṛks Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are prayed to come and sit on the sacred grass spread on the sacrificial altar for the drinking of Soma.

यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादय्यते । (*yadī sakhāyā sakhyāya somaiḥ sutebhiḥ suprayasā mādayyate |*)
(म. सं. ४-४१-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 4-41-3)*)

in these and similar ṛks it is said that Varuṇa drinks Soma along with Indra and other gods.

बिभ्रद्दापिं हिरण्ययं वरुणो वस्त निर्णिजं । परि स्पशो नि षेदिरे । (*bibhraddāpiṃ hiraṇyayaṃ varuṇo vasta nirṇijaṃ | pari spaśo ni ṣedire |*)
(म सं- १-२५-१३) (*(ma saṃ- 1-25-13)*)

in this ṛk there is the description that Varuṇa wears a golden mantle or robe and a shining garment. Varuṇa's chariot is golden, bright like the Sun, and has whips that urge the horses. Mitra and Varuṇa mount their chariot in a very high region of the sky ((ऋ सं ५-६३-१) (*(ṛ saṃ 5-63-1)*)); there are such descriptions. The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is golden and is in the upper world. And Varuṇa, sitting in his palace:

नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्ता३ स्वा । साम्राज्याय सुकृतुः । (*ni ṣasāda dhṛtavrato varuṇaḥ pastā3 svā | sāmrājyāya sukṛtuḥ |*)
अतो विश्वान्यद्भुता चिकित्त्वा अभि पश्यति । कृतानि या च कर्त्वा ॥ (*ato viśvānyadbhutā cikittvā abhi paśyati | kṛtāni yā ca kartvā ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-२५-१०, ११) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-25-10, 11)*)

sees all that goes on in the world. The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is very large, very high, firm, resting on a thousand pillars; and their house has a thousand doors (ऋ. सं. ७-८८-५ (*ṛ. saṃ. 7-88-5*)). The all-seeing Sun leaves his own dwelling and goes to the house of Mitra and Varuṇa to report the doings of men, and enters their beloved house; there are such descriptions too.

Varuṇa, alone or with Mitra, is, like other deities, called king in many places:

अबुध्ने राजा वरुणो वनस्योर्ध्वं स्तूपं ददते पूतदक्षः । (*abudhne rājā varuṇo vanasyordhvaṃ stūpaṃ dadate pūtadakṣaḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-२४-७) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-24-7)*)
त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः । (*tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. २-२७-१०) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 2-27-10)*)
तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूम । (*tena viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā yavaṃ na vṛṣṭirvyunatti bhūma |*)
(ऋ सं. ५-८५-३) (*(ṛ saṃ. 5-85-3)*)

### Printed p. 125

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 125 (as supplied).*

in these and similar ṛks it is said that Varuṇa is king not only of men but of the gods and of all the worlds. Besides Varuṇa, deities such as Indra, Yama and Soma also have the honorific name "king".

There are many stories connected with Indra, but with Varuṇa it is quite the opposite; there is not a single story. Varuṇa is much praised as the ordainer of physical and moral laws (वरुणस्य व्रतानि (*varuṇasya vratāni*)). The divine power of Mitra and Varuṇa is described by the word माया (*māyā*). When applied to the gods it means the hidden power they have to do good; when applied to demons the same word means the hidden power they have to do evil. In the good sense this word suits Mitra and Varuṇa; in the bad sense it applies to demons. As with the word असुर (*asura*), the word *māyā* is used in both senses. By this hidden *māyā* power in himself Varuṇa, standing in the atmosphere, measures the earth by the Sun as with a measuring rod. He makes the Sun cross the atmosphere and makes him dim with rain clouds. Then sweet (honey-mixed) drops fall ((ऋ. सं. ५-६३-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 5-63-4)*)). He makes the sky pour rain. Therefore this word *māyā* is applied chiefly to Varuṇa among the gods in the ṛks ६-४८-१४ (*6-48-14*); ७-२८-४ (*7-28-4*); १०-९९-१० (*10-99-10*); १०-१४७-५ (*10-147-5*) and others.

Varuṇa is the one who lays down the laws of nature; it is he who established earth and heaven. And

आसीदद्विश्वा भुवनानि संराड्विश्वेत्तानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि । (*āsīdadviśvā bhuvanāni saṃrāḍviśvettāni varuṇasya vratāni |*)
(मि, सं. ८-४२-१) (*(mi, saṃ. 8-42-1)*)

in this ṛk it is said that Varuṇa dwells in all the worlds and that his laws are observed everywhere;

तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अंतरस्मिन् तिस्रो भूमीरुःपराः षड्विधानाः । (*tisro dyāvo nihitā aṃtarasmin tisro bhūmīruḥparāḥ ṣaḍvidhānāḥ |*)
(ऋ. सं. ७-८७-५) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 7-87-5)*)

in this it is said that the three upper worlds and the three lower worlds (the nether worlds) are in his power. Varuṇa and Mitra rule the whole universe ((ऋ. सं. ५-६३-७) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 5-63-7)*)); they are the protectors of the whole world ((ऋ. सं. २-२७-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 2-27-4)*)); Varuṇa is the support of heaven, earth and sky ((ऋ. सं. ५-६९-१, ४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 5-69-1, 4)*)). He has placed fire in the water, the Sun in the sky, Soma on the stone. He has made a wide path for the Sun. Varuṇa, Mitra and

### Printed p. 126

*Running head: [126 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24: Sū. 186] (the colon is as supplied).*

Aryaman clear a path for the Sun ((ऋ सं ७-६०-४) (*(ṛ saṃ 7-60-4)*)). In many such ṛks the authority of Varuṇa is described.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā ((तै सं. ६-४-८-३) (*(tai saṃ. 6-4-8-3)*)) मित्रोऽहरजनयद्वरुणो रात्रिं (*mitro 'harajanayadvaruṇo rātriṃ*) — that is, Mitra created the day and Varuṇa the night. Therefore मैत्रं वा अहः । (*maitraṃ vā ahaḥ |*) नारुणी रात्रिः (*nāruṇī rātriḥ*) [the print has "ನಾರುಣೀ" for "ವಾರುಣೀ"]: it is said in many places that Mitra is lord of the day and Varuṇa lord of the night ((तै सं. २-१-७-४) (*(tai saṃ. 2-1-7-4)*)). In one place it is said that Varuṇa divided the seasons.

वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावशः । वेदा य उपजायते । (*veda māso dhṛtavrato dvādaśa prajāvaśaḥ | vedā ya upajāyate |*)
((म. सं. १-२५-८) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-25-8)*), as printed with the reference after the text)

here it is said that Varuṇa knows the twelve months, and

वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञ मक्तुं चादृचं । (*vi ye dadhuḥ śaradaṃ māsamādaharyajña maktuṃ cādṛcaṃ |*)
अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥ (*anāpyaṃ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśata ‖*)
(म. सं ७-६६-११) (*(ma. saṃ 7-66-11)*)

in this ṛk it is said that Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman divided autumn, the month, the day and the night.

It is said in many places that it is he too who regulates the waters. It is he who made the rivers flow; by his command they flow ceaselessly ((ऋ. सं. २-२८-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 2-28-4)*)). That the rivers, though they rush into the sea and pour water, do not fill it, is by his hidden power ((ऋ. सं. ५-८५-६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 5-85-6)*)). Varuṇa and Mitra are lords of the rivers. That Varuṇa is lord of the oceans is an established point, but it occurs very rarely in the Ṛgveda; perhaps the reason is that it is of no great importance. In the Purāṇas and the like Varuṇa is famous as lord of the waters, and it is said in the Purāṇas that, as one of the eight guardians of the quarters, he is lord of the west. There is no support for that in the Ṛgveda. In general all that is connected with Varuṇa is connected with the water in the atmosphere; among the deities prayed to for rain, Varuṇa and Mitra are chief. When the mountains are all covered by clouds, Varuṇa, with the overturned *bhāni* (cloud), pours water on heaven, earth and sky and wets the whole earth: so it is said in the ṛks ऋ. सं. ५-८५-३, ४नॆय (*ṛ. saṃ. 5-85-3, 4nèya*). A whole sūkta (ऋ. सं ५-६३नॆय (*ṛ. saṃ 5-63nèya*)) indicates their rain-giving power. In the Yajurveda Saṃhitā ((तै. सं ५-५ ४-१) (*(tai. saṃ 5-5 4-1)*)) आपो वरुणस्य पत्नय आसन् (*āpo varuṇasya patnaya āsan*) — the waters were Varuṇa's wives; and (तै. सं. ६-४-३-२) (*tai. saṃ. 6-4-3-2)*)) मित्रावरुणौ ना अपा नेतार् (*mitrāvaruṇau nā apā netār*) ("Mitra and Varuṇa are the leaders of the waters"; the print has "ವಿತ್ರಾವರುಣರು" [?] in the Kannada) is also said.

### Printed p. 127

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 127 (as supplied). The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 of Sūkta 186 (Varuṇa, then Aryaman) from p. 126.*

It is said again and again that the decrees of Varuṇa are well established; for this very reason he is called धृतव्रत (*dhṛtavrata*) ("he of firm laws"). This epithet is given to both Mitra and Varuṇa.

परि धामानि मर्मृशद्वरुणस्य पुरो गये विश्वे देवा अनु व्रतं नभंता- (*pari dhāmāni marmṛśadvaruṇasya puro gaye viśve devā anu vrataṃ nabhaṃtā-*)
मन्यके समे ॥ (*manyake same ‖*)
((म. सं. ८-४१-७) (*(ma. saṃ. 8-41-7)*), as printed; the book prints "ಮ. ಸಂ.")
न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनंति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि । (*na vāṃ devā amṛtā ā minaṃti vratāni mitrāvaruṇā dhruvāṇi |*)
((म. सं. ५-६९-४) (*(ma. saṃ. 5-69-4)*))

in these and similar ṛks it is said that the gods themselves obey the commands of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, and that even the ancient gods cannot violate their firm laws. Mitra and Varuṇa are the regulators of law (*ṛta*) and light. It is by the strength of these decrees that they are able to support the laws. This quality is found especially in these two, sometimes in the Ādityas, or in other common deities too. The epithet ऋतस्य गोपाः (*ṛtasya gopāḥ*) ("guardians of *ṛta*"), that is, those who keep the laws (or make them be kept), is found applied many times to Mitra and Varuṇa.

The power of Varuṇa is unfathomable. Neither flying birds nor flowing rivers can reach the limit of his kingdom's border; they cannot exceed his power; they cannot withstand his anger. Neither the sky nor the rivers have reached the boundary of the territory of Mitra and Varuṇa. All things lie hidden in Varuṇa. The dwellings of all beings and the three heavens and the three earths are laid in him. Varuṇa is omniscient. The flight of birds in the sky, the course of ships on the sea, the path of the far-travelling wind: all these are known to him. He sees all things past or to come. He is the witness of the true and false deeds of men. All the deeds, thoughts and devices of every man are known to Varuṇa. He can grasp all that is in heaven and earth and beyond them. However far one runs beyond the sky, no one can leave the range of Varuṇa's sight.

Since he is the regulator of morals, Varuṇa becomes very angry at sin; for both the violation of his laws and his anger he inflicts very cruel punishment. The noose of Varuṇa that binds sinners is spoken of in the ṛks १-२४-१५ ; १-२५-११ ; ६-७४-४ १०-८५-२४ (*1-24-15 ; 1-25-11 ; 6-74-4 10-85-24*) and others; that noose binds the speaker of untruth and releases the speaker of truth.

युवो राष्ट्रं बृहदिन्वति द्यौर्यौ सेतृभिररज्जुभिः सिनीथः । (*yuvo rāṣṭraṃ bṛhadinvati dyauryau setṛbhirarajjubhiḥ sinīthaḥ |*)

### Printed p. 128

*Running head: [128 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 185] (the supplied text reads "೧೮೫" here for 186, as printed).*

परि नो हेळो वरुणस्य वृज्या उरुं न इंद्रः कृणवदु लोकं ॥ (*pari no heḷo varuṇasya vṛjyā uruṃ na iṃdraḥ kṛṇavadu lokaṃ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ७-८४-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 7-84-2)*)
(म. सं. ७-८४-२) (*(ma. saṃ. 7-84-2)*)

(the reference is printed twice, first as "ಋ. ಸಂ." and then as "ಮ. ಸಂ.")

in this ṛk it is said that Varuṇa, accompanied by Indra, binds with bonds that are not of rope. The word *pāśa* (noose) occurs in the whole Ṛgveda only in one place, in a mantra addressed to Agni, and that too in the context of praying that the noose that binds his worshippers be loosed; therefore it may be said that these acts of binding with the noose and of releasing it belong to Varuṇa alone.

Varuṇa together with Mitra is the one who drives away, hates and punishes untruth. Mitra and Varuṇa punish those who are careless in their worship, but Varuṇa forgives those who repent. He unties as one unties a rope, and removes sin; he frees a man not only from sin committed by himself but also from sin committed by his ancestors. Those who daily violate the laws laid down by him and afterwards repent he also saves, and he shows compassion to those who have violated his commands through forgetfulness. In Varuṇa there are hundreds and thousands of medicines. He drives away death and removes sin. He can take away life and can give life. He is very skilful among those who protect immortality. Thus the description of the qualities of Varuṇa is in many ṛks. Here we have explained it very briefly; on a fitting occasion we shall explain it at length.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: फल्गुनीनक्षत्रमर्यमा देवता (*phalgunīnakṣatramaryamā devatā*) .... .... .... .... अनूराधा (*anūrādhā*) नक्षत्रं मित्रो देवता (*nakṣatraṃ mitro devatā*) .... .... .... .... ((तै. सं. ४-४-९-२)—ऎंदरॆ (*(tai. saṃ. 4-4-9-2)—èṃdarè*)) — that is, it is said that Aryaman is the lord of the Pūrva Phalgunī nakṣatra and Mitra of the Anurādhā nakṣatra.

आर्यमा—आदित्यर (*āryamā—ādityara*) — in the sūktas addressed to the Ādityas the Ādityas are generally Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. As we said before, in the Ṛgveda ((ऋ. सं. २-२७-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 2-27-1)*)) only the names of six are given: Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa and Aṃśa. In the ṛk ऋ सं. ९-११४-३ नॆय ऋक्किनल्लि (*ṛ saṃ. 9-114-3 nèya ṛkkinalli*) the number of the Ādityas is said to be seven, and in ऋ. सं. १०-७२-८ रल्लि (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-72-8 ralli*) it is said that Aditi first presented seven sons to the gods and afterwards obtained the eighth, Mārtaṇḍa. In अ. वे. ८-९-२१ (*a. ve. 8-9-21*) and in तै. ब्रा. (*tai. brā.*) १-१-९-१ (*1-1-9-1*) it is said that Aditi has eight sons: Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Dhātṛ, Indra and Vivasvān. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa ((श. ब्रा. ६-१-२.८ ; ११-६-३-८) (*(śa. brā. 6-1-2.8 ; 11-6-3-8)*)) it is said that the Ādityas are twelve, one for each month. In the Purāṇas and the like also the Ādityas are twelve.

Though the name of the deity Aryaman occurs about a hundred times in the Ṛgveda, because he has no complete individuality Yāska, in his Nirukta (the Nighaṇṭu), when explaining the forms and derivations of the names of deities, has left out the name of this deity Aryaman. Except in two mantras,

everywhere else he is mentioned together with other deities, and mostly with Mitra and Varuṇa. When addressing Agni in winning over maidens:

त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन् गुह्यं बिभर्षि । (*tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ nāma svadhāvan guhyaṃ bibharṣi |*)
(( ऋ. सं. ५-३-२) (*( ṛ. saṃ. 5-3-2)*))

he is said to be Aryaman: "you yourself."

भगो अर्यमा सविता पुरंधिर्मह्यं त्वादुर्गार्हपत्याय देवाः । (*bhago aryamā savitā puraṃdhirmahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ |*)
((ऋ. सं. १०-८५-३६) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-85-36)*))

in this ṛk the bridegroom says: "O gods, Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ and Purandhi gave this bride to me to assist my householder's life."

न तमंहो न दुरितं देवासो अष्ट मर्त्यं । (*na tamaṃho na duritaṃ devāso aṣṭa martyaṃ |*)
सजोषसो यमर्यमा मित्रो नयंति वरुणो अति द्विषः ॥ (*sajoṣaso yamaryamā mitro nayaṃti varuṇo ati dviṣaḥ ‖*)
((म. सं. १०-१२६-१) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-126-1)*), as printed; the book prints "ಮ. ಸಂ.")
शुनमस्मभ्यमूतये वरुणो मित्रो आर्यमा । (*śunamasmabhyamūtaye varuṇo mitro āryamā |*)
शर्म यच्छंतु सप्रथ आदित्यासो यदीमहे अति द्विषः ॥ (*śarma yacchaṃtu sapratha ādityāso yadīmahe ati dviṣaḥ ‖*)
((म. सं. १०-१२६-७) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-126-7)*))

Although in the sūkta ऋ. सं. १०-१२६ (*ṛ. saṃ. 10-126*) the gods are called Viśve Devāḥ, from the ṛks quoted above it is chiefly the Ādityas who are praised here. Besides, the words देवासः अष्ट (*devāsaḥ aṣṭa*) ("eight gods") in the first ṛk refer to the eight Ādityas (the number of the Ādityas is nowhere said in the Veda to be more than eight); and the word आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*) in the seventh ṛk also makes this plain. That in every ṛk of this sūkta (except the last) the names वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा (*varuṇo mitro aryamā*) ("Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman") are recited again and again like a refrain shows that among the Ādityas these Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman hold the chief place. Since not much about Aryaman is explained in the Ṛgveda, no special explanation is possible.

### Printed p. 131

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 131 (as supplied, "ವ ೪").*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे देवाः वो युष्माकं प्रेष्ठं प्रियतमं । सर्वेषामाह्वातृत्वाद्धविर्व-
> हनाच्चाग्निर्देवानां प्रियतमः । तमतिथिं गृणीषे । गृणे । सौमि ॥ व्यत्ययेन
> मध्यमः ॥ केन साधनेन । शस्तिभिः शंसनैः स्तुतिभिः । कीदृशोऽहं । तुर्वणिस्तूर्ण-
> वनिः शीघ्रं संभक्ता सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणः । यद्वा । एते अग्नि विशे-
> षणे । यस्तुर्वणिः शीघ्रं यज्ञस्य संभक्ता सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रियमाणः
> तमग्निं गृणिषे । यथा येन प्रकारेण नोऽस्माकं वरुण एतन्नामको देवः
> सुकीर्तिः शोभनकीर्तिमानसत् । सुकीर्तिं भिक्षे वरुणस्य भूरेः । ऋ. २-२८-१ ।
> इत्यादिमंत्रवर्णेषु वरणात्सुकीर्तिरेवैषणीया । अरिगूर्तोऽरिष्टदातृषु सदा
> शब्दितः अरीणां हनना- योद्युक्तो वा सूरिः प्रेरयितायं वरुण इषश्चान्नानि
> पर्षत् । पूरयेत् । तथा तमपि स्तुम इत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* O gods, I praise Agni, your dearest guest, with praises, swift and in accord with you; so may Varuṇa be of fair renown to us, fill us with food, and so we praise him too.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

देवाः (*devāḥ*) — O gods. तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) — eager to perform the sacrifice and please the gods. सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — beloved equally by all the gods: I. [Or (यः (*yaḥ*) — whichever Agni), तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) — eager to carry the oblation to the gods, सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — equally beloved among the gods] who is such, and: वः (*vaḥ*) — to you. श्रेष्ठं— (*śreṣṭhaṃ—*) — the most beloved. अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*) — guest-like. अग्निं (*agniṃ*) — Agni. शस्तिभिः (*śastibhiḥ*) — with praises. गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*) — I praise. यथा (*yathā*) — in what manner. अरिगूर्तः (*arigūrtaḥ*) — the destroyer of the enemies who give nothing. सूरिः (*sūriḥ*) — and the inspirer of men to action. वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) — Varuṇa. सुकीर्तिः (*sukīrtiḥ*) — of excellent fame. असत् (*asat*) — may he become, (and). इषश्च (*iṣaśca*) — food. पर्षत् (*parṣat*) — may he fill (in that way I praise Varuṇa also).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O gods, I, eager to perform the sacrifice and please the gods and equally beloved of all the gods, praise with hymns Agni, who is dearest to the gods and guest-like; and I praise Varuṇa too, the destroyer of those who give nothing and the inspirer of men to action, so that he may become for us a maker of excellent fame and fill us with food.

**Printed English translation**

I praise with hymns, (O gods), your best beloved guest, Agai [sic], who is prompt (to partake of the oblation), and who is well pleased along (with you); so that (thereby) Varuna, the possessor of renown, the subduer of foes, the animator (of men), may fill us with food.

### Printed p. 132

*Running head: [132 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186].*

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

The Viśve Devāḥ are said to be the deity of this sūkta. Therefore, having praised chiefly the deity Savitṛ in the first ṛk of this sūkta and the deities Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman (the Ādityas) in the second ṛk, the ṛṣi praises Agni and Varuṇa in the present third ṛk, that beginning प्रेष्ठं वो अतिथिं (*preṣṭhaṃ vo atithiṃ*).

प्रेष्ठं (*preṣṭhaṃ*) — प्रियतमं । सर्वेषामाह्वातृत्वादविर्वहनाच्चाग्निर्देवानां (*priyatamaṃ | sarveṣāmāhvātṛtvādavirvahanāccāgnirdevānāṃ*) प्रियतमः (*priyatamaḥ*) ("dearest; because he calls all and carries the oblations, Agni is dearest of the gods"): the meaning is "Agni, who is extremely beloved". How Agni is beloved of the gods: in the sacrifices and the like that men perform, Agni takes the office of Hotṛ, invites the gods intended by the sacrificers and brings them to the sacrificial ground, and he carries the oblations that the sacrificers offer in Agni to the gods and makes them reach them; therefore it is natural to say that Agni is beloved of the gods. In the sacrifices too Agni has a close bond with the daily life of men. Agni delivers to the gods what is offered by men in the fire; for this very reason he has the name *havyavāṭ* (हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*), "carrier of oblation"). Without him the gods feel no delight. This is said in the ṛk

महा अस्यध्वरस्य प्रकेशो न ऋते त्वदमृता मादयंते । (*mahā asyadhvarasya prakeśo na ṛte tvadamṛtā mādayaṃte |*)
((ऋ सं ७-११-१) (*(ṛ saṃ 7-11-1)*), as printed with "ಋ ಸಂ")

And in the matter of Agni bringing the gods and carrying the oblation to them:

अग्निं दूतं वृणीमहे होतारं विश्ववेदसं । (*agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe hotāraṃ viśvavedasaṃ |*)
((म. सं. १-१२-१) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-12-1)*))

in this ṛk Agni is prayed to as the messenger who brings the gods to the sacrificial ground and summons them.

अग्ने देवा इहावह जज्ञानो व्यक्तबर्हिषे । असि होता न ईड्यः । (*agne devā ihāvaha jajñāno vyaktabarhiṣe | asi hotā na īḍyaḥ |*)
((ऋ. सं. १-१२-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-12-2)*))

in this ṛk Agni is prayed: "O Agni, since you are the Hotṛ who brings the gods, bring the gods to this sacrificial ground." In १-१४-१ (*1-14-1*) it is prayed देवेभिर्याहि (*devebhiryāhi*) ("come with the gods") to our sacrifice. Agni goes by both paths, to the earth and to the vicinity of the gods; because of that it is the custom to call him the messenger (*dūta*).

### Printed p. 133

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 133 (as supplied). The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 of Sūkta 186 from p. 132.*

Because it is said that in sacrifices Agni plays the most important part in accomplishing the rites, the position that men give to the priest is given to Agni among the gods. Hence he has epithets such as priest (*ṛtvij*), sage (*vipra*), family-priest (*purohita*) and *hotā*. Of all these, to call Agni *hotā* (one who invites the gods, or who accomplishes the oblation) is the most distinctive. He is the dearest and best of all the Hotṛs. The work of carrying the oblations is Agni's chief work. Therefore the ṛṣi describes Agni as most beloved of the gods.

अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*) — Since it is said that man obtains Agni by the grace of the gods and that Mātariśvan first saw Agni and brought him to earth, it is established, as it were, that Agni belongs to the world of heaven. It is in this sense that Agni may be called the guest of men. Or, since a guest is always honourable and worthy of respect, Agni too, being worthy of worship, may have been praised by the epithet "guest".

तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) — Yāska has stated the derivation of this word: तुर्वणिस्तूर्णवनिः (*turvaṇistūrṇavaniḥ*) ((नि. ६-१४) (*(ni. 6-14)*)). For this word, formed from the root वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*), the meaning is तूर्णं हि यः संभजते स तूर्णवनिरित्युक्तः (*tūrṇaṃ hi yaḥ saṃbhajate sa tūrṇavanirityuktaḥ*): "one who comes promptly". In the present ṛk तुर्वणिः सजोषाः (*turvaṇiḥ sajoṣāḥ*) means that Agni is praised as one who, loved by the other gods or accompanied by them, comes quickly to this our sacrificial ground.

सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — the bhāṣyakāra has given two kinds of meaning for this word. First, सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणः (*sajoṣā yuṣmābhiḥ saha prīyamāṇaḥ*): "O gods, I praise the beloved Agni so that he may come with you." Then he explains in another way, यस्तुवर्णिः शीघ्रं यज्ञस्य संभक्ता सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणस्तमग्निं गृणीषे (*yastuvarṇiḥ śīghraṃ yajñasya saṃbhaktā sajoṣā yuṣmābhiḥ saha prīyamāṇastamagniṃ gṛṇīṣe*): "O gods, I praise that Agni whom you love and who comes quickly to the sacrificial ground." (The supplied text has "ಯಸ್ತುವರ್ಣಿಃ" for the bhāṣya's *yas turvaṇiḥ*; marked [?].)

वरुणः सुकीर्ति: (*varuṇaḥ sukīrti:*) — "in the way in which Varuṇa, being of good fame, has been prayed to make fame for us, in that way": this is Sāyaṇa's explanation. On this matter he has quoted the ṛk

अति यो मंद्रो यजथाय देवः सुकीर्तिं भिक्षे वरुणस्य भूरेः । (*ati yo maṃdro yajathāya devaḥ sukīrtiṃ bhikṣe varuṇasya bhūreḥ |*)
(म. सं २-२८-१) (*(ma. saṃ 2-28-1)*)

It is plain that in this ṛk fame is greatly desired from Varuṇa and praise is offered.

### Printed p. 134

*Running head: [134 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186].*

अरिगूर्तः (*arigūrtaḥ*) — this word occurs in the Ṛgveda only in this ṛk, nowhere else. Sāyaṇa explains it as अरिगूर्तोऽरिष्पदातृषु सदा शब्दितः (*arigūrto 'riṣpadātṛṣu sadā śabditaḥ*) ["ಅರಿಷ್ಪದಾತೃಷು" as supplied, marked [?]] अरीणां हननायोद्यु- (*arīṇāṃ hananāyodyu-*) क्तो वा (*kto vā*): "one who always makes a sound, that is, reproaches, towards the misers who give nothing to anyone"; or, another meaning is possible: "one ready to destroy enemies".

सूरिः (*sūriḥ*) — the word *sūri* is read among the names of the praiser ((नि. ३-१९) (*(ni. 3-19)*)), meaning "one who praises". And Yāska, having quoted the ṛk

इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा ३ नामभिः स्वैः । (*iheha jātā samavāvaśītāmarepasā tanvā 3 nāmabhiḥ svaiḥ |*)
जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ii (*jiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumakhasya sūrirdivo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe ii*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१८१-४) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-181-4)*)

has explained the word *sūri* in it as *īrayitā*, "inciter" ((नि. १२-३) (*(ni. 12-3)*)). The bhāṣyakāra too has taken this meaning in the present ṛk and explained सूरिः ऎंदरॆ प्रेरयिता अयं वरुणः (*sūriḥ èṃdarè prerayitā ayaṃ varuṇaḥ*) as "the inciter Varuṇa".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

प्रेष्ठम् (*preṣṭham*) ("most dear"): by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*) the suffix *iṣṭhan*; by प्रियस्थिर स्थिर—(पा. सू. ६-४-१५७) (*priyasthira sthira—(pā. sū. 6-4-157)*) the substitute *pra* for *priya*; by प्रकृत्यैकाच् (पा. सू. ६-३-१६३) (*prakṛtyaikāc (pā. sū. 6-3-163)*) the natural form remains, so the loss of *ṭi* does not occur; guṇa; because the suffix is marked *n* the first syllable is acute (printed "ಆದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತಸ್ವತರ"). अतिथिम् (*atithim*) (root अत सातत्यगमने (*ata sātatyagamane*)): by ऋतन्यंजि—(उ. सू. ४-४४२) (*ṛtanyaṃji—(u. sū. 4-442)*) the suffix *ithin*; by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) the first syllable is acute. गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*) (root ग्य शब्दे (*gya śabde*), *kryādi*): by व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*) the second-person singular ending in place of the first-person singular of the present; by क्रादिभ्यः श्ना (*krādibhyaḥ śnā*) the *śnā* suffix; by स्वादीनां ह्रस्वः (पा. सू. ७-३-८०) (*svādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ (pā. sū. 7-3-80)*) shortening of the root; by ई हल्यघोः (पा. सू. (*ī halyaghoḥ (pā. sū.*) ६-४-११३) (*6-4-113)*) *ī* for the *ā* of the suffix; the change to *ṇ* after *ṛ*; the verb-*nighāta* accent. तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) (root तुर्वी हिंसायां (*turvī hiṃsāyāṃ*)): the Uṇādi suffix *ani*; the last syllable of the suffix is acute. असत् (*asat*) (root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*)): *leṭ*; the third person singular *tip*; by इतश्चलोपः (*itaścalopaḥ*) loss of the final *i*; by लेटोऽडाट् (पा. सू. ३-४-६३) (*leṭo 'ḍāṭ (pā. sū. 3-4-63)*) the augment *aḍāṭ* [the sentence ends at the page break; it continues on p. 135 with "ಗಮ"]

### Printed p. 135

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4 ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 135 (as supplied).*

...the augment *aḍāṭ*. Because it stands at the beginning of the pāda there is no *nighāta* accent; because the augment is unaccented, the accent of the root remains. सुकीर्तिः (*sukīrtiḥ*) ("he whose fame is good"): by नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) (*nañsubhyām (pā. sū. 6-2-172)*) the last syllable of the later member is acute. पर्षत् (*parṣat*) (root पृ पालनपूरणयोः (*pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*)): *leṭ*; third person singular *śip* [as printed]; loss of *i*; augment *aḍ*; by सिब्बहुलं लेटि (पा. सू. ३-१-३४) (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi (pā. sū. 3-1-34)*) *sip*; on that account guṇa of the *ṛ* of the root with *r*; because of the *r* the *s* of *sip* becomes *ṣ*; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

> पयसि त्वदर्थं हविर्विमिमान उपगच्छामीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । सस्मिन् सर्वस्मिन्नूधसि
> फलाख्यक्षीरोत्पादके यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति विषुरूपे पयसि नानारूपे सोम-
> लक्षणोदकेऽर्कमन्नसाधनं स्तोत्रं विमिमानोऽहं युष्मानभिगच्छामि ॥

*Gist:* Mixing oblation for you in the multiform milk from one udder, or praising with the food-giving hymn, I approach you.

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads १ प्रतिपदार्थ १ (*1 pratipadārtha 1*) (inside the bhāṣya block); standard label inserted.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(O gods) समाने अहन् (*samāne ahan*) — on the same (sixth) day, or at all times. सस्मिन् (*sasmin*) — of the same (one). ऊधन् (*ūdhan*) — produced from the udder. विषुरूपे (*viṣurūpe*) — taking various forms. पयसि (*payasi*) — in the milk. अर्कं (*arkaṃ*) — the worshipful food such as the *caru*. विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*) — I who mix. जिगीषा (*jigīṣā*) — with the desire to conquer sin. सुदुघा (*sudughā*) — the good milker. धेनुः इव (*dhenuḥ iva*) — like a cow that comes of itself to be milked. उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) — Day and Night. नमसा (*namasā*) — with oblation and with homage. वः (*vaḥ*) — you. उप (*upa*) — approaching. एषे (*eṣe*) — (I desire your presence.)

*[As supplied, the label line of the next section reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*) (inside the bhāṣya block); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O gods, I who, on the sixth day of the sacrifice, mix the worshipful *caru*, *puroḍāśa* and other food in milk that comes from one udder and takes many forms, approach you with oblation and with homage, day and night, wishing your presence, with the desire to conquer sin, as a good milch-cow comes of itself to be milked.

**Printed English translation**

I approach you, (deities), with reverence, night and day, in the hope of overcoming (sin), as (willingly) as a gentle cow (comes to be milked)' mixing (for you) on the appropriate day the (sacrificial) food, (consisting) of multiform (preparations) of milk (generated) from the same udder. [The printed text has a stray closing quote mark after "milked)" as supplied.]

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Although the gods are prayed to in this ṛk, other gods are also praised in general, that is, collectively, besides the deity named उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) (the supplied text has "ಸವಷ್ಟಿರೂಪ" for "ಸಮಷ್ಟಿರೂಪ").

नमसा—हविषा नमस्कारेण वा (*namasā—haviṣā namaskāreṇa vā*) — with oblation or with homage: the sense is "I approach you, the gods, with oblation or with homage".

उषासानक्ता—अहनि रात्रौ च । यद्वा । अहोरात्रदेवते अप्यभिगच्छामि (*uṣāsānaktā—ahani rātrau ca | yadvā | ahorātradevate apyabhigacchāmi*) — the bhāṣyakāra has explained it in one way as "by day and by night", and in another way as "the deities called Uṣāsānaktā, presiding over day and night".

### Printed p. 137

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 137 (as supplied, "ಅ. ೨ ಅ ೫. ವ. ೪.").*

In this ṛk the deities presiding over night and morning, *naktoṣāsā*, are invoked. Yāska's explanation of the word *naktoṣasā* is this:

उषासानक्ता । उषासानक्कोषाश्च नक्ता चोषा व्याख्याता । नक्तेति (*uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsānakkoṣāśca naktā coṣā vyākhyātā | nakteti*)
रात्रिनामानक्ति भूतान्यवश्यायेनापि वा नक्ताव्यक्तवर्णा ॥ (*rātrināmānakti bhūtānyavaśyāyenāpi vā naktāvyaktavarṇā ‖*)
(नि. ८-११) (*(ni. 8-11)*)

Though read in two ways, *naktoṣāsā* and *uṣāsānaktā*, the sense is one. The explanation of the word *uṣāḥ* I have given earlier. *Naktā* is a name of night: because *naktā* means "of unclear colour"; since it is dark, things are unclear, that is, not seen well; so the night with darkness is called *naktā*. And in the night-time creatures are unable to do their several tasks. अनक्ति, क्लेदयति भूतानि अवश्यायेन इति (*anakti, kledayati bhūtāni avaśyāyena iti*) ("it wets creatures with dew"); अपि वानक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा । यथा अहः सर्वमभिव्यक्तरूपं भवति न तथा रात्रिः (*api vānaktā avyaktavarṇā | yathā ahaḥ sarvamabhivyaktarūpaṃ bhavati na tathā rātriḥ*) ("or *anaktā*, of unclear colour: as the day makes everything clearly visible, the night does not"). Since darkness troubles creatures so that their work and so on cannot go on properly, the night with such darkness is called *naktā*; or because nothing is seen well but all is unclear it is called *naktā*. By day the forms of all things are clearly seen; at night they are not so seen; therefore the night time is called *naktā*: thus the meaning is explained.

The explanation of the word *uṣāḥ* has been given before, it is said. That explanation is this: sixteen words, विभावरी (*vibhāvarī*), सूदरी (*sūdarī*) and so on, are names of Uṣas ((नि. २-१९) (*(ni. 2-19)*)), and

उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (*uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ*)

she is called *uṣāḥ* because she removes the darkness of the night time, that is, she is the later time, the last part of the night. In support of this meaning an example is given:

इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा । (*idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā |*)
यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवाय एवा रात्रुषसे योनिमारैक् ॥ (*yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya evā rātruṣase yonimāraik ‖*)
(पु. सं. १-११३-१) (*(pu. saṃ. 1-113-1)*)

The Nirukta on this ṛk is:

इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागमत् । चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञातत- ममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुःप्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्य (*idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātata- mamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥprasavāya rātrirādityasya*)

### Printed p. 138

*Running head: [138 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 186].*

एवं रात्रुषसे योनिमरिचत् स्थानं । स्त्रीयोनिरभियुत एनां (*evaṃ rātruṣase yonimaricat sthānaṃ | strīyonirabhiyuta enāṃ*) गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)

The best and most brilliant light of the Sun is rising. The time of dawn, which precedes the brightness of the Sun, appears before the light like its standard. How? As the light of the Sun, having shone all day, becomes at sunset the womb, that is, the cause, of the night, so the night at its end becomes the womb, that is, the cause, of the dawn-time; "womb" means the place of birth. The main sense is that at the end of day the night and at the end of night the dawn come, each changing into the other. Therefore *uṣas* means the light that, after the night has passed, before sunrise, spreads over all the quarters and appears.

The bhāṣyakāra (Sāyaṇa)'s explanation is: नक्तशब्द: उषश्यब्दश्च लोके कालविशेषवा- (*naktaśabda: uṣaśyabdaśca loke kālaviśeṣavā-*) चिनौ । इह तु तत्कालाभिमानिवह्निमूर्तिद्वये प्रयुज्येते । नक्तोषासा नक्तोषो- (*cinau | iha tu tatkālābhimānivahnimūrtidvaye prayujyete | naktoṣāsā naktoṣo-*) नामिके वह्निमूर्ति (*nāmike vahnimūrti*): the two words *nakta* (night) and *uṣas* (morning) in common usage denote the special times of night and morning; here, that is, in this ṛk or in the Ṛgveda, these words denote the presiding deities of night and morning. Therefore the words *naktoṣāsā* or *uṣāsānaktā* are used in the sense of the two forms (*mūrti*) of Agni, presiding over night and the dawn-time. The word सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) (of good form) used in this ṛk supports this sense: since night and morning are divisions of time they have neither form nor shape; if they are said to be the presiding deities of those times, form can be assigned to those deities; since such assignment is made in this ṛk, it is to be understood that the presiding deities of those times are meant here. The *ṣ* in the word *naktoṣasā* is lengthened for the sake of the metre.

सुदुघेव धेनुः (*sudugheva dhenuḥ*) — when the ṛṣi says that he wishes to come near the gods, he gives a comparison: as a good milch-cow, when evening comes, leaves the grazing outside and comes to her master's house: so the sense of the comparison is explained.

ईषे (*īṣe*) — the word ईषे (*īṣe*) may be formed from the root *iṣ* meaning "to go", or from the root *īṣ* with the same sense, according to the bhāṣyakāra's explanation. *Īṣe* means "I wish", "I desire", or "I desire to come near (you)".

### Printed p. 139

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 139 (as supplied). The window continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 4 of Sūkta 186 from p. 138, after the note on *īṣe*.*

समाने पयसि ऊधन् विषुरूपे (*samāne payasi ūdhan viṣurūpe*) — two kinds of meaning are possible for these words. One meaning: from milk drawn on a single day, many kinds of milk, curds, ghee, oblation and so on; another meaning: in a sacrifice whose fruit is milk, accompanied by many kinds of milk-products, that is, accompanied by soma-juices (such as *gavāśir* and *dadhyāśir*): thus the bhāṣyakāra has explained. The main idea is this: although the same kind of milk arises at the same time from the udders of all cows, it takes different forms such as milk, curds and ghee. The ṛṣi describes that he will come near the gods reciting a praise that is the means of the food (*caru*, *puroḍāśa* and the like) accompanied by these milk-products, or of the soma-juice.

विषुरूपे— नानारूपे (*viṣurūpe— nānārūpe*) — having many forms: although the milk is one, the things made from it, milk, curds and ghee, are of many kinds.

अर्कं— अन्नसाधनं स्तोत्रं (*arkaṃ— annasādhanaṃ stotraṃ*) — the bhāṣyakāra has here given the sense "food" for the word *arka*. Yāska in his Nirukta says:

अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चंति । (*arko devo bhavati yadenamarcaṃti |*)
अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चंति । (*arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcaṃti |*)
अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि । (*arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtāni |*)
अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्मा । (*arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimmā |*)
(सि. ५-४) (*(si. 5-4)*) (printed "ಸಿ." for "ನಿ.")

and thus has given four derivations of the word *arka*. (1) देवः । तावत्सर्व एवार्क इत्युच्यते यत्-यॆस्मात् एनं देवं अर्चंति स्तोतारः (*devaḥ | tāvatsarva evārka ityucyate yat-yèsmāt enaṃ devaṃ arcaṃti stotāraḥ*) ["ಯೆಸ್ಮಾತ್" as supplied]: *arka* means a god, because the worshippers worship this one with it; that is, the thing worshipped by the devotee (the deity) is called *arka*. (2) अर्को मंत्रो भवति । यत् यस्मात् अनेन मंत्रेण अर्चंति स्तोतारः तस्मादर्कः (*arko maṃtro bhavati | yat yasmāt anena maṃtreṇa arcaṃti stotāraḥ tasmādarkaḥ*): *arka* also means a mantra, because those who praise worship the deity with it (the *arka*, the ṛk, the mantra); so the word *arka* is also a name for a mantra. (3) अर्कमन्नं भवति । तद्धि अर्चति भूतानि, यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते, पूज्यं च सर्वस्यॆवान्नं (*arkamannaṃ bhavati | taddhi arcati bhūtāni, yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnamapi saṃskāraviśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate, pūjyaṃ ca sarvasyèvānnaṃ*): *arka* also means food. Food is necessary for all creatures, and

### Printed p. 140

*Running head: [140 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 186].*

everyone respects and desires it with regard; that is, because all respect and wish for it with love and regard, the word *arka* also means food. (4) अर्को वृक्षो भवति य एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृत्तः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्ना कटुकभावेन भवति (*arko vṛkṣo bhavati ya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛttaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimnā kaṭukabhāvena bhavati*): further, the name of a kind of tree, well known, also belongs to the word *arka*. The *arka* tree is called *ekkada giḍa* in the Karnāṭaka language; since its fuel sticks are used in sacrifices and it is used in medicine, the *arka* tree is a thing known to all; because it is bitter it is called कटुकिम्मा (*kaṭukimmā*) ["ಕಟುಕಿಮ್ಮಾ" as supplied in the first quotation, "ಕಟುಕಿಮ್ನಾ" in the second; marked [?]].

As an example for the explanation of the word *arka* Yāska has quoted the ṛk beginning गायंति त्वा (*gāyaṃti tvā*) and given its explanation; since it is unnecessary here it is not set out. (See Ṛg. Saṃ. part 2, page 385, as printed.)

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly)

ईषे (*īṣe*) (root इष गतौ (*iṣa gatau*), "to go"): by छंदसिलुज् लज् लिटः (*chaṃdasiluj laj liṭaḥ*) the *liṭ* in the sense of the present; first person singular; because it follows a non-verb the *nighāta* accent arises. जिगीषा (*jigīṣā*) (जेतुमिच्छा जिगीषा (*jetumicchā jigīṣā*), "the wish to conquer"; root जि जये (*ji jaye*)): by धातोः कर्मणः समान- (*dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samāna-*) (पा. सू. ३-१ ७) (*(pā. sū. 3-1 7)*) (as printed, the numeral incomplete) the suffix *san* in the sense of wish; doubling by सन्यजोः (*sanyajoḥ*); by अज्जनगमां सनि (पा. सू. ६-४-१६) (*ajjanagamāṃ sani (pā. sū. 6-4-16)*) lengthening of the *i* of the root when *san* follows; by सन्‌लिटो (*sanliṭo*) र्जेः (पा. सू ७-३-५७) (*rjeḥ (pā. sū 7-3-57)*) the guttural change of *j*; by अप्रत्ययात् (पा. सू. ३-३-१०२) (*apratyayāt (pā. sū. 3-3-102)*) the suffix *a* after a *san*-ending root; the feminine *ṭāp*; by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) *luk* of the instrumental singular; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) ("Uṣas and night"): by उषासोषसः (पा सा. ६-३-३१) (*uṣāsoṣasaḥ (pā sā. 6-3-31)*) (as printed "ಸಾ." for "ಸೂ.") the substitute *uṣāsā* for the earlier member in a dvandva; by देवताद्वंद्वे च (पा. सू. ६-२-१४१) (*devatādvaṃdve ca (pā. sū. 6-2-141)*) both members keep their own accent; by the sūtra सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) the substitute *ā* for the dual ending. अहन् (*ahan*): by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) *luk* when the locative singular follows; by न जि संबुद्ध्योः (*na ji saṃbuddhyoḥ*) the loss of *n* does not occur. विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*) (root माज् माने (*māj māne*)): the substitute *śānac* for the present; because of the *śluk* suffix doubling of the root; by भृञामित् (पा. सू. ७-४-७६) (*bhṛñāmit (pā. sū. 7-4-76)*) *i* for the reduplicative syllable; by अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*)

### Printed p. 141

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 4.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 141 (as supplied).*

(पा. सू. ६-१-१८९) (*(pā. sū. 6-1-189)*) the first syllable is acute. In a compound with a prefix the accent of the later member, a *kṛt* word. विषुरूपे (*viṣurūpe*) ("that which has many forms"): by बहुव्रीहौ प्र— (*bahuvrīhau pra—*) the accent of the earlier member.

#### Ṛk 5
