*[As supplied, a line reading शायणभाष्यं (*śāyaṇabhāṣyaṃ*) stands inside the bhāṣya block as the label; standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> त्वष्टा यज्ञसाधनपात्राभिमानी देवो रूपाणि योन् सृष्टानि रेतांसि
> रूपाणि कर्तुं प्रभुर्हि । हिशब्दः श्रुत्यंतरप्रसिद्दिद्योतनार्थः । यावच्छो वै रेतसः
> सिक्तस्य त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति । तै. सं. १-५-९-१ । इति श्रुतेः । स देवो विश्वान्
> सर्वानपि पशूनस्मदीयान् गवादिकान् समानजे । सम्यगनक्ति । व्यक्तीकरोति ॥ संपू-
> र्वादनक्केर्लिट तस्मान्नुडिति नुट् ॥ अथ प्रत्यक्षः । तेषामक्तानां पशूनां स्फातिं
> वृद्धिं नोऽस्मदर्थमा यज । सर्वतः पूजय । कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Tvaṣṭṛ, the deity of the vessels of sacrifice, is able to give forms to the shed seed (so the Taittirīya-saṃhitā), and he makes all our animals, cows and the rest, distinct; may he increase them for us.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

त्वष्टा-त्वष्टृवु (*tvaṣṭā-tvaṣṭṛvu*) (Tvaṣṭṛ). रूपाणि-सृष्टवाद रेतस्सुगळिगॆ रूपगळन्नु कॊट्टु परिष्करिसलु (*rūpāṇi-sṛṣṭavāda retassugaḷigè rūpagaḷannu kòṭṭu pariṣkarisalu*) (to give forms to the created seeds and refine them). प्रभुः हि-समर्थनागिद्दानॆ (*prabhuḥ hi-samarthanāgiddānè*) (is able). विश्वान् पशून्-नमगॆ संबंधिसिद समस्त पश्वादि गळन्नू (*viśvān paśūn-namagè saṃbaṃdhisida samasta paśvādi gaḷannū*) (all our animals and the like). समानजे-नैयक्षिकवाद स्वरूपवन्नु कॊट्टु परिष्करिसिदनु (*samānaje-naiyakṣikavāda svarūpavannu kòṭṭu pariṣkarisidanu*) (gave each its own form and refined it; the print has "ನೈಯಕ್ಷಿಕ" as supplied). तेषां-आ पश्वादिगळ (*teṣāṃ-ā paśvādigaḷa*) (of those animals and the rest). स्नातिं-वृद्धियन्नु (*snātiṃ-vṛddhiyannu*) (the increase). नः-नमगोस्कर (*naḥ-namagoskara*) (for us). आ यज-माडु (*ā yaja-māḍu*) (do).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*), run on after the Pratipadārtha; standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Tvaṣṭṛ is able to give forms to the created seeds and refine them. He gave each of all our animals and the rest its own form and refined it. O Tvaṣṭṛ, create those animals for us and increase their number.

**Printed English translation**

Twashtri, who is the master (in fashioning) the forms (of beings), has made all animals distinct; grant us, (Twashtri), their increase.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 9)**

कृष्णा-यास्कर विवरणॆयु (*kṛṣṇā-yāskara vivaraṇèyu*) (the head-word is printed *kṛṣṇā*, for *tvaṣṭā*) — Yāska's explanation:

त्वष्टा । त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्वषेर्वा स्याद्वीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्ष- (*tvaṣṭā | tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tvaṣervā syādvīptikarmaṇastvakṣa-*)
तेर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः ॥ माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने (*tervā syātkarotikarmaṇaḥ ‖ mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne*)
समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (नि. ८_१४) (*samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖ (ni. 8_14)*)

That is, for the word तृष्णा (*tṛṣṇā*) (the print; *tvaṣṭā* is meant) the Nirukta-authors say "one who pervades quickly", or "one who is shining", or "one who performs works (works of craft)"; some say "Mādhyamika", that is, one who is between heaven and earth; Śākapūṇi says Agni.

### Printed p. 262

*Running head: [262 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū 188] (as supplied).*

Some say that Tvaṣṭṛ is the craftsman of the gods, like Viśvakarman; for in the ṛk given by Yāska by way of example,

य इमे द्यावापृथवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । (*ya ime dyāvāpṛthavī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā |*)
तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥ (*tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān ‖*)
(म. सं. १०-११०-९) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-110-9)*)

it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of heaven and earth and the cause of form, beauty, prosperity, growth and so on suited to the beings in all the worlds. Besides, Yajurveda sentences such as त्वष्टा वै पशूनां मिथुनानां रूपकृत् (*tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt*) (तै. सं. ६-१-८-५ (*tai. saṃ. 6-1-8-5*)), त्वष्टा रूपाणा- मधिपतिः (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇā- madhipatiḥ*) (तै. सं. ३-३ (*tai. saṃ. 3-3*)), त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti*) declare Tvaṣṭṛ's skill in making things. And

मध्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोवृजन्नपि क्रतुं ॥ (*madhyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajramatakṣadāyasaṃ mayi devāsovṛjannapi kratuṃ ‖*)
(म. सं. १०-४८-३) (*(ma. saṃ. 10-48-3)*)

Indra says that Tvaṣṭṛ made for him the thunderbolt of iron. It is said in many mantras of the Ṛgveda that he made for the gods the implements needed for sacrifice and many other things.

It is well known that Tvaṣṭṛ is one of the twelve Ādityas; therefore Yāska explained the word as "shining".

Among the scriptural sentences giving individual opinions on the deity Tvaṣṭṛ, those cited below indicate only the deity connected with the Āprī sūkta:

होतायक्षत्त्वष्टारमचिष्टुमपाकग्ं रेतोधां विश्रवसं यशोधां । (*hotāyakṣattvaṣṭāramaciṣṭumapākagṃ retodhāṃ viśravasaṃ yaśodhāṃ |*)
पुरुरूपमकामकर्शनग्ं सुपोषः पोपैः स्यात्सुवीरो वीरैर्वेत्वाज्यस्य (*pururūpamakāmakarśanagṃ supoṣaḥ popaiḥ syātsuvīro vīrairvetvājyasya*)
होतरज । (*hotaraja |*)
(तै. ब्रा. ३-६-२-२) (*(tai. brā. 3-6-2-2)*)

In this mantra there are the epithets अचिष्टुं (*aciṣṭuṃ*), अपाकं (*apākaṃ*), रेतोधां (*retodhāṃ*), विश्रवसं (*viśravasaṃ*), यशोधां (*yaśodhāṃ*), पुरुरूपं (*pururūpaṃ*), अकाम कर्शनं (*akāma karśanaṃ*). Of these:

अचिष्टुं (*aciṣṭuṃ*) — चेष्टनरहितं, चांचल्यरहितं, स्थिरं (*ceṣṭanarahitaṃ, cāṃcalyarahitaṃ, sthiraṃ*): without restlessness, steady; one who is steady and not restless;

अपाकं (*apākaṃ*) — अबालं, प्राज्ञं (*abālaṃ, prājñaṃ*): not a child, wise (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 263

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 9] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 263 (as supplied).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 9 of Sūkta 188, on the epithets of Tvaṣṭṛ in the Praiṣa mantra.)*

रेतोधां (*retodhāṃ*) — पुत्रादिबीजस्य यजमाने धारयितारं (*putrādibījasya yajamāne dhārayitāraṃ*): one who sows the seed of sons and the like in the sacrificer;

विश्रवसं (*viśravasaṃ*) — विविधकीर्तियुक्तं (*vividhakīrtiyuktaṃ*): endowed with many kinds of fame;

यशोधां (*yaśodhāṃ*) — यजमाने यशसः धारयितारं (*yajamāne yaśasaḥ dhārayitāraṃ*): one who makes the sacrificer a sharer in glory;

पुरुरूपं (*pururūpaṃ*) — बहुरूपं (*bahurūpaṃ*): of many forms;

अकामकर्शनं (*akāmakarśanaṃ*) — कामानां अनाशयितारं (*kāmānāṃ anāśayitāraṃ*): one who makes the sacrificer's wishes fruitful: so it is explained.

These epithets show the individual nature of Tvaṣṭṛ. In showing the derivation of the word *tvaṣṭṛ* (८-१४ (*8-14*)) the Nirukta-authors say त्वष्या तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्वीप्तिकमणस्त्वक्षतीर्वा स्यात् करोटिकर्मणः (*tvaṣyā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syādvīptikamaṇastvakṣatīrvā syāt karoṭikarmaṇaḥ*) (the print has these forms): this name is, in the view of the Nirukta-authors, because he pervades quickly; or it may be formed from the root *tviṣ*, "to shine", or from the root *takṣ*, in the sense of a doer. From these derivations Tvaṣṭṛ is understood to be one who pervades quickly, one who shines, and a maker. To show to which world this deity belongs, they give माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*): some say he belongs to the group of atmospheric deities, and Śākapūṇi says he is Agni. The Bṛhaddevatā, approving the first view:

त्वष्टा रूपविकर्ता च योऽसौ माध्यमिके गणे । (*tvaṣṭā rūpavikartā ca yo 'sau mādhyamike gaṇe |*)
स्तुतः स च निपातेन सूक्तं स्य तन विद्यते । (*stutaḥ sa ca nipātena sūktaṃ sya tana vidyate |*)
(बृ. पे. ३-२५) (*(bṛ. pe. 3-25)*)

says in this verse that he belongs to the group of the middle-world deities. Before this:

त्वष्टा तु यस्त्वयमेव पार्थिवोऽग्निरिति स्तुतिः । (*tvaṣṭā tu yastvayameva pārthivo 'gniriti stutiḥ |*)
पार्थिवस्यास्य वर्चः स्युः कस्याप्यक् चार्तवेषु च ॥ (*pārthivasyāsya varcaḥ syuḥ kasyāpyak cārtaveṣu ca ‖*)
त्वषितस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् तूर्णमश्नुत एव ना । (*tvaṣitastvakṣatervā syāt tūrṇamaśnuta eva nā |*)
कर्मसूत्तारणो वेति तेन नामैतदश्नुते ॥ (*karmasūttāraṇo veti tena nāmaitadaśnute ‖*)
यः सहस्रतमो रश्मी रवेश्चंद्रमुपाश्रितः । (*yaḥ sahasratamo raśmī raveścaṃdramupāśritaḥ |*)
सोऽपि त्वष्टारमेवाग्निं परं चेह च यन्मधु ॥ (*so 'pi tvaṣṭāramevāgniṃ paraṃ ceha ca yanmadhu ‖*)
(बृ. दे. ३-१५ रिंद १७) (*(bṛ. de. 3-15 riṃda 17)*)

there is, in some places, an indication that the praise which is for the terrestrial Agni is the same praise addressed to Tvaṣṭṛ, a deity belonging to the earth. In the sūktas of the seasons too he is described as a portion of Agni.

### Printed p. 264

*Running head: [264 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188] (as supplied).*

Thus afterwards the derivation of the word *tvaṣṭṛ* found in the Nirukta is stated. It is also described that the thousandfold ray of the sun, pervaded by the moon, pervades honey, the other world and the earth, and likewise exists in Tvaṣṭṛ. Mainly the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā approve in this matter the view of Śākapūṇi stated in the Nirukta. In the Nighaṇṭu Tvaṣṭṛ is placed first with the Āprī deities (५-२ (*5-2*)), then with the atmospheric deities (५-५ (*5-5*)), and first with the deities of heaven (५-६ (*5-6*)). The story of Tvaṣṭṛ and the sage Dadhīci has been told in the special topics of sūkta १-१३९ (*1-139*). In the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa:

त्वष्टारं यजति वाग्वै त्वष्टा वाग्भेदं सर्वं । त्वाष्ट्रीं वाचमेव तत्प्री- (*tvaṣṭāraṃ yajati vāgvai tvaṣṭā vāgbhedaṃ sarvaṃ | tvāṣṭrīṃ vācameva tatprī-*)
णाति वाचं यजमाने दधाति । (*ṇāti vācaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*)
(इ. ब्रा. २-४) (*(i. brā. 2-4)*)

by this sentence identity between Tvaṣṭṛ and speech is stated, which is also one view.

य इमे द्रावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । (*ya ime drāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā |*)
तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् । (*tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān |*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-११०-९) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-110-9)*)

In this ṛk it is praised that this deity has a divine birth and that therefore even in the times of creation he shows his antiquity; the view is that Tvaṣṭṛ is most ancient:

इह त्वष्टारमग्रियं विश्वरूपमुपह्वये । अस्माकमस्तु केवलः ॥ (*iha tvaṣṭāramagriyaṃ viśvarūpamupahvaye | asmākamastu kevalaḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१३-१०) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-13-10)*)

त्वष्टारमग्रजां गोपां पुरोयावानमा हुवे । (*tvaṣṭāramagrajāṃ gopāṃ puroyāvānamā huve |*)
इंदुरिंद्रो वृषा हरिः पवमानः प्रजापतिः ॥ (*iṃduriṃdro vṛṣā hariḥ pavamānaḥ prajāpatiḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. ९-५-९) (*(ma. saṃ. 9-5-9)*)

in these and other ṛks this is known from the epithets *agriya* and *agraja*.

त्वष्टा रूपाणि हि प्रभुः पशून्विश्वान्स्मानजे । तेषां नः स्नातिमा यज । (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi hi prabhuḥ paśūnviśvānsmānaje | teṣāṃ naḥ snātimā yaja |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१८८-९) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-188-9)*)

तृष्णा रूपाणि विकरोति । (*tṛṣṇā rūpāṇi vikaroti |*)
(तै. सं. १-५-९-२) (*(tai. saṃ. 1-5-9-2)*)

These and other sentences praise Tvaṣṭṛ's work of making. Moreover he has the epithet *viśvarūpa* (ऋ. सं. १-१३-१० (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-13-10*)).

### Printed p. 265

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 9] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 265 (as supplied).*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 9, noted briefly)

समानजे (*samānaje*): preverb सम् (*sam*), root अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षकांतिगतिष्टु (*aṃjū vyaktimrakṣakāṃtigatiṣṭu*); in the Vedic manner *liṭ*; by लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेज् (*liṭastajhayoreśirej*) (पा. सू. ३-४-८१ (*pā. sū. 3-4-81*)) the substitute *eś* for the ending *ta*; because the suffix is treated as marked *k*, the nasal is dropped; when reduplications come on that basis, by तस्मान्नुट्- द्विहलः (*tasmānnuṭ- dvihalaḥ*) (पा. सू ७-४-७१ (*pā. sū 7-4-71*)) the augment *nuṭ*; by हिच (*hica*) (पा. सू. ८-१-३४ (*pā. sū. 8-1-34*)) the *nighāta* accent is prohibited, so by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute; by तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (पा. सू. ८-१-७१ (*pā. sū. 8-1-71*)) *sam* is unaccented. स्फातिम् (*sphātim*): root स्थायी वृद्धौ (*sthāyī vṛddhau*) (as printed); by क्तिच्‌क्तौच— (*kticktauca—*) (पा. सू. ३-३-१७४ (*pā. sū. 3-3-174*)) the suffix *ktic*; by लोपोव्यो— (*lopovyo—*) the dropping of *y*; being marked *c*, the last syllable is acute. यज (*yaja*): root यज देवपूजादिषु (*yaja devapūjādiṣu*); *loṭ*, second person singular; the verb-*nighāta* accent.

*[Stray/garbled line of the supplied text where the Saṃhitā label belongs: 108 गानगळु (*108 gānagaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उप॒ त्मन्या॑ वनस्पते॒ पाथो॑ दे॒वेभ्यः॑ सृज ।
> अ॒ग्निर्ह॒व्यानि॑ सिष्पदत् ॥ १० ॥

> *upa tmanyā vanaspate pātho devebhyaḥ sṛja |*
> *agnirhavyāni siṣpadat ‖ 10 ‖*

*[The Pada has त्र्यन्या (*tryanyā*) against the Saṃhitā's *tmanyā*, and its closing numeral is printed ೧೧ where ೧೦ is expected, as printed.]*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उप । त्र्यन्या । वनस्पते । पाथः । देवेभ्यः । सृज ।
> अग्निः । हव्यानि । सिस्वदत् ॥ ११ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे वनस्पते यूपाभिमानि देव त्मन्यात्मनैव देवेभ्योऽग्न्यादिभ्यः पाथः
> पशुरूपमन्नमुप सृज । उत्पादय । यूपाभावे पशुनियोजनाभावेन हविषोऽ-
> भावात् । त्वय्येवं कृतवति सत्यग्निर्हव्यानि हवींषि सिस्पदत् । स्वदयतु । स्वादू-
> करोतु ॥

*Gist:* O Vanaspati, deity of the sacrificial post, of your own accord produce the animal-food for Agni and the other gods; then Agni will make the oblations sweet, since without the post there is no animal and no oblation.

**Pratipadārtha** (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window)

वनस्पते—ऎलै यूपाभिमानिदेवतॆये (*vanaspate—èlai yūpābhimānidevatèye*) (O deity of the sacrificial post). त्मन्या—निन्न स्वरूपदिंदले (*tmanyā—ninna svarūpadiṃdale*) (by your own self). देवेभ्यः— अग्न्यादिदेवतॆगळिगॆ (*devebhyaḥ— agnyādidevatègaḷigè*) (for the gods, Agni and the rest). पाथः—पशुरूपवाद अन्नवन्नु (*pāthaḥ—paśurūpavāda annavannu*) (food in the form of an animal). उप सृज—सृष्टिमाडु (आनंतर) (*upa sṛja—sṛṣṭimāḍu (ānaṃtara)*) (create; then). अग्निः—अग्नियु (*agniḥ—agniyu*) (Agni). हव्यानि—हविस्सुगळन्नु (*havyāni—havissugaḷannu*) (the oblations). सिस्वदत्—आस्वादिसलि (*sisvadat—āsvādisali*) (let him taste).

### Printed p. 266

*Running head: [266 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188] (as supplied).*

**Bhāvārtha** (Ṛk 10; the Pratipadārtha ended on p. 265)

O deity of the sacrificial post, from your own nature create for Agni and the other gods the animal-food. Then let Agni taste the oblations.

**Printed English translation**

Vanaspati, deliver of yourself the victim to the gods, so that Agni may taste the oblation.

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 10)**

वनस्पते (*vanaspate*) — Yāska's explanation of the word *vanaspati*:

वनस्पत इत्येनमाहैष हि वनानां पाता ना पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः ॥ (*vanaspata ityenamāhaiṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā nā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ ‖*)
(नि. ८-३) (*(ni. 8-3)*)

तत्को वनस्पतिः । यूप इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*tatko vanaspatiḥ | yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*) (नि. ८-१८ (*ni. 8-18*))

That is, they call Agni himself *vanaspati*, for Agni is the protector or guardian of the forests. Though Agni is present within a tree, he does not burn it, so he is called its protector; or *vana* means wood used for the implements of sacrifice, such as timber. *Vanaspate* means "king of trees", a large tree. Who is the deity *vanaspati*? Kātthakya's view is that it is the wooden post set up in the sacrifice for binding the animal; Śākapūṇi's view is that *vanaspati* is Agni.

To support Kātkya's view Yāska gave a ṛk as an example:

अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन ॥ (*aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃto vanaspate madhunā daivyena ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. ३-८-१) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 3-8-1)*)

That is: O Vanaspati (sacrificial post), the sacrificers and priests anoint you in the sacrifice with ghee consecrated by mantras; so the post for binding the animal is addressed. In the third, sixth and eleventh ṛks of this same sūkta too Vanaspati is addressed as the sacrificial post, and it is well known that the post itself is the deity of this sūkta. In the eleventh ṛk of this sūkta, वनस्पते शतवल्यो विरोह सहस्रवल्या वि वयं रुहेम (*vanaspate śatavalyo viroha sahasravalyā vi vayaṃ ruhema*), "O Vanaspati, grow with hundreds and thousands of sprouts" applies to Vanaspati as a tree. In the ṛk ऋ सं. १०-७०-१० (*ṛ saṃ. 10-70-10*), वनस्पते रशनया नियूय (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūya*), "O Vanaspati, bind with the rope for binding the animal", confirms the sense "sacrificial post" for the word *vanaspati*. Therefore *vanaspati* means the sacrificial post; "Agni" is the indirect sense.

### Printed p. 267

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 9] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 267 (as supplied).*

The nature of Vanaspati must be understood by much examination. On the basis of this word some modern Western scholars have concluded that in the Vedic period the violent animal sacrifice was prominent and that the Āprī sūktas were *prayāja* mantras connected with such a sacrifice.

From a gross point of view *vanaspati* is the sacrificial post to which the sacrificial animal is bound. But whether it is the post to which the sacrificial animal is bound or not, its nature can be determined after noting the scriptural sentences and relying on them. In the Praiṣa sūkta:

होता यक्षद्वनस्पतिमुपावस्रक्षद्धियो जोष्टारग्ं शशमं नरः । स्वदात्स- (*hotā yakṣadvanaspatimupāvasrakṣaddhiyo joṣṭāragṃ śaśamaṃ naraḥ | svadātsa-*)
धितिर्यतुथाद्य देवो देवेभ्यो हव्यवाड्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज । (*dhitiryatuthādya devo devebhyo havyavāḍvetvājyasya hotaryaja |*)
(तै. ब्रा. ३-६-२-२) (*(tai. brā. 3-6-2-2)*)

the commentary on this mantra is as follows: वनस्पतिं यूपाधारभूतं दशमप्रयाजदेवतात्मक- मग्निं दैवो होता यजतु (*vanaspatiṃ yūpādhārabhūtaṃ daśamaprayājadevatātmaka- magniṃ daivo hotā yajatu*): "let the divine hotṛ sacrifice to Agni in the form of the tenth *prayāja* deity, who is the support of the post"; that is, Vanaspati is the support of the post, and the hotṛ is to sacrifice to him, Agni, the tenth *prayāja* deity. Vanaspati has the epithets धियो जोष्णा (*dhiyo joṣṇā*), स्वदात् स्वधितिः (*svadāt svadhitiḥ*), देवेभ्यः ऋतुधा हव्यवाट् (*devebhyaḥ ṛtudhā havyavāṭ*), यज्ञस्य आयुः कल्पमानः (*yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ*). Of these, धियो जोष्णा (*dhiyo joṣṇā*) is explained as बुद्धॆः प्रीणयितारं (*buddhèḥ prīṇayitāraṃ*), "a giver of joy to the mind"; स्वदितिः (*svaditiḥ*) as "prepared with the *svadhiti* (thunderbolt or) divine weapon"; ऋतुधा (*ṛtudhā*) as ऋत् विहिते कालविशेषे अद्य अस्मिन्कर्मणि स्वदादस्माभिर्दि- यमानं हविः स्वदयतु । किंच देवो वनस्पतिर्देवेभ्यो देवार्थं हव्या हवींष्य वाड्वहतु (*ṛt vihite kālaviśeṣe adya asminkarmaṇi svadādasmābhirdi- yamānaṃ haviḥ svadayatu | kiṃca devo vanaspatirdevebhyo devārthaṃ havyā havīṃṣya vāḍvahatu*): "at the appointed time, today, in this rite, let him sweeten the oblation given by us, and let the god Vanaspati carry the oblations to the gods": this is the sense of the mantra. And the epithet यज्ञस्य आयुः कल्पमानः (*yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ*) means "one who prolongs the life of the sacrifice". By such epithets the Praiṣa sūkta states the identity of Agni and Vanaspati. In the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa it is indicated by the sentence प्राणो वै वनस्पतिः (*prāṇo vai vanaspatiḥ*) (२-४ (*2-4*)) (the print has "ನಿರ್ದೆಶಿಸಿದೆ"). The Nirukta-authors first give the derivation of the word *vanaspati* and then state the nature of Vanaspati in the Āprī sūkta. In explaining the ṛk ऋ. सं. २-३७-३ (*ṛ. saṃ. 2-37-3*) they show the derivation of the word *vanaspati* in it (नि. ८-३ (*ni. 8-3*)): वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः (*vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ*): Agni is famed as *vanaspati* as the lord or protector of the forests, and the word is formed from the root *van*, meaning "to obtain"; then, discussing the nature of the deities of the Āprī sūkta (८-१८ (*8-18*)), तत् को वनस्पतिः, यूप इति कात्क्यः अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*tat ko vanaspatiḥ, yūpa iti kātkyaḥ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*), they state the two opinions, and to support the view of Kātkya (the print has दुतवन्नु (*dutavannu*) for the word "view")

### Printed p. 268

*Running head: [268 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188] (as supplied).*

अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन । (*aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃto vanaspate madhunā daivyena |*)
यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा द्रविणेह धत्ताद्यद्वा क्षयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे ॥ (*yadūrdhvastiṣṭhā draviṇeha dhattādyadvā kṣayo māturasyā upasthe ‖*)

they cited this ṛk. In this ṛk Sāyaṇa addresses the word *vanaspati* as the sacrificial post. Then, to support the view of Śākapūṇi, the Nirukta-authors cited

वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् । (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān |*)
स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्धवींष्यवतां द्यावापृथिवी हवं मे ॥ (*svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavaddhavīṃṣyavatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī havaṃ me ‖*)
(१०-७०-१०) (*(10-70-10)*)

Here too Sāyaṇa takes it as the post; but the Nirukta-authors' view is that it is the Agni inside the post. Durgācārya, explaining this ṛk in the Nirukta, says एवमग्निर्वनस्पतिः । यत् पुनरेतदुक्तं यूपांजनीयायां 'यूपे वनस्पतिशब्दः' इति । अत्र ब्रूमः—अग्निरेवास् यूपांतर्गतो यूपात्मना वर्तमानो यूपां- जनीयायां वनस्पतिशब्देनोच्यते (*evamagnirvanaspatiḥ | yat punaretaduktaṃ yūpāṃjanīyāyāṃ 'yūpe vanaspatiśabdaḥ ' iti | atra brūmaḥ—agnirevās yūpāṃtargato yūpātmanā vartamāno yūpāṃ- janīyāyāṃ vanaspatiśabdenocyate*). He thus establishes that here *vanaspati* is none other than the Agni within the post. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā:

वनस्पतिं तु यं प्राहुरयं सोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः । (*vanaspatiṃ tu yaṃ prāhurayaṃ so 'gnirvanaspatiḥ |*)
अयं वनानां हि पतिः पाता पालयतीति वा ॥ (*ayaṃ vanānāṃ hi patiḥ pātā pālayatīti vā ‖*)
अग्निर्गृत्समदेनायं वनस्पतिरितीळितः । (*agnirgṛtsamadenāyaṃ vanaspatiritīḷitaḥ |*)
मंदस्वेत्यस्य सूक्तस्य षळ्ळ्यचस्य तृतीयया ॥ (*maṃdasvetyasya sūktasya ṣaḷḷyacasya tṛtīyayā ‖*)
यूपवत्तरुवच्चैव स्तुतियार्यस्य प्रसंगजा । (*yūpavattaruvaccaiva stutiyāryasya prasaṃgajā |*)
सर्वेणांजति सूक्तेन तृतीये सा तु मंडले ॥ (*sarveṇāṃjati sūktena tṛtīye sā tu maṃḍale ‖*)
(बृ. दे. ३-२६रिंद २८) (*(bṛ. de. 3-26riṃda 28)*)

by these sentences they discuss the nature of the Āprī deity addressed in the ṛk ऋ. सं. १-१३-११ (*ṛ. saṃ. 1-13-11*) and say that here *vanaspati* means the terrestrial Agni, that in the ṛk ऋ सं. २-३७-२ (*ṛ saṃ. 2-37-2*) too Gṛtsamada addresses this terrestrial Agni by the word *vanaspati*, and that only in some ṛks of the third maṇḍala is the sense post or tree, and that also by contextual reasons. Besides:

इहैष पवमानोग्निर्मध्यमोग्निर्वनस्पतिः । (*ihaiṣa pavamānognirmadhyamognirvanaspatiḥ |*)
अमुष्मिन्नेव विप्रैस्तु लोकेग्निश्युचिरुच्यते ॥ (*amuṣminneva vipraistu lokegniśyucirucyate ‖*)
(बृ दे १-६६) (*(bṛ de 1-66)*)

(the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window, after the Bṛhaddevatā verse).

...in this verse, showing that *vanaspati* means the Agni of the middle world, they state definitively that, except in a few places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, in the many other places this word indicates Agni and there is no doubt of it.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 10, noted briefly)

तन्न्या (*tannyā*) (the print): the word *ātman*; when the instrumental singular follows, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (पा. सद. (*pā. sada.*) [sic] ७-१-३९ (*7-1-39*)) the substitute *yā* for it; by मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरात्मनः (*maṃtreṣvājyāderātmanaḥ*) the initial *ā* is dropped. सृज (*sṛja*): root सृज विसर्गे (*sṛja visarge*); *loṭ*, second person singular; the verb-*nighāta* accent. सिष्टदत् (*siṣṭadat*): root स्वद आस्वादने (*svada āsvādane*); by छंदसिलुज् लज् लिटः (*chaṃdasiluj laj liṭaḥ*) (पा. सू. ३.४-६ (*pā. sū. 3.4-6*)) *luṅ* in the sense of *loṭ* after the causative; third person singular *tip*; by इतश्च (*itaśca*) the final *i* is dropped; by णिश्रिद्रुसुभ्यः— (*ṇiśridrusubhyaḥ—*) (पा. सू. ३-१-४९ (*pā. sū. 3-1-49*)) the substitute *caṅ* for *cli*; reduplication of the root on account of *caṅ*; by बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्— (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasyamāj—*) (पा. सू. ६-४-७५ (*pā. sū. 6-4-75*)) the augment *aṭ* does not occur; owing to the connection with a finite verb the *nighāta* accent.

### Printed p. 270

*Running head: [270 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. . A. 24. Sū. 188] (as supplied; the print has a blank where the maṇḍala numeral belongs).*

> समज्यते सम्यग्लक्ष्यते । स्वाहाकृतीषु स्वाहाकारेषु सत्सु हविःषु दीयमानेषु
> रोचते । अत्यर्थं दीप्यते । एताः प्रयाजदेवता यज्ञावयवाभिमानिन्यः । तद्वारा
> यज्ञ एव स्तूयत इति केषांचिन्मतं । अग्निरेव नामांतरमित्यन्ये ॥

*Gist:* Agni goes in front of the gods, to war with the demons or in the sacrifice, and is celebrated by the gāyatra mantra; when oblations are offered with *svāhā* he blazes. These *prayāja* deities preside over parts of the sacrifice, so the sacrifice itself is praised through them, some think; others say they are only other names of Agni.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्निः—अग्नियु (*agniḥ—agniyu*) (Agni). देवानां—देवतॆगळिगॆल्ला (*devānāṃ—devatègaḷigèllā*) (of all the gods). पुरोगाः—युद्ध कालदल्लालि अथवा यागकालदल्लागलि मुंदाळागिद्दानॆ (ई अग्नियु) (*purogāḥ—yuddha kāladallāli athavā yāgakāladallāgali muṃdāḷāgiddānè (ī agniyu)*) (the leader, in time of war or in time of sacrifice). गायत्रेण—गायत्ररूपवाद मंत्र दिंद (*gāyatreṇa—gāyatrarūpavāda maṃtra diṃda*) (by the mantra in gāyatra form). समज्यते—वर्णितनागिद्दानॆ (*samajyate—varṇitanāgiddānè*) (is celebrated). स्वाहाकृतीषु—स्वाहाकारपूर्वकवागि हविस्सन्नु अर्पिसिदाग (*svāhākṛtīṣu—svāhākārapūrvakavāgi havissannu arpisidāga*) (when oblations are offered with *svāhā*). रोचते—प्रकाशिसुत्तानॆ (*rocate—prakāśisuttānè*) (he shines).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भानुवार (*bhānuvāra*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

In time of war or in time of sacrifice Agni goes before all the gods. This Agni is celebrated by a mantra in gāyatra form. When oblations are offered with *svāhā* he shines.

**Printed English translation**

Agni, the preceder of the gods, is characterized by the Gayatri measure; (metre) ; he blazes when the oblations are offered.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 11)**

पुरोगाः (*purogāḥ*) — आयमग्निर्देवानां पुरोगा आसुरयुद्धं प्रति पुरोगामी । यद्वा । देवानां मध्यॆ यज्ञं प्रत्यग्नि रेव पुरोगामी (*āyamagnirdevānāṃ purogā āsurayuddhaṃ prati purogāmī | yadvā | devānāṃ madhyè yajñaṃ pratyagni reva purogāmī*) (the print has "ಆಯಮ" and "ಆಸುರ"): that is, in fighting the demons this Agni is the leader, the chief, of the gods and of men; or in the sacrifice, when many gods are invited and praised, Agni has the first place among them, that is, Agni is praised first. The word *purohita* has more or less the same sense: because he is established in front of the sacrificers at sacrifices (on the sacrificial altar), Agni is called *purohita*. From whatever point of view one looks, it must be said that Agni has the first (chief) place in sacrifices and the like. On this Yāska says अग्निः कस्मात् अग्रणीर्भवतीति (*agniḥ kasmāt agraṇīrbhavatīti*) (नि. ७-१४ (*ni. 7-14*)), explaining the derivation of the word *agni*: because he is like a leader in front of all, he is named Agni. Therefore here Agni is described by the word *purogāḥ*.

गायत्रेण सं अज्यते (*gāyatreṇa saṃ ajyate*) — by the *gāyatrī* metre, or by the sāman mantra called *gāyatra*, we offer this mantra called *svāhākṛti* to Agni: this is the sense. The word गायत्रवेपसे (*gāyatravepase*) in the ṛk ऋ. सं १-१४२-१२ (*ṛ. saṃ 1-142-12*) supports this meaning too.

### Printed p. 271

*Running head: [Ā. 2. Ā. 5. Va. 9] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 271 (as supplied).*

स्वाहाकृतीपु (*svāhākṛtīpu*) (the print has *pu* for *ṣu*) — Yāska's explanation:

स्वाहाकृतयः । साहाकृतयः स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा । स्वा वागाहेति (*svāhākṛtayaḥ | sāhākṛtayaḥ svāhetyetat su āheti vā | svā vāgāheti*)
वा । स्वं प्राहेति वा । स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा ॥ (*vā | svaṃ prāheti vā | svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā ‖*)
(सि. ८-२) (*(si. 8-2)*)

The word *svāhā* has four etymological meanings.
(1) सु आहेति वा (*su āheti vā*) — *su* = well, *āha* = says: since it is pronounced well or clearly, it is called *svāhā*.
(2) स्वा वागाहेति वा (*svā vāgāheti vā*) — *svā* = one's own speech: there is a scriptural sentence तं स्वा वाग- भ्यवदज्जुहुधीति तत्साहाकारस्य जन्म (*taṃ svā vāga- bhyavadajjuhudhīti tatsāhākārasya janma*) (Brāhmaṇa); that is, since in the sacrifice the sacrificer himself adds the word *svāhā* at the end of the Vedic ṛk, it is called *svāhā*.
(3) स्वं प्राहेति वा (*svaṃ prāheti vā*) — here *svam* = his own oblation, *āha* = he says he will offer: hence the name *svāhā*.
(4) स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा (*svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā*) — since the oblation he offers is offered by pronouncing the word *svāhā*, that is, by giving the oblation in the fire, it is called *svāhā*.

For the sense of *svāhākāra* Yāska gave this ṛk as an example:

सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः । (*sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |*)
अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदंतु देवाः ॥ (*asya hotuḥ pradiśyatasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradaṃtu devāḥ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं १०-११०-११) (*(ṛ. saṃ 10-110-11)*)

Its chief meaning: Agni, just born (that is, now established in the sacrifice), sits before the gods and carries on the sacrifice, performing the hotṛ's office, that is, the work of invoking the gods. May the gods eat the oblation offered with the word *svāhā* by such a hotṛ, who sits in the east and presents it. Therefore *svāhā* is the word uttered at the end of a mantra when an oblation is offered in the fire according to rule, in the sacrifice, for the pleasure of the gods.

In some Āprī sūktas the plural स्वाहाकृतयः (*svāhākṛtayaḥ*) is used. In this sūkta the eleven deities, the eleven *prayāja* mantras used in the offering (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 272

*Running head: [272 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 188] (as supplied).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 11 of Sūkta 188, on *svāhākṛti*.)*

...mantras: because the *svāhā* is added in reciting them for all the eleven deities, the plural स्वाहाकृतयः (*svāhākṛtayaḥ*) is used.

In the Purāṇas and elsewhere the word *svāhā* is used in another sense: in the Mahābhārata *Svāhā* is the name of the daughter of Bṛhaspati, son of the sage Aṅgiras; in the Purāṇas the goddess Svāhā is said to be the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati and the wife of Agni.

स्वाहा इत्येवंपूर्वा कृतिः करणमुच्चारणं यक्ष्यमाणदेवतानां ताः स्वाहाकृतयः । तद्वंति हव्यानि (*svāhā ityevaṃpūrvā kṛtiḥ karaṇamuccāraṇaṃ yakṣyamāṇadevatānāṃ tāḥ svāhākṛtayaḥ | tadvaṃti havyāni*) — as an epithet of the word *havyāni* it means oblations accompanied by the mantra *svāhā* used for presenting the offering. It is a word chiefly recited in the last ṛks of the Āprī sūktas. In some ṛks it is also an adverbial: १-१३-१२ (*1-13-12*) has स्वाहा कृषोतन (*svāhā kṛṣotana*), १-१४-१२ (*1-14-12*) has स्वाहा कर्तन (*svāhā kartana*); in ३-४-११, ७-२-११ (*3-4-11, 7-2-11*) and १०-७०-११ (*10-70-11*) it is in the instrumental sense; in २-३-११ (*2-3-11*) it is an epithet of the oblation, and in १०-११०-११ (*10-110-11*) an epithet of *haviḥ*.

In explaining this word, some have held that the deity-form *svāhākṛti* is indicated, and others that Agni is indicated. In the Praiṣa sūkta:

होता यक्षदग्निग् स्वाहाज्यस्य............वियॆंतु होतरज । (*hotā yakṣadagnig svāhājyasya............viyèṃtu hotaraja |*)
(तै. ब्रा. ३-६-२-२) (*(tai. brā. 3-6-2-2)*)

is recited. On this Sāyaṇa says योऽयं स्वाहाशब्दोदितः उत्तमप्रयाजदेवः अग्निः तं दैव्यू होता यजतु (*yo 'yaṃ svāhāśabdoditaḥ uttamaprayājadevaḥ agniḥ taṃ daivyū hotā yajatu*): "let the divine hotṛ sacrifice to that Agni, the last *prayāja* deity, who is named by the word *svāhā*"; he explains that the word indicates Agni as the eleventh *prayāja* deity. The Nirukta-authors:

साहाकृतयः । स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा, स्वा वागाहेति वा स्वं प्राहेति (*sāhākṛtayaḥ | svāhetyetat su āheti vā, svā vāgāheti vā svaṃ prāheti*)
वा, स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा । (*vā, svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā |*)
(सि. ८-२१) (*(si. 8-21)*)

explaining that it is famed as *svāhākṛti* either because "he recited it well", "because one's own speech said it", or because the oblation is offered with the mantra *svāhā*, and citing the ṛk १०-११०-११ (*10-110-11*), make this sense clear. In the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa:

स्वाहाकृतीर्यजति प्रतिष्ठा वै स्वाहाकृतयः प्रतिष्ठायामेव तद्वज्ञमंततः (*svāhākṛtīryajati pratiṣṭhā vai svāhākṛtayaḥ pratiṣṭhāyāmeva tadvajñamaṃtataḥ*)
प्रतिष्ठापयति । (*pratiṣṭhāpayati |*)
(ऎ. च. २-इ) (*(è. ca. 2-i)*)

### Printed p. 273

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 9] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 273 (as supplied).*

it is explained that, since the oblation is completed by the *svāhākṛti*, it is the support of the whole sacrifice and sets the sacrifice on a right foundation. In the Bṛhaddevatā:

स्वाहाकृतयोऽनेकाश्च विदुषां मतयोऽभवन् । (*svāhākṛtayo 'nekāśca viduṣāṃ matayo 'bhavan |*)
तत्सर्वं त्वयमेवाग्निर्भवतीति विनिश्चयः ॥ (*tatsarvaṃ tvayamevāgnirbhavatīti viniścayaḥ ‖*)
अयं हि कर्ता स्वाहानां कृतिस्तासामिहैकजा । (*ayaṃ hi kartā svāhānāṃ kṛtistāsāmihaikajā |*)
अयं प्रसूतिर्भूतानां सर्वेषामयमव्ययः ॥ (*ayaṃ prasūtirbhūtānāṃ sarveṣāmayamavyayaḥ ‖*)
(बृ. दे. ३-२९ रिंद ३०) (*(bṛ. de. 3-29 riṃda 30)*)

The opinions of the learned about *svāhākṛti* are not of one kind; yet the whole sense indicated by this word is meant for this terrestrial Agni: because this Agni is the maker of the *svāhās* and is also their making, the terrestrial Agni is so called. Following the Nirukta-authors' view आग्नेयी इति तु स्थितिः (*āgneyī iti tu sthitiḥ*) (नि. ८-२२ (*ni. 8-22*)) the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā have given their opinion.

In the last ṛks of the Āprī sūktas of the *svāhākāra* kind, the deities Pūṣan, the Maruts, Vāyu, Sūrya, Indra, Varuṇa and others are all addressed; above all of them:

पुरोगा आग्निर्देवानां गायत्रेण समज्यते । साहाकृतीषु रोचते । (*purogā āgnirdevānāṃ gāyatreṇa samajyate | sāhākṛtīṣu rocate |*)
(ऋ. सं. १-१८८-११) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 1-188-11)*)

सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः । (*sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |*)
अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदंतु देवाः ॥ (*asya hotuḥ pradiśyatasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradaṃtu devāḥ ‖*)
(म सं १०-११०-११) (*(ma saṃ 10-110-11)*)

in these ṛks Agni is praised as the leader of the gods from the time of his birth. And describing the power of the *svāhākṛti*:

आ याह्यग्ने समिधानो अर्वाजिंद्रेण देवैः सरथं तुरेभिः । (*ā yāhyagne samidhāno arvājiṃdreṇa devaiḥ sarathaṃ turebhiḥ |*)
बर्हिर्न आस्तामदितिः सुपुत्रा स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयंतां ॥ (*barhirna āstāmaditiḥ suputrā svāhā devā amṛtā mādayaṃtāṃ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं) (*(ṛ. saṃ)*)
(म. सं ३-४-११) (*(ma. saṃ 3-4-11)*)

आग्ने वह वरुणमिष्टये न इंद्र दिवो मरुतो अंतरिक्षात् । (*āgne vaha varuṇamiṣṭaye na iṃdra divo maruto aṃtarikṣāt |*)
सीदंतु बर्हिर्विश्व आ यजत्राः स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयंतां ॥ (*sīdaṃtu barhirviśva ā yajatrāḥ svāhā devā amṛtā mādayaṃtāṃ ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-७०-११) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-70-11)*)

in these ṛks it is indicated that, because the gods rejoice at the mantra *svāhā*, the word *svāhā* has such a divine place in the sacrifice. (The print gives the reference of the third ṛk twice, (ऋ. सं) (*(ṛ. saṃ)*) and (म. सं ३-४-११) (*(ma. saṃ 3-4-11)*).)

### Printed p. 274

*Running head: [274 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. ೨೪. Sū. 188] (as supplied; the print omits the adhyāya sign).*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 11, noted briefly)

पुरोगा: (*purogā:*): root गम्‌ल्य गत् (*gamlya gat*); by जनसनखन क्रमगमॊविट् (*janasanakhana kramagamòviṭ*) (पा. सू. ३-२-६७ (*pā. sū. 3-2-67*)) the suffix *viṭ*; when it follows, by विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् (*viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt*) (पा. सू. ६-४-४१ (*pā. sū. 6-4-41*)) the nasal *m* of the root becomes *ā*; the suffix is wholly dropped; in the compound the accent of the first member of the *kṛt* compound. गायत्रेण (*gāyatreṇa*): गायत्राः संबंधि गायत्रम्. तस्येदम् (*gāyatrāḥ saṃbaṃdhi gāyatram. tasyedam*) (पा. सू. ४-३-१२२ (*pā. sū. 4-3-122*)) the suffix *aṇ*; by यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) the preceding *ī* is dropped; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute; instrumental singular. अज्यते (*ajyate*) (root अंजूव्यक्तिम्रक्षकांतिगतिषु (*aṃjūvyaktimrakṣakāṃtigatiṣu*)): *laṭ* in the passive, third person singular; owing to the connection with a finite verb the *nighāta* accent. रोचते (*rocate*) (root रुच दीप्ति (*ruca dīpti*)): *bhvādi*, *laṭ*, third person singular; by तिज्जतिजः (*tijjatijaḥ*) (पा. सू. ८-१-२८ (*pā. sū. 8-1-28*)) the *nighāta* accent.

*(Sūkta 188 ends here, with eleven ṛks. No colophon line is printed in the supplied text.)*

#### Sūkta 189

नूर ऎंभत्तॊंभत्तनॆय सूक्तवु. (*nūra èṃbhattòṃbhattanèya sūktavu.*) — "the hundred and eighty-ninth sūkta."

*[As supplied, the label line reads कायिभास्कर (*kāyibhāskara*) (garbled, for *sāyaṇabhāṣya*); the following lines are Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 189, printed as plain lines, and are given here as a block.]*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (introduction)

> अग्ने नयेति दशमं सूक्तमष्टर्चमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभवाग्नेयं । अग्ने
> नयोष्टावाग्नेयमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाशिनशस्त्रयोस्ट्रैष्टुभश्चंदसि विनि-
> योगः । अथैतस्या इत्यत्राग्ने नयाग्रे बृहन्नित्यष्टानामुत्तमास्तुत्मास्ति स्र उद्दरेत् ।
> आ, ४-१३ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ अत्र शौनकः । उत्पथप्रतिपन्नो यो भ्रष्टो वापि पथः
> क्वचित् । पंथानं प्रतिपद्येत कृत्वा वा कर्म गर्हितं ॥ अग्ने नयेति सूक्तेन
> प्रत्यृचं जुहुयाद्कृतं । जपेच्च प्रयतो नित्यमुपतिष्ठेत वानलं । ऋग्वि १-२७ ।
> इति ॥ आद्याश्चतस्रः श्रवणाकर्मणि विनियुक्ताः । श्रावण्यां पौर्णमास्यामित्यत्र
> सूत्रितं । अग्ने नय सुपथा राये आस्मानिति चतसृभिः प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा । आ. गृ २-१-४ ।
> इति ॥ अग्नॆये पशौ वनापुरोडाशयोराद्ये द्वे अनुवाक्ये । तथा च सूत्रितं ।
> अग्ने नय सुपथा राये आस्मान् पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैः । अ ३-७ । इति ॥
> आद्या प्रायणीयेष्टावाग्नेयस्यानुवाक्या । सैवोदयनीये याज्या । तदहः
> प्रायणीयेष्टिरित्यत्र सूत्रितं । अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्माना देवानामपि
> पंथामगन्म । आ. ४-३ । इति ॥ विपरीताश्च याज्यानुवाक्या इति च ॥

*Gist:* The sūkta beginning "Agne naya" is the tenth sūkta of this group, of eight ṛks, by Agastya, in *triṣṭubh*, to Agni (Anukramaṇikā). It is used in the morning litany; Śaunaka prescribes it for one who has strayed from the path, the first four ṛks are used in the Śrāvaṇa rite (Āśvalāyana Gṛhya), and the ṛks are variously used in the animal sacrifice, in the Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya offerings (Śrauta rules).

### Printed p. 275

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 9] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 275 (as supplied).*

**Anuvāda (Kannada)** of Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 189 (continued from p. 274). This sūkta beginning अग्ने नय (*agne naya*) is the tenth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Agastya is the seer of this sūkta; Agni is the deity; the metre is *triṣṭubh*. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated as अग्ने नयाष्टावाग्नेयं (*agne nayāṣṭāvāgneyaṃ*) and so on. Its use for the *triṣṭubh* mantras of the Āśvina litany at the time of reciting the morning-recitation mantras is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra rule अथैतस्या इत्यत्राग्ने नयाग्रे बृहन्नित्य- ष्टानामुत्तमादुत्तमास्तिस्र उद्धरेत् (*athaitasyā ityatrāgne nayāgre bṛhannitya- ṣṭānāmuttamāduttamāstisra uddharet*) (आ ४-१३ (*ā 4-13*)). And on the use of this sūkta the sage Śaunaka in the work Ṛgvidhāna says:

उत्पथप्रतिपन्नो यो भ्रष्टो वापि पथः क्वचित् । (*utpathapratipanno yo bhraṣṭo vāpi pathaḥ kvacit |*)
पंथानं प्रतिपद्येत कृत्वा वा कर्म गर्हितं ॥ (*paṃthānaṃ pratipadyeta kṛtvā vā karma garhitaṃ ‖*)
अग्ने नयेति सूक्तेन प्रत्यृ चं जुहुयाद्भृतं । (*agne nayeti sūktena pratyṛ caṃ juhuyādbhṛtaṃ |*)
जपेच्च प्रयतो नित्यमुपतिष्ठेत वानलं ॥ (*japecca prayato nityamupatiṣṭheta vānalaṃ ‖*)
(मुग्विधान. १-२७) (*(mugvidhāna. 1-27)*)

That is: a person who, while climbing a hill or travelling to a distant country, goes astray somewhere on the way, or unknowingly does a reprehensible act, should offer ghee in the fire with each ṛk of this sūkta beginning "Agne naya", and should, in purity, recite this sūkta daily and worship Agni; then he will find the right path: so they say. Besides, the first four ṛks of this sūkta are to be offered, each ṛk separately, in the rite called *upākarman* on the full moon with the Śravaṇa asterism, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra rule अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मानितिचतसृभिः प्रत्यैचं हुत्वा (*agne naya supathā rāye asmāniticatasṛbhiḥ pratyaicaṃ hutvā*) in the section श्रावण्यां पौर्णमास्यां (*śrāvaṇyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ*) (आ गृ. सू. २-१-४ (*ā gṛ. sū. 2-1-4*)). And in the animal sacrifice connected with Agni, when the *vapā* and *puroḍāśa* offerings are made, the first two ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as *puronuvākyā* mantras, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra rule अग्नेनय सुपथा राये अस्मान् पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैः (*agnenaya supathā rāye asmān pāhi no agne pāyubhirajasraiḥ*) (आ ३-७ (*ā 3-7*)). And in the Prāyaṇīya offering (the first day of the sacrifice) the first ṛk of this sūkta is to be used as the *puronuvākyā* mantra to Agni, and in the Udayanīya offering (the last day of the sacrifice) the same ṛk as the *yājyā* mantra, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra rules, in the section तदहः प्रायणीयॆष्टि (*tadahaḥ prāyaṇīyèṣṭi*), अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्माना देवानामपि पंथामगन्न (*agne naya supathā rāye asmānā devānāmapi paṃthāmaganna*) and also विपरीताश्च याज्यानुवाक्या (*viparītāśca yājyānuvākyā*) (आ. ४-३ (*ā. 4-3*)). (The print gives the work "ಮುಗ್ವಿಧಾನ" for *Ṛgvidhāna*, as supplied.)

### Printed p. 277

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 277 (as supplied).*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

देव—देवतात्मनाद (*deva—devatātmanāda*) (divine in nature). अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये,  (*agne—èlai agniye, *)(O Agni). विश्वानि वयुनानि—सकल ज्ञान गळन्नू (*viśvāni vayunāni—sakala jñāna gaḷannū*) (all kinds of knowledge). विद्वान्—तिळिदिरुव नीनु (*vidvān—tiḷidiruva nīnu*) (you who know). आस्मान्—नम्मन्नु (*āsmān—nammannu*) (us). सुपथा—श्रेष्ठवाद मार्गदिंद (*supathā—śreṣṭhavāda mārgadiṃda*) (by the excellent way). राये—स्वर्गादिरूपवाद संपत्तन्नु पडॆयलु ! (*rāye—svargādirūpavāda saṃpattannu paḍèyalu !*) (to obtain wealth in the form of heaven and the like). नय—करॆदुकॊंडु होगु (*naya—karèdukòṃḍu hogu*) (lead). जुहुराणं— कुटिलवाद मार्गदल्लि ऎळॆयतक्क (*juhurāṇaṃ— kuṭilavāda mārgadalli èḷèyatakka*) (that draws us on a crooked path). एनः—पापवन्नु (*enaḥ—pāpavannu*) (sin). अस्मत्—नम्मिंद (*asmat—nammiṃda*) (from us). युयोधि—बेरॆ माडु (*yuyodhi—berè māḍu*) (remove). ते—निनगॆ (*te—ninagè*) (to you). भूयिष्ठां—अत्यधिकवागि (*bhūyiṣṭhāṃ—atyadhikavāgi*) (most abundantly). नमउक्तिं—नमस्कारोक्तियन्नु (*namauktiṃ—namaskāroktiyannu*) (the utterance of homage). विधेम—पठिसुवॆवु (*vidhema—paṭhisuvèvu*) (we shall recite).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O divine Agni, you who know all kinds of knowledge, lead us by the excellent way to obtain wealth in the form of heaven and the like. Remove from us the sin that draws us on a crooked path. We shall recite to you most abundant homage.

**Printed English translation**

Agni, knowing all kinds of knowledge, lead us by good ways to wealth, remove far from us the sin that would force us astry, that we may offer to you most ample adoration. [sic: "astry"]

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1)**

राये (*rāye*) — the word *rayi* is read among the names of water (नि. २-२४ (*ni. 2-24*)) and among the names of wealth (३-९ (*3-9*)). Besides, Yāska:

रयिरिति धननाम रातेर्दानकर्मणः (*rayiriti dhananāma rāterdānakarmaṇaḥ*) (नि. ४-१७ (*ni. 4-17*))

gives the sense "wealth" for the word *rayi*, explaining that the word is formed from the root *rā*, "to give, to make a gift", and has the sense wealth. In the present ṛk too the sense is the same.

देव (*deva*) — Yāska's Nirukta on the word *deva* is as follows:

देवो दानाद्वा, दीपनाद्वा, द्योतनाद्वा, द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा, यो देवः सा देवता (*devo dānādvā, dīpanādvā, dyotanādvā, dyusthāno bhavatīti vā, yo devaḥ sā devatā*) (नि. ७-१५ (*ni. 7-15*))

That is, this deity is named *deva* because he gives riches and the like (*dānāt*); because he lights up everything with his splendour (*dīpanāt*, *dyotanād vā*: the two words have the same sense); or because he dwells in the heavenly place (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 278

*Running head: [278 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189] (as supplied).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 of Sūkta 189, after the Nirukta note on *deva*.)*

...in heaven; therefore he is named *deva*: thus many senses are given for the word *deva*. Here the word *deva* is an epithet of the word *agne*, so all the explanations above fit.

वयुनानि (*vayunāni*) — the word *vayunam* is read among the ten names of praise, *asremāḥ*, *anemāḥ* and others, and among the eleven names of wisdom, *ketaḥ*, *ketuḥ* and others (नि. २-१३ (*ni. 2-13*)). Besides, Yāska on this word: वयुनं वेतेः कांतिर्वा प्रज्ञा वा (*vayunaṃ veteḥ kāṃtirvā prajñā vā*) (नि. ५-१५ (*ni. 5-15*)): the word *vayunam* is formed from the root *veti* and has the sense "brightness" or "wisdom"; and in support of this he gives as an example the ṛk

अहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुं ज्याया हेतिं परिबाधमानः । (*ahiriva bhogaiḥ paryeti bāhuṃ jyāyā hetiṃ paribādhamānaḥ |*)
हस्तघ्नो विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान् पुमान्सुमांसं परि पातु विश्वतः ॥ (*hastaghno viśvā vayunāni vidvān pumānsumāṃsaṃ pari pātu viśvataḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. ६-२५-१९) (*(ma. saṃ. 6-25-19)*)

where too *vayunāni* is explained as *prajñānāni*, "wisdoms".

नमउक्तिं (*namauktiṃ*) — नमस्कारोक्तिं । स्तुतिं (*namaskāroktiṃ | stutiṃ*): the sense is "we shall recite a hymn with homage".

*[As supplied, the label line reads व्याकरणक्रिया (*vyākaraṇakriyā*); standard label inserted.]*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 1, noted briefly)

नय (*naya*) (root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*)): *loṭ*, second person singular; by आमंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमनवत् (*āmaṃtritaṃ pūrvamavidyamanavat*) the preceding vocative *agne*, though present, counts as absent, so the *nighāta* accent does not occur; the stem-suffix *śap* being unaccented, the accent of the root remains. राये (*rāye*): the dative has come in the sense of the accusative by the statement सुपांसुपो भवंति (*supāṃsupo bhavaṃti*); by ऊडिदं पदादि— (*ūḍidaṃ padādi—*) (पा. सू. १-१७१ (*pā. sū. 1-171*), as printed) the ending is acute. वयुनानि (*vayunāni*) (root अज गतिक्षेपणयोः (*aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*)): by अजियमिशीज्भ्यश्च (*ajiyamiśījbhyaśca*) (उ. सू ३-४४१ (*u. sū 3-441*)) the suffix *unan*; by अजेव्यघञ्षपोः (*ajevyaghañṣapoḥ*) (पा. सू २-४-५६ (*pā. sū 2-4-56*)) the substitute *vī* for the root; on account of the suffix guṇa of its *ī*; the substitute *ay*; by *vyatyaya* the suffix has the first-syllable acute. युयोधि (*yuyodhi*): being at the beginning of the pāda, the *nighāta* accent does not occur; by the prescription that *hi* is unmarked-*p*, the acute comes, so the last syllable is acute. जुहुराणम् (*juhurāṇam*) (root हुर्छा कौटिल्ये (*hurchā kauṭilye*)): by हुर्छेःसनो लुक् छलोपश्च (*hurcheḥsano luk chalopaśca*) (उ. सू. २-२८४ (*u. sū. 2-284*)) the suffix *ānac* after the desiderative; *luk* of the desiderative; dropping of the root's *cha*

### Printed p. 279

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 279 (as supplied).*

(continued); by अट् कुप्वाज्— (*aṭ kupvāj—*) the suffix's *n* becomes *i*; the suffix being marked *c*, the last syllable is acute. नमउक्तिम् (*namauktim*): by तादौचनिति— (*tādaucaniti—*) (पा. सू. ६-२-५० (*pā. sū. 6-2-50*)) the preverb takes its natural accent. विधेम (*vidhema*) (root विध विधाने (*vidha vidhāne*)): *tudādi*, *liṅ*, first person plural; by शिज्जतिजः (*śijjatijaḥ*) (पा. सू. ८-१-२५ (*pā. sū. 8-1-25*), as printed) the *nighāta* accent.

> पूः । च । पृथ्वी । बहुला । नः । उर्वि । भव । तोकाय । तनयाय । शं । योः
> ॥ २ ॥

> *agne | tvaṃ | pāraya | navyaḥ | asmān | svastibhiḥ | ati | duḥgāni | viśvā |*
> *pūḥ | ca | pṛthvī | bahulā | naḥ | urvi | bhava | tokāya | tanayāya | śaṃ | yoḥ*

*[The supplied text repeats the line ॥ २ ॥ (*‖ 2 ‖*) once after the Pada; kept as a note. A line reading सहायधान्य, c (*sahāyadhānya, c*) stands inside the Pada block where the bhāṣya label belongs; standard label inserted.]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> आयुष्कामेष्ट्यामग्ने त्वं पारयेति द्वे स्विष्टकृतो याज्ये पाहि न इति
> चतुर्थ्यनुवाक्या । पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैरग्ने त्वं पारया नव्यो अस्मानिति
> संयाज्ये । आ. २-१० । इति सूत्रितं ॥ एते एव स्वस्त्रयन्यामपि संयाज्ये इति
> सूत्रितत्वात् ॥
> हे आग्ने त्वं नव्यो नवतरः स्तुत्यो वा त्वमस्मान्यागानुष्ठात्मनति पारय ।
> कर्म समापय्यातिपारय । अतिक्रामय । केन साधनेन । स्वस्तिभिः । अस्तिरभिपूजितः ।
> सुशब्दः शोभनवचनः । अत्यंतं पूजितैर्यज्ञादिसाधनैः । कानि । दुर्गाणि दुर्गमनानि
> पापानि । अनतिक्रमणीयानि दुरिताख्यान्यतिपारय । किंच नोऽस्माकं पृथ्वी पृथुतरा
> पूश्च पुर्यपि भवत्विति शेषः । चशब्दो वक्ष्यमाणेन सह समुच्चयार्थः । पूरिति
> जात्येकवचनं । पुराण्यपि भवंतित्यर्थः । तथा नोऽस्माकमुर्वि पृथ्व्यपि बहुतरा
> भवतु । त्वं तु तोकायापत्याय तनयाय पुत्राय । तोकशब्दोpपत्यसामान्य-
> वचनः । तनयशब्दः पुत्रवचनः । शं सुखं योर्मिश्रयिता भव । यद्वा । रोगाणां
> शमनं भयानां यावनं च भव । कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The first lines give the ritual use (Āśvalāyana: in the wish-for-long-life offering, two *sviṣṭakṛt* yājyā mantras; with *pāhi naḥ* as the fourth anuvākyā; and as saṃyājyā). Then: O Agni, adorable, take us across the hard-to-cross sins by the highly honoured sacrificial means; let our town and wide land be abundant; be the giver of happiness to our offspring, or the remover of disease and fear.

### Printed p. 280

*Running head: [280 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū 189] (as supplied).*

*[As supplied, the line १ प्रतिपदार्थ १ (*1 pratipadārtha 1*) with block marks stands where the Pratipadārtha label belongs; standard label inserted. The following lines carry block marks in the supplied text and are given as prose.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). नव्यः—स्तुत्यनागिद्दु (*navyaḥ—stutyanāgiddu*) (praiseworthy). आस्मान्—नम्मन्नु ! (*āsmān—nammannu !*) (us). स्वस्तिभिः—अत्यंत मंगळात्मकवाद यज्ञादिसाधनगळिंद (*svastibhiḥ—atyaṃta maṃgaḷātmakavāda yajñādisādhanagaḷiṃda*) (by the highly auspicious means such as sacrifice). दुर्गाणि — (साधारणवाद साधनगळिंद) दाटलु साध्यविल्लदिरुव पापगळिंद (*durgāṇi — (sādhāraṇavāda sādhanagaḷiṃda) dāṭalu sādhyavilladiruva pāpagaḷiṃda*) (from sins that cannot be crossed by ordinary means). अति पारय—दाटिसु (*ati pāraya—dāṭisu*) (take across). नः—नम्म (*naḥ—namma*) (our). पूः— पट्टणवु (*pūḥ— paṭṭaṇavu*) (town). पृथ्वी—अत्यंत विस्त्रतवादद्दागियू, उर्वी च—विस्त्रतवाद भूमियू कूड (*pṛthvī—atyaṃta vistratavādaddāgiyū, urvī ca—vistratavāda bhūmiyū kūḍa*) (very wide, and the wide earth too). बहुला—अधिकसंख्यातवागियू आगलि (*bahulā—adhikasaṃkhyātavāgiyū āgali*) (may it be abundant). तोकाय—नम्म प्रौत्रादिगळिगू (*tokāya—namma prautrādigaḷigū*) (to our grandchildren and the rest). तनयाय— पुत्ररिगू (*tanayāya— putrarigū*) (to our sons). शंयोः—सुखवन्नुंटुमाडुववनागि (*śaṃyoḥ—sukhavannuṃṭumāḍuvavanāgi*) (making happiness). अथवा शंयोः—रोगशमनवन्नू भय राहित्यवनू उंटुमाडुववनागि (*athavā śaṃyoḥ—rogaśamanavannū bhaya rāhityavanū uṃṭumāḍuvavanāgi*) (or: producing cure of disease and freedom from fear). भव—अगु (*bhava—agu*) (be).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भाषार्थ (*bhāṣārtha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, being praised, take us across the hard sins by the highly auspicious means such as sacrifice. May our town be very wide, and the wide earth abundant. For all our sons, grandsons and the rest, be a producer of cure of disease and freedom from fear.

**Printed English translation**

Adorable Agni, convey us by the sacred acts (of worship), beyond all evil ways : may our city be spacious ; our land be extensive ; be the bestower of happiness upon our offspring, upon our sons (the print ends without a full stop at "sons")

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषयगळु: (*viśeṣayagaḷu:*), run on after the printed English; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 2)**

This ṛk अग्ने त्वं पाराय (*agne tvaṃ pārāya*) and the next ṛk are to be recited as *yājyā* mantras at the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering in the offering for one desiring long life, and the fourth ṛk of this sūkta, पाहिनो अग्ने (*pāhino agne*), as a *puronuvākyā* mantra, according to the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra rule पाहिनो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैरग्ने त्वं पाराया नव्यो अस्मानिति संयाज्ये (*pāhino agne pāyubhirajasrairagne tvaṃ pārāyā navyo asmāniti saṃyājye*); and it is said there that in the *svastyayana* too these ṛks are to be recited as *yājyā* mantras (आ. २-१० (*ā. 2-10*)).

नव्य: (*navya:*) — नवतरः स्तुत्यो वा (*navataraḥ stutyo vā*). For the word *navya* Yāska's explanation is "newer" (नि. ६-९ (*ni. 6-9*)). In many places it is described that when kindling-sticks and the like are put into Agni he grows and is ever new. Sāyaṇa adds the sense स्तुत्यः (*stutyaḥ*), "praised". The word *navya* is used of Agni in many ṛks (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window).

### Printed p. 281

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 281 (as supplied).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 of Sūkta 189.)*

स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*) — अस्तिरभिपूजितः । सुशब्दः शोभनवचनः । अत्यंतं पूजितैर्यज्ञादि साधनैः (*astirabhipūjitaḥ | suśabdaḥ śobhanavacanaḥ | atyaṃtaṃ pūjitairyajñādi sādhanaiḥ*): that is, by the worshipful means such as sacrifice. Yāska's explanation is स्वस्तित्यविनाशिनाम । अस्तिरभि पूजतः सु अस्तीति (*svastityavināśināma | astirabhi pūjataḥ su astīti*) (नि. ३-२१ (*ni. 3-21*)): *svasti* is a name of the imperishable; *asti* is "honoured", *su asti*: that which has no destruction and therefore is worthy of worship. The prefix *su* also conveys the senses "very", "good", "beautiful".

पूः (*pūḥ*) — a city, the town in which we live. The bhāṣyakāra has said that this word is a singular of the class (*jātyekavacana*): although a singular is used, it can be given a plural sense. बहुला (*bahulā*) — *bahutarā*: the sense is that it should provide many kinds of happiness and wealth, sons and grandsons.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 2, noted briefly)

पारय (*pāraya*) (root पार तीरसमाप्ति (*pāra tīrasamāpti*)): *loṭ* after the causative, second person singular; owing to the connection with a finite verb the *nighāta* accent. दुर्गाणि (*durgāṇi*) (root गम्‌ल्य गत् (*gamlya gat*)): by सुदुरोरधिकरणे (*suduroradhikaraṇe*) the suffix *ḍa*; because of the *ḍ*-marking the *ṭi* of the root is dropped; the accent of the first member of the *kṛt* compound. विश्वा (*viśvā*): by शेष्वंदसि बहुलम् (*śeṣvaṃdasi bahulam*) (पा. सू. ६-१-७० (*pā. sū. 6-1-70*), as printed) the *śi* is dropped. पृथ्वी (*pṛthvī*): being read in the *gaurādi* group, the suffix *ṅīṣ*; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. भवा (*bhavā*) (root भू सत्तायां (*bhū sattāyāṃ*)): *loṭ*, second person singular; being at the beginning of the pāda the *nighāta* accent does not occur and the accent of the root remains; by द्वचोतस्तिजः (*dvacotastijaḥ*) (पा. सू. ६-३-१३५ (*pā. sū. 6-3-135*)) lengthening in the Saṃhitā. तनयाय (*tanayāya*) (root तनु विस्तारे (*tanu vistāre*)): by वलिमलितनिभ्यःकयन् (*valimalitanibhyaḥkayan*) (उ. सू ४-५३९ (*u. sū 4-539*)) the suffix *kayan*; the suffix being marked *n*, by इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) the first syllable is acute.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वममीवा रोगानस्मदस्मत्तो युयोधि । व्यावर्तये । या
> अनग्नित्रा अग्निनापालिताः कृष्टीः प्रजा अभ्यमंत आभिमिमतेऽस्मान् ॥ यच्छब्दाध्या-
> हारादनिघातः ॥ ता युयोधि । यद्वा । ता अनग्नित्राः पापिन्यः कृष्टयः प्रजा अभ्य-
> मंत । त्वयाभ्यमितुमभितो रोगैः प्रापयितुमर्हंति । वयं तु न तादृशाः ।
> अतोऽस्मत्तो वियोजयेत्यर्थः । न केवलं वियोगमात्रं अपि तु पुनःपुनरिदं
> कर्तव्यं । अस्मभ्यमस्मदर्थं सुविताय शोभनफलाय हे यजत्र यष्टव्य देव
> द्योतमानाग्ने विश्वेभिरमृतेभिः सर्वरमरणधर्मभिरन्यैर्यष्टव्यर्देवैः सह क्षां
> पृथिवीं देवयजनलक्षणामागच्छेति शेषः ॥

*Gist:* O Agni, remove from us diseases and the sinful people, unprotected by Agni, who press upon us; and, O adorable god, come with all the other immortal gods to the earth, the sacrificial ground, for our good.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). त्वं—नीनु (*tvaṃ—nīnu*) (you). अमीवाः—रोगगळन्नू(मत्तु) (*amīvāḥ—rogagaḷannū(mattu)*) (diseases, and). अनग्नित्राः— अग्नियिंद अरक्षितरादवरू (*anagnitrāḥ— agniyiṃda arakṣitarādavarū*) (those unprotected by Agni). याः कृष्टीः—नम्म शत्रुरूपरू आद याव प्रजॆगळु (*yāḥ kṛṣṭīḥ—namma śatrurūparū āda yāva prajègaḷu*) (which people, in the form of our enemies). अभ्यमंत- नम्मन्नु प्रतिभटिसि द्वेषिसुत्तारॆयो, अवरन्नू (*abhyamaṃta- nammannu pratibhaṭisi dveṣisuttārèyo, avarannū*) (who oppose and hate us, them too). पुनः—पदे पदे (*punaḥ—pade pade*) (again and again). अस्मत्—नम्मिंद (*asmat—nammiṃda*) (from us). युयोधि—दूरमाडि नाशपडिसु (*yuyodhi—dūramāḍi nāśapaḍisu*) (remove and destroy). अस्मभ्यं—नमगॆ (*asmabhyaṃ—namagè*) (for us). सुविताय—श्रेष्ठवाद फलवन्नु ऒदगिसुवुदक्कागि (*suvitāya—śreṣṭhavāda phalavannu òdagisuvudakkāgi*) (to provide excellent fruit). यजत्र—यज्ञार्हनू (*yajatra—yajñārhanū*) (worthy of sacrifice). देव—प्रकाशमाननू आद अग्निये ! (*deva—prakāśamānanū āda agniye !*) (shining Agni). विश्वेभिर- मृतेभिः—मरणधर्मरहितराद सकल देवतॆगळॊडनॆयू (*viśvebhira- mṛtebhiḥ—maraṇadharmarahitarāda sakala devatègaḷòḍanèyū*) (with all the immortal gods). क्षां—यज्ञभूमिगॆ दयमाडु (*kṣāṃ—yajñabhūmigè dayamāḍu*) (come to the sacrificial ground).

*[As supplied, the label line reads भःवार्ध (*bhaḥvārdha*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, remove and destroy from us again and again our diseases and the enemies who, unprotected by you, harass us. To provide us with excellent fruit, O worshipful, shining Agni, come to the sacrificial ground with all the immortal gods.

*[As supplied, the label line reads English Translatin (*English Translatin*); standard label inserted.]*

**Printed English translation**

Agni, remove from us disease, and those men who, unprotected by Agni, are adverse to us ; and, adorable divinity, (visit) the earth, with the all immortals, rfo our welfare. [sic: "rfo"]

### Printed p. 283

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Adhyāya 5. Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 283 (as supplied).*

*[The supplied text has no Special Topics label before the next line; standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 3)**

अमीवाः (*amīvāḥ*) — diseases. This word, formed from the root अम रोगॆ (*ama rogè*) (*curādi*, *parasmaipada*), indicates disease or injury. Yāska, citing the ṛk

यस्ते गर्भममीवा दुर्णामा योनिमाशये । (*yaste garbhamamīvā durṇāmā yonimāśaye |*)
अग्निष्टं ब्रह्मणा सह निष्क्रव्यादमनीनशत् ॥ (*agniṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā saha niṣkravyādamanīnaśat ‖*)
(ऋ. सं. १०-१६२-२) (*(ṛ. saṃ. 10-162-2)*)

gives for the word *amīvā* in it the sense रोगभूतः (*rogabhūtaḥ*), "diseased" (नि. ६-१२ (*ni. 6-12*)).

अनग्नित्राः (*anagnitrāḥ*) — those not protected by Agni, that is, those who do sinful acts, demons.

अमृतेभिः (*amṛtebhiḥ*) — अमरणधर्मभिरन्यैर्यष्टवैर्दैवैः (*amaraṇadharmabhiranyairyaṣṭavairdaivaiḥ*): by the other worshipful gods free from death.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 3, noted briefly)

अनग्नित्रा (*anagnitrā*): अग्निना त्राताः अग्नित्राः न अग्नित्राः अनग्नित्राः (*agninā trātāḥ agnitrāḥ na agnitrāḥ anagnitrāḥ*); by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ— (*tatpuruṣe tulyārtha—*) (पा. सू. ६-२-२ (*pā. sū. 6-2-2*)) the first member *nañ* keeps its natural accent. अमंत (*amaṃta*) (root माज् माने शब्दे च (*māj māne śabde ca*)): in the Vedic manner *laṅ* in the present sense; by *vyatyaya* *luk* of the stem-suffix; third person plural; since *yat* is understood, by यद्व- त्तान्नित्यम् (*yadva- ttānnityam*) the *nighāta* accent is prohibited; since the augment *aṭ* is acute, the first syllable is acute. कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*) (root कृष विलेखने (*kṛṣa vilekhane*)): by क्तिच् कौच संज्ञायाम् (*ktic kauca saṃjñāyām*) (पा सू ३-३-१७४ (*pā sū 3-3-174*)) the suffix *ktic*; on account of the connection with *ṣ*, retroflex *ṭ*; being marked *c*, the last syllable is acute. सुविताय (*suvitāya*): सुष्टु इतः सुवितः (*suṣṭu itaḥ suvitaḥ*), root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*); the suffix *kta*; by तन्नादीनां छंदसि बहुलमुपसंख्यानम् (*tannādīnāṃ chaṃdasi bahulamupasaṃkhyānam*) (पा. सू. ६-४-७७-१ (*pā. sū. 6-4-77-1*), as printed) *uva* for the *u*; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. अमृतेभिः (*amṛtebhiḥ*): by नञतो जरमर— (*nañato jaramara—*) (पा. सू. ६-२-११६ (*pā. sū. 6-2-116*)) the first syllable of the final member is acute; in the Vedic usage the *bhis* ending optionally takes *ais*, so by बहुवचनेझल्येत् (*bahuvacanejhalyet*) it takes *e*. यजत्र (*yajatra*): root यज देवपूजादिषु (*yaja devapūjādiṣu*); by अमिनक्षियजि— (*aminakṣiyaji—*) (उ सू. ३-३८४ (*u sū. 3-384*)) the suffix *atran*; in the vocative, by आमंत्रितस्यच (*āmaṃtritasyaca*) the *nighāta* accent.

#### Ṛk 4

*[As supplied, the label line of the Saṃhitā reads संवादादि (*saṃvādādi*) and that of the Pada पडॆदार् (*paḍèdār*); standard labels inserted.]*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पा॒हि नो॑ अग्ने पा॒युभि॒रज॑स्रैरु॒त प्रि॒ये सद॑न॒ आ शु॑शु॒
> क्वान् ।
> मा ते॑ भ॒यं ज॑रि॒तारं॑ यविष्ठ नू॒नं वि॑द॒न्माप॒रं स॑हस्वः
> ॥ ४ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पाहि । नः । अग्ने । पायुभिः । अजस्रैः । उत । प्रिये । सदने । आ । शुशुक्वान् ।
> मा । ते । भयं । जरितारं । यविष्ठ । नूनं । विदत् । मा । अपरं । सहस्वः ॥ ४ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> पाहि न इत्यस्या विनियोगद्वयमग्ने त्वं पारयेत्यत्रोक्तं ॥ तथाग्नेय-
> पशावेषैव हविषोऽनुवाक्या । तथा च सूत्रितं । पाहि नो आग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैः
> प्र वः शुक्राय भानवे भरध्वं । आ ३-७ । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने नोऽस्मानजस्रैरनवरतैरविच्छिन्नैः पायुभिः पालनप्रकारैः पाहि ।
> पालय । उतापि च प्रिये सदने तव प्रियभूते यागगृह आ सर्वतः शुशुक्वान्
> दीप्यमानो भवेति शेषः । किंच हे यविष्ठ युवतम ते तव जरितारं गरितारं
> स्तोतारं मां नूनमद्य भयं मा विदत् । मा लभतां । माप्पोतु । हे सहस्वो
> बलवन्नग्ने अपरमपरस्मिन्काले भयं मा विदत् । अपरं मदन्यं वा मा विदत् ॥

*Gist:* Two ritual uses are stated (see the Ṛk 1 note), and the verse is the animal-offering anuvākyā. O Agni, protect us by unbroken protections; blaze all round in your dear sacrificial house; may fear not find me, your singer, now or at any later time, O youngest and mighty one.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—अग्निये (*agne—agniye*) (O Agni). नः—नम्मन्नु (*naḥ—nammannu*) (us). अजस्रैः—अनवरतवादुदू अविच्छिन्नवादुदू आद (*ajasraiḥ—anavaratavādudū avicchinnavādudū āda*) (unbroken, uninterrupted). पायुभिः—रक्षणाक्रमगळिंद (*pāyubhiḥ—rakṣaṇākramagaḷiṃda*) (by means of protection). पाहि—रक्षिसु (*pāhi—rakṣisu*) (protect). उत—मत्तु (*uta—mattu*) (and). प्रिये सदने—निनगॆ प्रीति पात्रवाद यज्ञगृहदल्लि (*priye sadane—ninagè prīti pātravāda yajñagṛhadalli*) (in the sacrificial house dear to you). आ—सुत्तलू (*ā—suttalū*) (all round). शुशुक्वान्—प्रकाशिसु (*śuśukvān—prakāśisu*) (shine). यविष्ठ—अत्यंत युवक नाद ऎलै अग्निये (*yaviṣṭha—atyaṃta yuvaka nāda èlai agniye*) (O youngest Agni). ते—निन्न (*te—ninna*) (your). जरितारं—स्तोतृवाद नन्नन्नु (*jaritāraṃ—stotṛvāda nannannu*) (me, your singer). नूनं—ईग (*nūnaṃ—īga*) (now). भयं— भयवु (*bhayaṃ— bhayavu*) (fear). मा विदत्—समीपिसदंतागलि (*mā vidat—samīpisadaṃtāgali*) (let it not approach). सहस्वः—बलशालियाद ऎलै अग्निये,  (*sahasvaḥ—balaśāliyāda èlai agniye, *)(O mighty Agni). अपरं— बेरॆकालदल्लियू सह (*aparaṃ— berèkāladalliyū saha*) (at another time too). मा—नन्नन्नु भयवु समीपिसदिरलि.  (*mā—nannannu bhayavu samīpisadirali. *)(let fear not approach me).

**Bhāvārtha** (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window)

O youngest Agni, protect us by unbroken and uninterrupted means of protection, and blaze all round in the sacrificial house dear to you. O mighty (the supplied text breaks off here).

### Printed p. 285

*Running head: [ಅ. ಅ.ವ ೫. ವ ೧೦] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 285 (as supplied, as printed).*

*(Continuation of the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 4 of Sūkta 189, which broke off at the end of the previous window with the words "O mighty…".)*

...O mighty Agni, let there be no fear at all for me, your singer, either at this time of the sacrifice or at any other time.

**Printed English translation**

Cherish us, Agni, with incessant bounties ; shine always in your favourite abode : let no danger, youngest (of the gods), assail your worshipper to-day ; nor, mighty one, let it assault him at any other season.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 4)**

पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*) — पालनप्रकारैः (*pālanaprakāraiḥ*), by modes of protection. In this ṛk the use of the word पाहि (*pāhi*) indicates the act of protection; is not then the use of the word *pāyubhiḥ*, which has the same sense, in vain? The answer: there are many kinds of protection. The word अजस्रैः (*ajasraiḥ*) indicates that in some circumstances the protection must be continual, with no break; and that protection may be of many kinds: protecting us from harm by enemies and wild beasts; from the fear of fire, water and the like; from diseases and other afflictions; protecting by giving food and the like so that we do not die afflicted by hunger. The word *pāyubhiḥ* is used to indicate such many kinds of means of protection.

मा (*mā*) — here the word *mā* indicates prohibition; the sense is "let it not arise".

जरितारं (*jaritāraṃ*) — स्तोतारं मां (*stotāraṃ māṃ*), "me, the praiser". There is the Nirukta statement जरतेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (*jarateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ*) (नि. १०-८ (*ni. 10-8*)).

नूनं (*nūnaṃ*) — for this word Yāska says:

नूनमिति विचिकित्सार्थीयो भाषायामुभयमन्वध्यायं विचिकित्सार्थीयश्च पदपूरणश्च (*nūnamiti vicikitsārthīyo bhāṣāyāmubhayamanvadhyāyaṃ vicikitsārthīyaśca padapūraṇaśca*)

That is, they describe the word *nūnam* as used in the sense of doubt (*vicikitsā*) elsewhere than in the metrical texts, and in the sense of doubt and as a mere filler of the pāda in the metrical texts. Durgācārya (the print has "ದುರ್ಗಾಚಾರರು") explains: विचिकित्सानाम विवेकपूर्वको अवधारणाभिप्रायः (*vicikitsānāma vivekapūrvako avadhāraṇābhiprāyaḥ*), that *vicikitsā* is settling a point by reasoning in circumstances where there is doubt. In this ṛk the bhāṣyakāra explains the word *nūnam* as "now".

यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*) — *yuvatama*, the best of the young. Since Agni, always kindled and blazing with kindling-sticks, ghee and the like, it is customary to address him as young:

अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविगृहपतियुर्वा । हव्यवाड्जु ह्यास्यः ॥ (*agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavigṛhapatiyurvā | havyavāḍju hyāsyaḥ ‖*)
(म. सं. १-१२-६) (*(ma. saṃ. 1-12-6)*)

in this and other ṛks Agni is described by the word *yuvā*. The word is used also of other deities.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 4, noted briefly)

पाहि (*pāhi*) (root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*)): *loṭ*, second person singular; being at the beginning of the pāda, the *nighāta* accent does not occur; by the prescription that *hi* is unmarked-*p* it becomes acute. पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*): the same root; by कृवापा— (*kṛvāpā—*) (उ. सू. १-१ (*u. sū. 1-1*)) the suffix *uṇ*; by आतोयुक् चिण् कृतोः (*ātoyuk ciṇ kṛtoḥ*) the augment *yuk*; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute. शुशुक्वान् (*śuśukvān*) (root शुच दीप्ति (*śuca dīpti*)): when *liṭ* comes, by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*) the substitute *kvasu*; on that basis reduplication of the root; by *vyatyaya* the root's *c* becomes a velar; by the suffix accent the vowel after *v* is acute. जरितारम् (*jaritāram*): since roots have many meanings, the root ज्यष् (*jyaṣ*) (as printed) is used here in the sense of praise; the suffix *tṛc* in the agent sense; the augment *iṭ*; guṇa of the root's *ṛ* and *r* following; the suffix being marked *c*, the last syllable is acute. यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*): अशतियेन युवा (*aśatiyena yuvā*) (as printed); by अतिशायनेतमबिष्ठन् (*atiśāyanetamabiṣṭhan*) (पा. सू. ५-३-५५ (*pā. sū. 5-3-55*)) the suffix *iṣṭhan*; by स्कूलदूर— (*skūladūra—*) (पा. सू. ६-४-१५६ (*pā. sū. 6-4-156*)) *van* is dropped; guṇa of the *u*; the substitute *av*; in the vocative the vocative *nighāta* accent. विदत् (*vidat*) (root विद्‌ल्य लाभे (*vidlya lābhe*)): by माजिलुज् (*mājiluj*) (पा. सू. ३-३-१७५ (*pā. sū. 3-3-175*)) when *māṅ* is in the compound, *luṅ* in the third person singular with *tip*; by इतत्व (*itatva*) the final *i* of it is dropped; because it is marked *l*, by पुषादिद्युतादि— (*puṣādidyutādi—*) (पा. सू ३-१-५५ (*pā. sū 3-1-55*)) the substitute *aṅ* for *cli*; because it is marked *ṅ*, the guṇa of the penultimate does not occur; by नमाज् योगे (*namāj yoge*) (पा. सू. ६-४-७४ (*pā. sū. 6-4-74*)) the augment *aṭ* does not occur; owing to the connection with a finite verb the *nighāta* accent. सहस्व (*sahasva*): by मतुवसोरुः संबुद्धौ (*matuvasoruḥ saṃbuddhau*) (पा. सू. ८-३-१ (*pā. sū. 8-3-1*)) *ru* in the vocative; by आमंतित्रस्य च (*āmaṃtitrasya ca*) (as printed) the *nighāta* accent.

*Gist:* The first lines give the ritual use (Āśvalāyana Gṛhya: the oblation to Agni with this ṛk in the one-potsherd cake offering). Then: O Agni, do not give us over to the harmful, hungry, evil-doing enemy, nor to biting serpents and the like, nor to animals that hurt with horns, nor to any hurtful thief or demon; O mighty one, never give us up.

**Pratipadārtha** (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the window)

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). नः—नम्मन्नु (*naḥ—nammannu*) (us). अघाय—हिंसकनू (पापिष्ठनू) (*aghāya—hiṃsakanū (pāpiṣṭhanū)*) (to the harmful, sinful). अविष्यवे- हॊट्टॆबाकनू (*aviṣyave- hòṭṭèbākanū*) (to the glutton). दुच्चुनाय्कॆ—दुःखकारियू आद (*duccunāykè—duḥkhakāriyū āda*) (to the doer of harm). रिपवे—शत्रुविगॆ (*ripave—śatruvigè*) (to the enemy). मा अव सृजः— बिट्टुकॊट्टु (नम्मन्नु अवन) अधीनरन्नागि माडबेड (*mā ava sṛjaḥ— biṭṭukòṭṭu (nammannu avana) adhīnarannāgi māḍabeḍa*) (do not give us over and make us subject to him). दत्वते—दंतादिगळिरुवुवू (*datvate—daṃtādigaḷiruvuvū*) (to those with teeth and the like). दशते— कच्चतक्कवू अद सर्पादिगळिगू (*daśate— kaccatakkavū ada sarpādigaḷigū*) (to biting serpents and the like). मा—सिक्कि नरळुवंतॆ माडबेड (*mā—sikki naraḷuvaṃtè māḍabeḍa*) (do not let us fall into their grip and suffer). नः—नम्मन्नु (*naḥ—nammannu*) (us). अदते— दंतविल्लदे (कॊंबु मुंताद साधनगळिंद) हिंसिसुव प्राणिगळिगू (*adate— daṃtavillade (kòṃbu muṃtāda sādhanagaḷiṃda) hiṃsisuva prāṇigaḷigū*) (to animals that hurt without teeth, with horns and the like). मा—सिक्किस बेड (हागॆये) (*mā—sikkisa beḍa (hāgèye)*) (do not give us over; likewise). रिषते—हिंसॆमाडतक्क इतर प्राणिगू बिट्टुकॊडबेड (*riṣate—hiṃsèmāḍatakka itara prāṇigū biṭṭukòḍabeḍa*) (do not give us up to any other hurting creature). सहसावन्—बलशालियाद ऎलै अग्निये (*sahasāvan—balaśāliyāda èlai agniye*) (O mighty Agni). मा परा दाः—नन्नन्नु अपजयक्कू अवमानक्कू ईडुमाडबेड (*mā parā dāḥ—nannannu apajayakkū avamānakkū īḍumāḍabeḍa*) (do not expose me to defeat and humiliation).

### Printed p. 288

*Running head: [288 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189] (as supplied).*

**Bhāvārtha** (Ṛk 5; the Pratipadārtha ended on p. 287)

O mighty Agni, do not give us over to the enemy who is harmful, voracious and a causer of sorrow, and do not make us subject to him. Likewise do not let us fall to creatures that bite with teeth and the like, or that hurt without teeth with horns and the like. Do not make us fit objects of defeat and humiliation.

**Printed English translation**

Abandon us not, Agni, to a wicked, voracious, malevolent foe; (abandon us) not to one who bas fangs, and who bites ; nor to one without teeth ; nor to the malignant ; nor give us up, powerful Agni, to disgrace. [sic: "bas"]

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 5)**

अघाय (*aghāya*) — हिंसकाय (*hiṃsakāya*). The word *agha*, formed from the root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*) with the preverb आज् (*āj*), means one who injures, a wicked person. The word *riṣate* has the same sense. Here *aghāya*, *aviṣyave*, *ripave* and the like are in the dative singular, and the prayer is: do not hand us over to the harmful; that is, protect us so that we do not fall into the hands of a harmful one.

अविष्यवे (*aviṣyave*) — अविष्यतिरत्तिकर्मा । अन्नेच्छवे (*aviṣyatirattikarmā | annecchave*): to one who eats too much, that is, to demons and the like.

दुच्चुनाय्कॆ (*duccunāykè*) — since the word *śuna* is read among the twenty names of happiness (नि. ३-१३ (*ni. 3-13*)), *śuna* means happiness. दुष्टसुखकारिणे दुःखकारिण इत्यर्थः (*duṣṭasukhakāriṇe duḥkhakāriṇa ityarthaḥ*): the sense is one who destroys such happiness and causes sorrow.

दत्वते (*datvate*) — दंतवते (*daṃtavate*): wicked creatures with teeth (the print says "ಹುಲ್ಲುಗಳುಳ್ಳ", as supplied); they bite men with their sharp teeth.

दशते (*daśate*) — serpents and the like that bite with venomous fangs. Though the teeth of poisonous creatures are not frightful, the poison enters the body at the bite and causes death, so serpents and the like are dangerous.

अदतॆ (*adatè*) — wicked creatures without teeth; that is, some animals whose teeth are not frightful nevertheless harm men with horns, hooves and the like. Wild buffaloes, bulls and others harm people with their horns, and donkeys, horses and others with their hooves. The prayer is that we be protected from such various wicked creatures.

### Printed p. 289

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2. Ā. 5. Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 289 (as supplied).*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page for Ṛk 5, noted briefly)

सृजः (*sṛjaḥ*) (root स्रज विसर्गे (*sraja visarge*), as printed, *tudādi*): when *māṅ* is in the compound, *laṅ*, second person singular; because of the connection with *māṅ* the augment *aṭ* does not occur; owing to the connection with a finite verb the *nighāta* accent. अविष्यवे (*aviṣyave*): by सनाशंसभीक्षउः (*sanāśaṃsabhīkṣauḥ*) the suffix *u* after the desiderative stem *aviṣya*; by आतोलोपः (*ātolopaḥ*) (पा. सू ६-४-४८ (*pā. sū 6-4-48*)) the preceding *a* is dropped; by the suffix accent the last syllable is acute; dative singular. दुच्चुनाय्कॆ (*duccunāykè*): दुष्टं शुनं यस्य सः (*duṣṭaṃ śunaṃ yasya saḥ*); the change of gender is by *vyatyaya*; by परादिश्चंदसि बहुलम् (*parādiścaṃdasi bahulam*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१९९ (*pā. sū. 6-1-199*)) the first syllable of the final member is acute. दत्वते (*datvate*): दंताः अस्य संति इति तद्वान् (*daṃtāḥ asya saṃti iti tadvān*); the substitute *dat* for *danta*; by the statement स्वर विधौव्यंजन- मविद्यमानवत् (*svara vidhauvyaṃjana- mavidyamānavat*) the intervening *t* counts as absent, so by ह्रस्वनुड्ड्यां- मतुप् (*hrasvanuḍḍyāṃ- matup*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१७६ (*pā. sū. 6-1-176*)) the suffix *matup* is acute; dative singular. दशते (*daśate*) (root दंश दशने (*daṃśa daśane*)): the participle for *laṭ*; the stem-suffix *śap*; by दंशसंज स्वंजां शपि (*daṃśasaṃja svaṃjāṃ śapi*) (पा सू. ६-४-२५ (*pā sū. 6-4-25*)) the nasal of the root is dropped; by तास्यनुदात्तेत्— (*tāsyanudāttet—*) (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६ (*pā. sū. 6-1-186*)) the *lasārvadhātuka* ending is unaccented, so the accent of the root remains. रिषते (*riṣate*) (root रिष हिंसायां (*riṣa hiṃsāyāṃ*)): the participle for *laṭ*; by the statement संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः (*saṃjñāpūrvako vidhiranityaḥ*) guṇa of the penultimate does not occur; as before the accent of the root remains. दाः (*dāḥ*) (root डुदाज् दाने (*ḍudāj dāne*), as printed): *luṅ* because of the connection with *māṅ*, second person singular; because of the connection with *māṅ* the augment *aṭ* does not occur; the verb-*nighāta* accent (the print has "ತಿಜಿಂತಸಿಘಾತ", as supplied).

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वि घ॒ त्वावा॑ ऋतजात यंसद्गृणा॒नो अ॑ग्ने ॒नॆत्वे॒३॒॑ऽवरू॑थं ।
> विश्वा॑द्रिरि॒क्षोरु॒त वा॑ निनि॒त्सोर॑भि॒ह्रुता॒मसि॒ हि दे॑व वि॒ष्पट्
> ॥ ६ ॥
