*[As supplied, the label line of the Pratipadārtha reads प्रतिपद-र्थ (*pratipada-rtha*), inside the bhāṣya block, and its lines carry the quote marks of the block; the label is replaced by the standard label and the lines are un-quoted.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अस्य—ई अग्निगॆ (*asya—ī agnigè*) (of him, Agni). धृतं—आज्यवु (*dhṛtaṃ—ājyavu*) (ghee (printed with a different first letter)). योनिः—उत्पत्ति कारणवु (आदुदरिंद) (*yoniḥ—utpatti kāraṇavu (ādudariṃda)*) (the origin, the cause (therefore)). धृतं— आज्यवन्नु (*dhṛtaṃ— ājyavannu*) (ghee). मिमिक्षे—प्रोक्षिसुत्तेनॆ (*mimikṣe—prokṣisuttenè*) (I sprinkle). धृते—धृतदल्लि (*dhṛte—dhṛtadalli*) (in ghee (printed as in the Pratipadārtha)). श्रितः—(अग्नियु) आश्रयवन्नु पडॆ दिद्दानॆ (*śritaḥ—(agniyu) āśrayavannu paḍè diddānè*) (he has taken refuge (Agni)). अस्य.—ई अग्निगॆ (*asya.—ī agnigè*) (of him, Agni (printed with a full stop after the word)). धृतमु—धृतवे (*dhṛtamu—dhṛtave*) (ghee itself (printed with a different ending)). धाम—तेजस्सिन आधारवु (*dhāma—tejassina ādhāravu*) (the support of lustre). वृषभ—फलगळन्नु सुरिसतक्क ऎलै अग्निये (*vṛṣabha—phalagaḷannu surisatakka èlai agniye*) (O showering Agni, who pours out fruits). अनुष्वधं—अर्पिसिद ऎल्ला हविस्सुगळिगागियू (*anuṣvadhaṃ—arpisida èllā havissugaḷigāgiyū*) (for all the oblations offered). आ वह—देवतॆगळन्नु करॆदुकॊंडु बा (*ā vaha—devatègaḷannu karèdukòṃḍu bā*) (bring the gods). मादयस्व—अवरन्नु तृप्तिगॊळिसु (*mādayasva—avarannu tṛptigòḷisu*) (gratify them). स्वाहाकृतं—स्वाहाकारपूर्वकवागि अर्पिसिद (*svāhākṛtaṃ—svāhākārapūrvakavāgi arpisida*) (offered with the svāhā-call). हव्यं—हविस्सन्नु (*havyaṃ—havissannu*) (the oblation). वक्षि—वहिसु. (*vakṣi—vahisu.*) (carry).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Ghee is the origin of this Agni; he has taken refuge in ghee alone; therefore I sprinkle the ghee. Ghee is the support of this Agni's lustre. O showering Agni, bring the gods to all the oblations offered, gratify them, and carry the oblation offered with the svāhā-call.

**Printed English translation**

I sprinkle the butter, for butter is his birth-place, he is nourished by butter ; butter is his radiance ; Agni, showerer (of benefits), bring the gods to the offered oblation ; exhilarate them ; convey to them the offering that has been reverently sanotified [sic].

*(The printed English reads "sanotified" [sic] for "sanctified".)*

#### Sūkta 4 (Maṇḍala 2)

नाल्कनॆय सूक्तवु (*nālkanèya sūktavu*) ("the fourth sūkta").

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (introduction)

> हुवे व इति नवर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं । भार्गवः सोमाहुतिनामक ऋषि: ।
> अग्निर्देवता । त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । हुवे नव सोमाहुतिर्भार्गवो हेत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥
> प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोस्त्रैष्टुभे छंदसीदं । सूत्रितं च । हुवे वः सुद्योत्मानं
> नि होता होतृषदन इति सूक्ते ॥ आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

*Gist:* The fourth sūkta has nine ṛks, seer Somāhuti Bhārgava, deity Agni, Triṣṭubh metre; used in the morning litany and Āśvina śastra.

*[In the supplied text the Anuvāda, the heading lines and the Saṃhitā of Ṛk 1 stand inside the quoted block of the bhāṣya, with garbled labels; the Anuvāda and heading lines are moved out of the block and un-quoted, nothing being dropped.]*

**Anuvāda (Kannada)** of Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 4 of Maṇḍala 2. This sūkta beginning हुवे वः (*huve vaḥ*) is the fourth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. Somāhuti, born in the family of Bhṛgu, is the seer of this sūkta; Agni is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: हुवे नव सोमाहुतिर्भार्गवो ह (*huve nava somāhutirbhārgavo ha*) (a line-end hyphen is joined). That this sūkta is used for the Triṣṭubh-metre mantras at the time of reciting the morning anuvāka and the Āśvina śastra mantras is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra हुवे वः सुद्योत्तानं नि होता होतृषदन इति सूक्ते (*huve vaḥ sudyottānaṃ ni hotā hotṛṣadana iti sūkte*) (आ. ४-१३ (*ā. 4-13*)).

**Sūkta 4 — heading lines (printed as plain lines)**

सूक्त—४ (*sūkta—4*)
॥ मंडल—२ ॥ अनुवाक— १॥ सूक्त—४ ॥ (*‖ maṃḍala—2 ‖ anuvāka— 1‖ sūkta—4 ‖*)
॥ अष्टक— २ ॥ अध्याय— ५ ॥ वर्ग- २४, २५ ॥ (*‖ aṣṭaka— 2 ‖ adhyāya— 5 ‖ varga- 24, 25 ‖*)
' सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ.- ९ । (*' sūktadalliruva ṛksaṃkhyè.- 9 |*)
ऋषिः—सोमाहुतिर्भार्गवः । (*ṛṣiḥ—somāhutirbhārgavaḥ |*)
देवता—अग्निः ॥ (*devatā—agniḥ ‖*)
छंदः—त्रिष्टुप् । (*chaṃdaḥ—triṣṭup |*)

(Sense: sūkta 4; maṇḍala 2, anuvāka 1, sūkta 4; aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 5, varga 24, 25; the number of ṛks in the sūkta, nine; seer Somāhuti Bhārgava; deity Agni; metre Triṣṭubh.)

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> हुवे । वः । सुद्योत्मानं । सुवृक्तिं । विशां । अग्निं । अतिथिं । सुप्रयसं ।
> मित्रः इव । यः । दिधिषाय्यः । भूत् । देवः । आदेवे । जने । जातवेदाः ii १ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे यजमाना वो युष्मदर्थमग्निं हुवे । आह्वयामि । कीदृशं तं ।
> सुद्योत्मानं सुष्टु द्योतमानं । सुवृक्तिं सुवर्जितं पापैः शोभनस्तुतिं वा ।
> विशां यजमानानामतिथिवत्सदा पूज्यं । सुप्रयसं शोभनहनिर्लक्षणान्नं । किंच
> जातवेदा जातानां वेदिता यो देवोऽग्निर्मित्र इव सखेव आदित्य इव वा दीधि-
> षायो धारयिता भूत् । भवति । कुत्रॆति उच्यते । आदेवे देवपर्यंते जने ।
> मनुष्यप्रकृतिदेवपर्यंतेषु । तेषां धारकोऽभवदित्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Bright, sinless, hospitable, omniscient Agni, who supports all beings from men to gods like a friend, is invoked for the sacrificers.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(ऎलै यजमानरे) वः—निमगागि (*(èlai yajamānare) vaḥ—nimagāgi*) (O sacrificers: for you). सुद्योत्मानं—श्रेष्ठवाद प्रकाशवुळ्ळवनू (*sudyotmānaṃ—śreṣṭhavāda prakāśavuḷḷavanū*) (of excellent radiance). सुवृक्तिं—पापवर्जितनू अथवा उत्तमवाद स्तुतियुळ्ळवनू (*suvṛktiṃ—pāpavarjitanū athavā uttamavāda stutiyuḷḷavanū*) (free from sin, or having excellent praise). विशां—यजमानरिगॆ (*viśāṃ—yajamānarigè*) (to the sacrificers). अतिथिं- अतिथियंतॆ पूज्यनू (*atithiṃ- atithiyaṃtè pūjyanū*) (worshipful like a guest). सुप्रयसं—हविस्सिन रूपद अन्नवुळ्ळवनू आद (*suprayasaṃ—havissina rūpada annavuḷḷavanū āda*) (having food in the form of oblation, such). अग्निं—अग्नियन्नु (*agniṃ—agniyannu*) (Agni). हुवे—प्रार्थिसि करॆयुत्तेनॆ (*huve—prārthisi karèyuttenè*) (I invoke with prayer). जातवेदाः जातप्रज्ञनाद (*jātavedāḥ jātaprajñanāda*) (Jātavedas, the omniscient (the dash is lacking in the print)). यः देवः—देवतात्मनाद (*yaḥ devaḥ—devatātmanāda*) (who, divine). याव अदे अग्नियु (*yāva ade agniyu*) (that same Agni (two words in the print)). मित्र इव—सखनंतॆ अथवा मित्रदेवनंतॆ (*mitra iva—sakhanaṃtè athavā mitradevanaṃtè*) (like a friend or like the god Mitra). आ देवे जने—मानवरु मॊदलुगॊंडु देवतॆगळवरॆगू इरुव प्रजॆगळन्नु (*ā deve jane—mānavaru mòdalugòṃḍu devatègaḷavarègū iruva prajègaḷannu*) (the people who are from men to gods). दिधिषाय्यः—धरिसिरुववनागि (*didhiṣāyyaḥ—dharisiruvavanāgi*) (supporting). भूत्— आगिरुत्तानॆ. (*bhūt— āgiruttānè.*) (he is).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O sacrificers, on your behalf I invoke with prayer Agni, who has excellent radiance, who is free from sin or has excellent praise, who is worshipful to the sacrificers like a guest, and who has food in the form of oblation. Agni, the omniscient, of divine self, supports like a friend the beings from men up to the gods (he protects them).

**Printed English translation**

I invoke, on your behalf, the resplendent, the sinless Agni, the guest of mortals, the accepter of (sacrificial) food, who, knowing all that has been born, is like a friend, the supporter (of all beings), from men to gods.

### Printed p. 472

*Running head (as supplied): [472 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं २. अ. १. सू ४] (*[472 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ 2. a. 1. sū 4]*).*

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1)**

Addressing the sacrificers, the seer of the mantra says that on their behalf he invokes Agni, सुवृक्तिं—सुवर्जितं पापैः (*suvṛktiṃ—suvarjitaṃ pāpaiḥ*) (as printed): "sin" means the acts that cause sorrow, and Agni is one freed from them; or शोभनस्तुतिं वा (*śobhanastutiṃ vā*): one praised with auspicious hymns. And it is described that Agni is always worthy of worship, like a guest, for the sacrificers.

जातवेदाः यः देवः मित्र इव दिधिषाय्यः अग्निः सखेव आदित्य इव वा मनुष्यप्रभृति देवपर्यंतेषु जनेषु धारयिता भवति (*jātavedāḥ yaḥ devaḥ mitra iva didhiṣāyyaḥ agniḥ sakheva āditya iva vā manuṣyaprabhṛti devaparyaṃteṣu janeṣu dhārayitā bhavati*) (a line-end hyphen inside it is joined): Agni, the omniscient, is the supporter of all beings from men up to gods like a friend, that is, a well-wisher like a friend who does good to all beings, or a protector like the sun: thus it is explained in two ways.

अतिथिं—अतिथिवत्तूज्यं । दर्शादितिथिमपेक्ष्य आगंतारं वा । (*atithiṃ—atithivattūjyaṃ | darśāditithimapekṣya āgaṃtāraṃ vā |*) Agni is worthy of worship by the sacrificer, like a guest who has come to the house; or the meaning is explained that Agni comes at the will of the sacrificers who perform sacrifices (the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices and the like) following the lunar days (tithi) such as the new moon. The Nirukta-writers, having cited the ṛk

जुष्टो दमूना अतिथिर्दुरोण इमं नो यज्ञमुप याहि विद्वान् । (*juṣṭo damūnā atithirduroṇa imaṃ no yajñamupa yāhi vidvān |*)
विश्वा अग्ने अभियुजो विहत्या शत्रूयतामा भरा योजनानि ॥ (*viśvā agne abhiyujo vihatyā śatrūyatāmā bharā yojanāni ‖*)

(पु. सं ५-४-५ (*pu. saṃ 5-4-5*)) (as printed) (rendered loosely: pleasing in the house, a guest in the dwelling, come, knowing, to this our sacrifice of ours; O Agni, having struck down all attacks, bring the possessions of those who behave as enemies; the printed last word is a misprint), have given the explanation of the word:

अतिथिरभ्यतितो गृहान् भवति । अभ्येति तिथिषु परकुलानीति वा परगृहाणीति वा। (*atithirabhyatito gṛhān bhavati | abhyeti tithiṣu parakulānīti vā paragṛhāṇīti vā|*)
अयमपीतरोऽतिथेरेतस्मादेव । (*ayamapītaro 'titheretasmādeva |*)

(नि ४-४ (*ni 4-4*)). Durgācārya, commenting on it, says: गृहान् अभि अभिमुख्येन असौ अतितो भवति (*gṛhān abhi abhimukhyena asau atito bhavati*) — since he comes seeking houses, he is called a guest. Or, he comes and joins the houses of those who sacrifice on lunar days such as the new moon; therefore Agni is called a guest. Or अभ्येति तिथिसु परकुलानि पौर्णमास्यादिषु यजमानकुलानि अभ्यागच्छति इति अतिथिः । (*abhyeti tithisu parakulāni paurṇamāsyādiṣu yajamānakulāni abhyāgacchati iti atithiḥ |*) आयमपीतरोऽतिथिरेतस्मादेव। (*āyamapītaro 'tithiretasmādeva|*) (as printed): that is, because on other lunar days (days) he goes to the sacrificial houses of other families, and on sacrificial days such as the full moon he comes to the houses of the sacrificers, for these two reasons the name "guest" has come to Agni; thus he has explained the meaning.

*(The supplied text ends here, at the end of the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 on p. 472; Ṛk 2 follows in the next window.)*

#### Ṛk 2

*[As supplied, the label line of the Saṃhitā reads संहितापार्श्व (*saṃhitāpārśva*); standard label inserted. A figure line of the supplied text, an image repeating the Saṃhitā and Pada of this ṛk, was viewed; the Pada agrees with the machine text, and one Saṃhitā word, not clearly legible in the image, is left as supplied and marked with a query (see the Kannada text). The Saṃhitā, printed as plain lines, is given as a quoted block with its split line joined.]*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इ॒मं वि॒धंतो॑ अ॒पां स॒धस्थे॑ द्वि॒ताद॑धु॒र्भृग॑वो वि॒क्ष्वा॒३॒॑त्रियोः ।
> ए॒ष विश्वा॑न्य॒भ्य॑स्तु॒ भूमा॑ दे॒वाना॑म॒ग्निर॑र॒तिर्जी॒राश्वः॑ ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इमं । विधंतः । अपां । सधस्थे । द्विता । अदधुः । भृगवः । विक्षु । आयोः ।
> एष । विश्वानि । अभि । अस्तु । भूम । देवानां । अग्निः । अरतिः । जीरअश्वः ॥ २ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> इममग्निं विधंतः परिचरंतो भृगवोऽस्मत्पूर्वे महर्षयोऽपां सधस्थे
> सहस्थानेऽंतरिक्ष आयोर्मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य स्वभूतासु विक्षु प्रजास्त्वत्विक्षु तेषां
> मध्यॆ च द्विता द्वयोः स्थानाददधुः । आधारयन् ॥ दधातेर्लज रूपं ॥ एषोऽ-
> ग्निर्भूम भूम्नात्यर्थं विश्वानि भूतजातान्यस्मद्विरोधीन्यभ्यस्तु । अभिभवतु । स
> कीदृशः । देवानामरतिरीश्वरः । तेषां मध्यॆ शीघ्रमरणशीलो वात्मद्यागं प्रति ।
> तथा जीराश्वः क्षिप्राश्वः ॥

*Gist:* Ancient Bhṛgus manifested this Agni twice, in the atmosphere and among men; may Agni, lord of the gods with swift horses, overcome all our foes.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

इमं—ई अग्नियन्नु (*imaṃ—ī agniyannu*) (this Agni). विधंतः—परिचरिसतक्क (*vidhaṃtaḥ—paricarisatakka*) (those who serve). भृगवः—भृगुऋषिगळु (*bhṛgavaḥ—bhṛguṛṣigaḷu*) (the Bhṛgu seers). अपां- सधस्थे—अंतरिक्षदल्लियू (*apāṃ- sadhasthe—aṃtarikṣadalliyū*) (in the abode of the waters, the atmosphere (the entry is printed with a spaced hyphen)). आयोः विक्षु—यजमानरिगॆ सेरिद ऋत्विक्कुगळ गुंपिनल्लियू (*āyoḥ vikṣu—yajamānarigè serida ṛtvikkugaḷa guṃpinalliyū*) (in the group of priests belonging to the sacrificers). द्विता—ऎरडु स्थानगळिंदलू अथवा ऎरडु सल (*dvitā—èraḍu sthānagaḷiṃdalū athavā èraḍu sala*) (from the two places, or twice). अदधुः—आविर्भूतनागुवंतॆ माडिदरु (*adadhuḥ—āvirbhūtanāguvaṃtè māḍidaru*) (they caused him to be manifested). देवानां—देवतॆगळ (*devānāṃ—devatègaḷa*) (of the gods). अरतिः—ईश्वरनू (*aratiḥ—īśvaranū*) (the lord). जीराश्वः—वेगवाद अश्वारूढनागिरुववनू आद (*jīrāśvaḥ—vegavāda aśvārūḍhanāgiruvavanū āda*) (one who is mounted on a swift horse). एषः अग्निः—ई अग्नियु (*eṣaḥ agniḥ—ī agniyu*) (this Agni). भूम—अधिकवागि (*bhūma—adhikavāgi*) (abundantly). विश्वानि—नम्म विरोधिगळॆल्लरन्नू (*viśvāni—namma virodhigaḷèllarannū*) (all our enemies). अभ्यस्तु— सोलिसि नाशपडिसलि (*abhyastu— solisi nāśapaḍisali*) (let him conquer and destroy).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Bhṛgu seers who serve this Agni caused him to be manifested twice: once in the atmosphere, and once on earth among the priests, thus in two places. May this Agni, the lord of the gods, mounted on a swift horse, completely conquer and destroy all our enemies.

### Printed p. 474

*Running head (as supplied): [474 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २ अ. १. सू ४] (*[474 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2 a. 1. sū 4]*).*

**Printed English translation**

The Bhrigus, worshipping Agni, have twice made him manifest, (once) in the abode of the waters, and (once) amongst the sons of men ; may that Agni, the sovereign of the gods mounted on a rapid courser, ever overcome all (our foes).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 2)**

Here, for the word भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*) the meaning अस्मत्पूर्वे महर्षयः (*asmatpūrve maharṣayaḥ*) is explained: the great seers more ancient than Gṛtsamada, the seer of the mantra. And since Gṛtsamada belonged to the Bhṛgu family, it is natural that he calls the earlier seers of the Bhṛgu family his forefathers.

आयोः विक्षु—मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य स्वभूतासु प्रजासु ऋत्विक्षु (*āyoḥ vikṣu—manuṣyasya yajamānasya svabhūtāsu prajāsu ṛtvikṣu*): the word denoting "man" is explained as the sacrificer, and, since the priests and the sons, grandsons and others are dear to the sacrificers, the great seers caused Agni to be manifested in the atmosphere, that is, in the form of lightning, and in the houses of the priests and the people who belong to the sacrificers (in two places). That is, it is explained that Agni exists in two ways: in the atmosphere as lightning, and, for the sake of sacrifice, among the priests.

एषः भूम विश्वानि अभ्यस्तु—अग्निः ( भूम्ना ) अत्यर्थं अस्मद्विरोधीनि भूतजातानि अभिभवतु (*eṣaḥ bhūma viśvāni abhyastu—agniḥ ( bhūmnā ) atyarthaṃ asmadvirodhīni bhūtajātāni abhibhavatu*) (a line-end hyphen inside it is joined): the wish of the sacrificers is described that Agni may conquer all the beings that belong to the enemies of us, the sacrificers.

देवानां अरतिः— अवतिरीश्वरः । शीघ्रमरणशीलो वा । (*devānāṃ aratiḥ— avatirīśvaraḥ | śīghramaraṇaśīlo vā |*) (as printed): two kinds of meaning are explained for the word अरति (*arati*) here: that Agni is the lord of the gods, or that among the gods he is the one who comes most quickly of all to the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 475

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. .४] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 475 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. .4] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 475*).*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अग्निं । देवासः । मानुषीषु । विक्षु । प्रियं । धुः । क्षेष्यंतः । न । मित्रं ।
> सः । दीदयत् । उशतीः । ऊर्म्याः । आ । दक्षाय्यः । यः । दास्वते । दमे । आ ॥ ३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> देवासो देवाः क्षेष्यंतः स्वर्गं प्रति गच्छंतः संतः पूर्वं मानुषीषु
> मनुष्यसंबंधिनीषु विक्षु प्रजासु प्रियं देवानां प्रीणयितारमग्निं धुः । अधुः
> स्थापितवंतः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । क्षेष्यंतो मित्रं न । रायं प्रति गच्छंतो नरा मित्रं
> प्रियं सखायं स्वगृहरक्षार्थं स्थापयंति । तद्वत् । स एवं देवैः स्थापितो
> योऽग्निर्दास्वते हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय तदर्थं दमे तदीये यागगृह आ
> आहितः स्थापितो दक्षाय्यः समर्धयिता दाता वा सोऽग्निरुशतीः कामयमाना
> ऊर्म्या रात्रिः सर्वासु रात्रिष्वादीदयत् । दीप्यते सर्वतः । सर्वरात्रीरादीपयति
> वा ॥

*Gist:* The gods, going to heaven, placed Agni among men like a friend left to guard a house; he shines on all the nights.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

क्षेष्यंतः—धनार्थवागि हॊरक्कॆ होगतक्क मानवरु (*kṣeṣyaṃtaḥ—dhanārthavāgi hòrakkè hogatakka mānavaru*) (men going out for wealth). मित्रं न—(तम्म गृहद रक्षणॆगॆ) तम्म स्नेहितरन्निरिसुवंतॆ (*mitraṃ na—(tamma gṛhada rakṣaṇègè) tamma snehitarannirisuvaṃtè*) (as they set their friends (to guard their houses)). देवासः—देवतॆगळु (*devāsaḥ—devatègaḷu*) (the gods). क्षेष्यंतः—स्वर्गवासिगळागि होगु वाग (*kṣeṣyaṃtaḥ—svargavāsigaḷāgi hogu vāga*) (when going to live in heaven). मानुषीषु—मानवरिगॆ संबंधिसिद (*mānuṣīṣu—mānavarigè saṃbaṃdhisida*) (belonging to men). विक्षु—प्रजॆगळल्लि (*vikṣu—prajègaḷalli*) (among the people). प्रियं—देवतॆगळिगॆ प्रीतिकारकनाद अग्नियन्नु (*priyaṃ—devatègaḷigè prītikārakanāda agniyannu*) (Agni, dear to the gods). धुः—स्थापिसिदरु (*dhuḥ—sthāpisidaru*) (they established). यः—देवतॆगळिंद स्थापितनाद याव अग्नियु! (*yaḥ—devatègaḷiṃda sthāpitanāda yāva agniyu!*) (that Agni who, established by the gods (the entry ends with an exclamation mark)). दास्वते—हविस्सन्नु अर्पिसतक्क यजमाननिगागि (*dāsvate—havissannu arpisatakka yajamānanigāgi*) (for the sacrificer who offers oblations). दमे—अवन यागगृहदल्लि (*dame—avana yāgagṛhadalli*) (in his sacrificial house). आ—स्थापितनागि (*ā—sthāpitanāgi*) (being established). दक्षाय्यः—(अवन संपत्तन्नु) वृद्धिपडिसुत्तानॆयो (*dakṣāyyaḥ—(avana saṃpattannu) vṛddhipaḍisuttānèyo*) (increases (his wealth)). सः—आ अग्नियु (*saḥ—ā agniyu*) (that Agni). उशतीः—अवनन्नु अपेक्षिसतक्क (*uśatīḥ—avanannu apekṣisatakka*) (longing for him). ऊर्म्याः—सकल रात्रिगळल्लू (*ūrmyāḥ—sakala rātrigaḷallū*) (on all the nights). आ दीदयत्—प्रकाशिसुत्तानॆ. (*ā dīdayat—prakāśisuttānè.*) (shines).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

When the gods were going to heaven to dwell, they placed Agni, dear to the gods, among men, as a man going out for wealth places his friend to guard his house. The Agni who, established in the house of the sacrificer who offers oblations, increases his wealth, shines on all the nights for which he longs.

**Printed English translation**

The gods, intending to dwell (in heaven), left, as a dear friend amongst the human races, that Agni, who, present in the obanber [sic] of sacrifice, is bounteous to the donor of offerings, aud [sic] shines on the nights when he is wished for.

*(The printed English reads "obanber" and "aud" [sic].)*

### Printed p. 476

*Running head (as supplied): [476 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २ अ. १. सू. ४] (*[476 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2 a. 1. sū. 4]*).*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 of Sūkta 4 of Maṇḍala 2. As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषयुक्त: (*viśeṣayukta:*); standard label inserted.)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 3)**

देवाः क्षेष्यंतः मानुषीषु विक्षु प्रियं मित्रं न धुः (*devāḥ kṣeṣyaṃtaḥ mānuṣīṣu vikṣu priyaṃ mitraṃ na dhuḥ*): two kinds of meaning are explained for this sentence. देवाः स्वर्ग० प्रतिगच्छंतः मनुष्यसंबंधिनीषु प्रजासु अग्निं प्रीणयितारं स्थापितवंतः (*devāḥ svarga0 pratigacchaṃtaḥ manuṣyasaṃbaṃdhinīṣu prajāsu agniṃ prīṇayitāraṃ sthāpitavaṃtaḥ*) (the print has the digit zero for the anusvāra in the second word): the first meaning is that when the gods were going to heaven, they first established among the people who belong to men Agni, who gives them delight. The second meaning is by way of illustration: क्षेष्यंतः मित्रं न— रायं प्रतिगच्छंतो नराः प्रियं सखायं स्वगृहरक्षार्थं स्थापयंति तद्वत् (*kṣeṣyaṃtaḥ mitraṃ na— rāyaṃ pratigacchaṃto narāḥ priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ svagṛharakṣārthaṃ sthāpayaṃti tadvat*): as people going out to gain their wealth place their dear friends to guard their houses, so the gods have placed Agni among men: this second meaning is also explained.

यः दास्यते दमे आ दाक्षाय्यः—एवं देवैः स्थापितः अग्निः हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय यागगृहे आहितः समर्थयिता दाता वा (*yaḥ dāsyate dame ā dākṣāyyaḥ—evaṃ devaiḥ sthāpitaḥ agniḥ havirdattavate yajamānāya yāgagṛhe āhitaḥ samarthayitā dātā vā*) (as printed): Agni, thus established by the gods, placed in the sacrificial hall in his own dwelling by the sacrificers, fulfils the desired objects of the sacrificer who offers the oblation, or increases the wealth of the sacrificers: thus it is described.

This Agni, उर्माः आ दीदयत् (*urmāḥ ā dīdayat*)—सर्वासु रात्रिषु दीप्यते सर्वरात्रीरादिपयति वा (*sarvāsu rātriṣu dīpyate sarvarātrīrādipayati vā*) (a line-end hyphen inside it is joined): he shines in the night-time, that is, he shines fully the whole night from evening to morning; or he shines in the nights of all days: two kinds of meaning are explained.

### Printed p. 477

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २ अ. ५ व २४] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 477 (*[a. 2 a. 5 va 24] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 477*).*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अस्याग्नेः पुष्टिः शरीरवृद्धी रण्वा रमणीया शब्दयुक्ता वा । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । स्वस्य पुष्टिरिव । यथा लोके स्वकीया पुष्टिः स्वस्मै रमणीया भवति
> तद्वत् । यद्वास्याग्नेः संबंधिनी पुष्टियर्यथा यजमानविषया रण्वा तद्वत् ।
> किंच हियानस्य समृद्धिं गच्छतो व्याप्नु वतो दक्षोः काष्ठान् दिधक्षोर्दग्धु-
> मिच्छोरस्याग्नेः संदृष्टिः संदर्शनाविर्भावोऽपि रण्वा । योग्निरोषधीषु काष्ठेषु
> जिह्वां ज्वालां । जात्येकवचनं । ज्वाला विभरिभ्रत् । अत्यर्थ० विहरति । कंपयती-
> त्यर्थः ॥ हरतेर्यज्लुगंतत्वेन दाधर्त्यादिषु । पा. ७-४-६५ । निपातिताल्लेट्य-
> डागमः । यद्योगादनिघातः ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथ्यो रथार्होऽत्यो न वाजी
> यथा वारान् दंशवारणसाधनान्वाल्वान् दोधवीति । कंपयति तद्वत् । योS-
> ग्निर्ज्वालाः कंपयति अस्याग्नेः पुष्टि रण्वति ॥

*Gist:* Agni's growth is delightful like one's own; he shakes his flames among the fuel as a chariot-horse its tail.

*(The bhāṣya contains grammatical remarks, including a reference to Pāṇini, on the verb form, the substitution and the accent; they are transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

रथ्यः—रथवन्नु वहिसलु योग्यवाद (*rathyaḥ—rathavannu vahisalu yogyavāda*) (fit to draw a chariot). अत्यः—अश्ववु (*atyaḥ—aśvavu*) (the horse). वारान्—सॊळ्ळॆगळन्नु ऒडिसुव तन्न बालद गॊंचलन्नु (*vārān—sòḷḷègaḷannu òḍisuva tanna bālada gòṃcalannu*) (the tuft of his tail that drives away mosquitoes (printed "oḍisuva")). दोधवीति न—बीसि आडिसुवंतॆ (*dodhavīti na—bīsi āḍisuvaṃtè*) (like one who sways and shakes it). यः—याव अग्नियु (*yaḥ—yāva agniyu*) (which Agni). ओषधीषु—काष्ठादिगळल्लि (*oṣadhīṣu—kāṣṭhādigaḷalli*) (in the fuel and the like). जिह्वां—जिह्वारूपवाद तन्न ज्वालॆयन्नु (*jihvāṃ—jihvārūpavāda tanna jvālèyannu*) (his flame in the form of a tongue). वि भरिभ्रत्—नाना कडॆगळल्लियू प्रसरिसि विहरिसुत्तानॆयो (*vi bharibhrat—nānā kaḍègaḷalliyū prasarisi viharisuttānèyo*) (he spreads about in many places and ranges). अस्य—आ अग्निय पुष्टियुतवाद प्रसरवु (*asya—ā agniya puṣṭiyutavāda prasaravu*) (the nourished spread of that Agni). स्वस्य— द्रष्टृविन (*svasya— draṣṭṛvina*) (of the seer himself). पुष्टिः इव—स्वंत शरीरद पुष्टियुतवाद बॆळवणिगॆयंतॆ (*puṣṭiḥ iva—svaṃta śarīrada puṣṭiyutavāda bèḷavaṇigèyaṃtè*) (like the nourishing growth of one's own body). रण्वा—रमणीयवागिदॆ (*raṇvā—ramaṇīyavāgidè*) (is delightful). हियानस्य—वृद्धियन्नु हॊंदि हरडुववनू (*hiyānasya—vṛddhiyannu hòṃdi haraḍuvavanū*) (of the one who grows and spreads). धक्षोः—काष्ठादिगळन्नु दहिसुववनू आद अदे अग्निय (*dhakṣoḥ—kāṣṭhādigaḷannu dahisuvavanū āda ade agniya*) (who burns the fuel and the like, of that same Agni). संदृष्टिः—मनोहरवाद दर्शनवू सह आकर्षकवागिदॆ. (*saṃdṛṣṭiḥ—manoharavāda darśanavū saha ākarṣakavāgidè.*) (the charming sight too is attractive).

*[As supplied, the label line of the Bhāvārtha reads भानुवार (*bhānuvāra*); standard label inserted.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

As a horse fit to draw a chariot sways the tuft of its tail to drive away mosquitoes, the Agni who spreads his flame-like tongue in many places over the fuel and the like: the nourished spread of that Agni is delightful, like the nourishing growth of the seer's own body. The sight of that same Agni, who grows, spreads and burns the fuel and the like, is also attractive.

**Printed English translation**

The cherishing of Agni is as agreeable as (the cherishing) of one's self ; (pleasant) is his appearance, when spreading abroad, and consuming (the fuel) ; he brandishes his flame amongst the bushes, as a chariot-horse lashes with his tail.

### Printed p. 478

*Running head (as supplied): [478 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २. आ. १. सू ४] (*[478 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2. ā. 1. sū 4]*).*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 4)**

अस्य पुष्टिः रण्वा स्वस्य पुष्टिरिव (*asya puṣṭiḥ raṇvā svasya puṣṭiriva*)—अग्नेः शरीरवृद्धिः रमणीया शब्दयुक्ता वा । (*agneḥ śarīravṛddhiḥ ramaṇīyā śabdayuktā vā |*) Agni's bodily growth is charming or accompanied by sound. An illustration is given for this: यथा लोके स्वकीया पुष्टिं स्वस्मै रमणीया (*yathā loke svakīyā puṣṭiṃ svasmai ramaṇīyā*) (as printed): as, in the world, the bodily nourishment of living beings is agreeable to each of them, so is the illustration for Agni's bodily growth. यद्वा अस्याग्नेः संबंधिनी पुष्टिः यजमानविषया रणा स्वस्याग्नेः पुष्टिः यथा रण्वा तद्वत् (*yadvā asyāgneḥ saṃbaṃdhinī puṣṭiḥ yajamānaviṣayā raṇā svasyāgneḥ puṣṭiḥ yathā raṇvā tadvat*) (as printed): another kind of meaning is explained: as the growth of this Agni by the oblations offered by the sacrificers is charming toward the sacrificers, so this Agni's own bodily growth also gives joy.

हियानस्य धक्षोः संदृष्टिः रण्वा (*hiyānasya dhakṣoḥ saṃdṛṣṭiḥ raṇvā*)—समृद्धिं गच्छतो कार्ष्णा दग्गु मिच्छोः अस्याग्नेः संदर्शनाविर्भावोपि रण्वा । (*samṛddhiṃ gacchato kārṣṇā daggu micchoḥ asyāgneḥ saṃdarśanāvirbhāvopi raṇvā |*) (as printed): it is explained that the manifestation by which Agni, grown great and wishing to burn the herbs and the like that are in the forest, makes himself appear is also radiant and delightful to all.

रथ्यः अत्यो न वार्ता दोधवीति (*rathyaḥ atyo na vārtā dodhavīti*) (as printed)—रथार्हः वाजी यथा दंशवारणसाधर्ना वार्ला कंपयति तद्वत् अग्निः काष्ठेषु ज्वालाः कंपयति (*rathārhaḥ vājī yathā daṃśavāraṇasādharnā vārlā kaṃpayati tadvat agniḥ kāṣṭheṣu jvālāḥ kaṃpayati*) (as printed): it is explained that as a horse that draws a chariot waves its tail to drive away flies and the like that trouble its body, so Agni, when he spreads over the fuel, makes his flames spread around and tremble. The word अत्य (*atya*) has been read by Yāska among the names of the horse (नि. २-२७ (*ni. 2-27*)).

In this ṛk Agni in the form of a forest fire is described. As the bodily nourishment of people is agreeable and pleasing to them, so when Agni grows great and burns the fuel and the like with a roaring sound, it is charming and delightful to the people who watch it. An illustration is given for this here: when mosquitoes settle on a horse's hindquarters and bite, the horse merely sweeps its tail around to drive them off; in the same way Agni spreads his flames around, envelops trees and the like and burns them: this meaning is described here. It is also said that such a sight, though fearful, is in a way attractive or charming to look at.

> आ यन्मे॒ अभ्वं॑ व॒नदः॒ पनं॑तो॒तिग्भ्यो॒ नामि॑मीत॒ वर्ण॑० ।
> स चि॒त्रेण॑ चिकिते॒ रंसु॑ भा॒सा जु॑जु॒र्वा यो मुहु॒रा युवा॒ भूत् ॥ ५ ॥

> सः । चित्रेण । चिकिते । रंसु । भासा । जुजुर्वान् । यः । मुहुः । आ । युवा । भूत् ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> यत् यस्याभ्वं महत्त्वं मे मम संबंधिनो वनदो वनंतः संभक्तारः ।
> यद्वा वनदोऽवनदो भृशं शब्दयंतः स्तोतारः ॥ अवशब्दो भृशार्थवाची ।
> तत्पूर्वान्नदेः क्विप् । आवाप्योरित्यकारलोपः ॥ अपनंत । समंतात् स्तुवंति ।
> सोऽग्निरुशिग्गोऽस्मदीयं रूपं कामयमानेभ्य ऋत्विग्गोऽ वर्णं स्वसदृशं
> रूपं नामिमिता ॥ नशब्दश्चार्थे ॥ निर्मिवीते च । स च रंसु रमणीयेष्वाज्यादिह-
> विःषु निमित्तेषु चित्रेण भासा हिरण्यकनकादिनानावर्णया दीप्त्या चिकिते । विज्ञा-
> यते । किंच योऽग्निर्जुजुर्वान् जीर्णः सन् ज्वालोपशमे स एव मुहुः पुनः-
> पुनरा युवा सर्वतो मिश्रयिता तरुणो वाभूत् । अभवति पुनराज्यादिसंगोगात् ।

*Gist:* Whose greatness my kinsmen praise loudly, who shapes his form for the priests, shines in many colours at oblations, and though ageing becomes young again.

*(The bhāṣya contains short grammatical remarks on the formation of two words; they are transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

*[As supplied, the label line of the Pratipadārtha reads प्रतिसदार्फ् (*pratisadārph*), inside the bhāṣya block, and its lines carry the quote marks of the block; the label is replaced by the standard label and the lines are un-quoted.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यत्—याव अग्निय (*yat—yāva agniya*) (of which Agni). अभ्वं—महत्त्ववन्नु (*abhvaṃ—mahattvavannu*) (greatness). मे—नन्न बंधुगळु (*me—nanna baṃdhugaḷu*) (my kinsmen). वनदः—गट्टि यागि शब्द माडिसुत्ता (*vanadaḥ—gaṭṭi yāgi śabda māḍisuttā*) (making loud sound (the word is divided by a line break)). आ पनंत—सुत्तलू स्तुतिसुत्तारॆयो (*ā panaṃta—suttalū stutisuttārèyo*) (they praise all around). सः—आ अग्नियु (*saḥ—ā agniyu*) (that Agni). उशिग्भ्यः— अवन रूपवन्नु नोडबेकॆंदु अपेक्षिसुव ऋत्विक्कुगळिगॆ (*uśigbhyaḥ— avana rūpavannu noḍabekèṃdu apekṣisuva ṛtvikkugaḷigè*) (for the priests who desire to see his form). वर्णं—तन्न रम्यवाद रूपवन्नु (*varṇaṃ—tanna ramyavāda rūpavannu*) (his charming form). नामिमीत—निर्मिसि तोरिसुत्तानॆ (मत्तु) (*nāmimīta—nirmisi torisuttānè (mattu)*) (he creates and shows (and)). रंसु—रमणीयवाद आज्यादि हविस्सुगळन्नु अर्पिसिदाग (*raṃsu—ramaṇīyavāda ājyādi havissugaḷannu arpisidāga*) (when charming oblations such as ghee are offered). चित्रेण—नानारूपवाद (*citreṇa—nānārūpavāda*) (of various forms). भासा—कांतियिंद (*bhāsā—kāṃtiyiṃda*) (with lustre). चिकिते—प्रकाशितनागुत्तानॆ (*cikite—prakāśitanāguttānè*) (he shines). यः—याव अग्नियु (*yaḥ—yāva agniyu*) (which Agni). जुजुर्वान्—जीर्णवागुवनो (अवने) (*jujurvān—jīrṇavāguvano (avane)*) (he who is consumed (that very one)). मुहुः—पुनः पुनः (आज्या हुतिगळन्नु अर्पिसुवुदरिंद) (*muhuḥ—punaḥ punaḥ (ājyā hutigaḷannu arpisuvudariṃda)*) (again and again (by offering ghee oblations)). आ युवा भूत्—तरुणनागि आगुत्तानॆ (*ā yuvā bhūt—taruṇanāgi āguttānè*) (he becomes young).

### Printed p. 480

*Running head (as supplied): [480 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. अ. १. सू. .४] (*[480 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. .4]*).*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Agni whose greatness my kinsmen praise all around with a loud voice shapes and shows his charming form to the priests who desire to see his form; and when charming oblations such as ghee are offered, he shines with a lustre of many forms. When he is being consumed, by the offering of ghee oblations he attains youth again.

**Printed English translation**

Whose greatness my colleagues loudly extol, who has manifested his real form to the priests, who is recognized at oblations by his variegated radiance, and who though frequently growing old, again and again becomes young.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 5)**

अभ्वं वनदः आ पनंत—यस्य महत्त्वं संभक्तारः यद्वा वनदो अवनदो बृशं शब्दयंतः स्तोतारः समंतात् स्तुवंति (*abhvaṃ vanadaḥ ā panaṃta—yasya mahattvaṃ saṃbhaktāraḥ yadvā vanado avanado bṛśaṃ śabdayaṃtaḥ stotāraḥ samaṃtāt stuvaṃti*) (as printed): the word for "great", spelt in the print with the Kannada ending, has been read by Yāska among the names of "great" (नि. ३-१३ (*ni. 3-13*)); here it is used in the sense of Agni's greatness. For the word वनद (*vanada*) the meaning is given that they make the greatness manifest, or that they sound loudly. It is explained that when the priests of the sacrificers praise Agni they make his abundant greatness manifest by hymns, or praise him with a loud voice so that all may know.

उशिग्भ्यः वर्णं नामिमीत (*uśigbhyaḥ varṇaṃ nāmimīta*): the meaning is that Agni creates for the priests who wish to see his own form a form that matches his greatness. The word उशिक् (*uśik*) (with the sense of "desiring") is stated among the names of lustre-acts (नि. ३-९ (*ni. 3-9*)) and is explained by Yāska: उशिग् वष्टेः कांति कर्मणः (*uśig vaṣṭeḥ kāṃti karmaṇaḥ*) (नि ६-१ (*ni 6-1*)).

रंसु-चित्रेण चिकिते (*raṃsu-citreṇa cikite*): it is explained that by the offering of oblations such as ghee this Agni shines with the lustres of charming things such as gold. That is, the purport is that Agni's flames, endowed with many colours such as red, golden and white, are delightful to look at.

जुजुर्वान् मुहुः आ युवा (*jujurvān muhuḥ ā yuvā*)—ज्वालोपशमे जीर्णर्स्स स एव पुनः पुनः मिश्रयिता तरुणो ना भवति (*jvālopaśame jīrṇarssa sa eva punaḥ punaḥ miśrayitā taruṇo nā bhavati*) (as printed): Agni, when his flames subside and he is lustreless, shines again, having attained youth, at the time of receiving oblations (the sentence continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 481

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. २५ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 481 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 25 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 481*).*

That an old man becomes young is unknown in the world; but Agni, though old many times, shines with youth: thus a contrast is stated. Here Agni, when he is going out, is said to be in old age; but when sticks, wood, ghee, oblations and the like are put on the small embers of the fire and the homa is made, the small fire again becomes great and shines brightly with flames, and this is described here as Agni becoming young again.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> योऽग्निर्वना वनानि वृक्षसमूहान् ततृषाणो न तृषित इव । त्वरमाण
> इत्यर्थः । आभाति । आभासयति । दहतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा वना वने आभाति । किंच वार्ण
> उदकमिव पथा प्रवणेन मार्गेण गच्छति । तद्वत् इतस्ततो गच्छति । रथ्येव रथस्य
> वोढाश्व इव स्वानीत् । शब्दयति ! यद्वा रथशब्दात् सोर्ड्यादेशः । यथा रथो
> युद्धमार्गेण गच्छन् स्वनति तद्वत् । किंच कृष्णाध्वा कृष्णवर्त्मा तपुस्तापको रणो
> रमणीय एवंभूतः सन् चिकेत । ज्ञायते । प्रकाशत इत्यर्थः । क इव । नभोभि-
> र्नक्षत्रैः स्वयमानः प्रकाशमानो द्यौरिव द्युलोक इव । यद्वा नभोभिरंतरिक्ष-
> प्रदेशविशेषैः स्वयमानः शोभमानो द्यौरादित्य इव । नीलवर्णांतरिक्षचार्या-
> दित्यो यथा ज्ञायते तद्वत् स्वसंचारेण कृष्णीभूते मार्गे ज्ञायते । प्रकाशत
> इत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Agni, eager, burns the woods, flows like water, sounds like a chariot-horse, is dark-pathed, hot and shines like the sky with stars.

*(The bhāṣya contains an exclamation mark in place of a danda after a word, as printed, and short grammatical remarks; they are transcribed in the block and not explained. The supplied text ends here, after the bhāṣya of Ṛk 6 at the end of p. 481; the Pratipadārtha follows in the next window.)*

### Printed p. 482

*Running head (as supplied): [482 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. अ. १. सू. ४] (*[482 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. 4]*).*

*(Continuation of Ṛk 6 of Sūkta 4 of Maṇḍala 2: its Pratipadārtha follows the bhāṣya of the previous page. The Pratipadārtha has two bracketed alternatives, as printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यः—याव अग्नियु (*yaḥ—yāva agniyu*) (which Agni). वना—वनगळन्नु (*vanā—vanagaḷannu*) (the forests). ततृषाणो न —दाहदिंद कूडिरुवव नंतॆ (*tatṛṣāṇo na —dāhadiṃda kūḍiruvava naṃtè*) (like one afflicted with thirst (the word is divided by a line break)). आ भाति—दहिसुत्तानॆयो [अथवा (*ā bhāti—dahisuttānèyo [athavā*) (he burns (the bracketed alternative begins here)). वना—वनदल्लि (*vanā—vanadalli*) (in the forest). आ भाति—प्रकाशिसुत्तानॆयो] (मत्तु) (*ā bhāti—prakāśisuttānèyo] (mattu)*) (he shines (the bracket closes here) (and)). वार्ण—उदकवु यावरीतियल्लि (*vārṇa—udakavu yāvarītiyalli*) (as water). पथा—इळिजाराद प्रदेशदल्लि वेगवागि हरियु वुदो हागॆ वेगवागि प्रसरिसुवनो (*pathā—iḷijārāda pradeśadalli vegavāgi hariyu vudo hāgè vegavāgi prasarisuvano*) (in sloping ground, flows swiftly, so he spreads swiftly (the word is divided by a line break)). रथ्या इव—रथवन्नु वहिसुव युद्धाश्ववु (*rathyā iva—rathavannu vahisuva yuddhāśvavu*) (like a war-horse that draws a chariot). स्वानीत्— शब्द माडुवंतॆ शब्द माडुवनो (आ अग्नियु) (*svānīt— śabda māḍuvaṃtè śabda māḍuvano (ā agniyu)*) (sounds, so he sounds (that Agni)). कृष्णाध्वा—कृष्णवर्णद मार्गवुळ्ळवनागियू (*kṛṣṇādhvā—kṛṣṇavarṇada mārgavuḷḷavanāgiyū*) (having a black-coloured path). तपुः—दहिसुववनागियू (*tapuḥ—dahisuvavanāgiyū*) (burning). रण्वः—(आदरू) रमणीयनागियू (*raṇvaḥ—(ādarū) ramaṇīyanāgiyū*) ((yet) delightful). नभोभिः—नक्षत्रगळिंद (*nabhobhiḥ—nakṣatragaḷiṃda*) (by the stars). स्मयमानः—प्रकाशिसतक्क (*smayamānaḥ—prakāśisatakka*) (shining). द्यौरिव—अंतरिक्षदंतॆ [अथवा (*dyauriva—aṃtarikṣadaṃtè [athavā*) (like the atmosphere (the bracketed alternative begins here)). नभोभिः—अंतरिक्ष प्रदेशगळल्लि (*nabhobhiḥ—aṃtarikṣa pradeśagaḷalli*) (in the regions of the atmosphere). स्मयमानः—शोभिसतक्क (*smayamānaḥ—śobhisatakka*) (shining). द्यौरिव—आदित्यनंतॆ] (*dyauriva—ādityanaṃtè]*) (like the sun (the bracket closes here)). चिकेत—तिळियल्पडुत्तानॆ (*ciketa—tiḷiyalpaḍuttānè*) (he is known).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Agni who burns the forests as if parched with thirst, who spreads swiftly in the forest as water flows swiftly in sloping ground, and who makes a loud noise like a horse that draws a chariot in war: that Agni, though he has a black path and burns, is yet delightful and is known like the sun shining in the region of the atmosphere.

**Printed English translation**

Who shines amidst the forests, as if satisfying himself (with food) : who (rushes along), like water down a deolivity [sic], and thunders like a chariot (of war); dark-pathed, consuming, yet delightful, he is regarded like the sky smiling with constellations.

*(The printed English reads "deolivity" [sic] for "declivity".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 6)**

Here Agni is described as being in the form of a forest fire. वना ततृषाणो न आभाति (*vanā tatṛṣāṇo na ābhāti*)—वृक्षसमूर्हा तृषित इव त्वरमाणः आभासयति । (*vṛkṣasamūrhā tṛṣita iva tvaramāṇaḥ ābhāsayati |*) (as printed): it is described that Agni spreads through the groups of trees in the forest like a hungry person who eats his food hurriedly; or यद्वा वने आभाति (*yadvā vane ābhāti*), that he shines of himself in the forest. Because Agni's spreading is very swift, a comparison with a hungry person is stated.

वार्ण पथा (*vārṇa pathā*)—उदकमिव प्रवणेन मार्गेण इतस्ततो गच्छति (*udakamiva pravaṇena mārgeṇa itastato gacchati*): as water flows very swiftly and spreads in low ground, so Agni too spreads quickly here and there among the trees in the forest: thus the spreading of Agni is compared to the spreading of water.

### Printed p. 483

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ ५. व. २५] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 483 (*[a. 2. a 5. va. 25] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 483*).*

रथ्येव स्वानीत् (*rathyeva svānīt*)—रथो यथा युद्धमार्गेण गच्छन् स्वनति (*ratho yathā yuddhamārgeṇa gacchan svanati*): as a horse that draws a chariot neighs when charging in war to attack the enemies, so Agni, spreading and burning in the forest, makes fearful crackling sounds; or he makes a sound like the noise made by the swiftly moving chariot of a charioteer attacking the enemies: the illustration of the sound is explained.

कृष्णाध्वा तपुः रण्वः नभोभिः स्वयमानः दौरिव चिकेत (*kṛṣṇādhvā tapuḥ raṇvaḥ nabhobhiḥ svayamānaḥ dauriva ciketa*) (as printed): here the seer has explained the meaning by giving a very excellent and natural comparison. As a forest fire burns the forest and goes forward, the region burnt by the fire becomes black like collyrium. Wherever a fire burns well and the embers go out, that region appears black: this is well known in the world, and those who have seen lands burnt by a forest fire know it well. Therefore it is natural that the region burnt by Agni is called a black path. Even though the forest is burnt and the ground is black, it is natural that here and there, in places in the middle, embers and flames are not yet extinguished. Such a region is compared to the sky with stars; that is, the black earth is compared to the blue sky, and the embers or flames of the fire here and there to the stars; or it is compared to the sun shining with great radiance in the blue sky. In this context it should be understood that the fire still burning unextinguished in the middle of the burnt black earth is compared to the sun. Here the poet has used the words दौरिव स्वयमानः नभोभिः (*dauriva svayamānaḥ nabhobhiḥ*) in a very serious and meaningful way. Just as, when the sky with stars is described as shining like a smiling man, the sight of a smiling man or woman delights the mind, so the sight of the blue sky shining with stars also delights the mind. In the same way the seer explains that there is a black earth burnt by Agni, and thereby displays his skill in composition. (Some words of this passage are misspelt in the print and are left as printed.)

*Gist:* Agni spreads over the wide earth, ranges freely like an unherded beast, blackening what he burns and drying the bushes.

*(The bhāṣya contains short grammatical remarks on the accent and the particle; they are transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यः—याव अग्नियु (*yaḥ—yāva agniyu*) (which Agni). व्यस्थात्—नानाप्रदेशगळन्नु व्यापिसिरुत्तानॆयो (मत्तु) (*vyasthāt—nānāpradeśagaḷannu vyāpisiruttānèyo (mattu)*) (pervades the various regions (and)). उर्विं—विस्त्रतवाद पृथिवियन्नु (*urviṃ—vistratavāda pṛthiviyannu*) (the wide earth). अभि दक्षत्—व्यापिसि सुत्तलू हरडुत्तानॆयो (*abhi dakṣat—vyāpisi suttalū haraḍuttānèyo*) (spreads around, pervading). सः अग्निः—आ अग्नियु (*saḥ agniḥ—ā agniyu*) (that Agni). पशुर्न—पशुवु स्वच्छंददिंद सुत्तुवंतॆ (*paśurna—paśuvu svacchaṃdadiṃda suttuvaṃtè*) (like an animal that wanders at will). स्वयुः—ताने स्वतंत्रवागि विहरिसुत्तलू (*svayuḥ—tāne svataṃtravāgi viharisuttalū*) (ranging by himself, freely). अगोपाः—नियमरहितनागियू (*agopāḥ—niyamarahitanāgiyū*) (without restraint). शोचिष्मान्—कांतियन्नु हरडुत्तलू (*śociṣmān—kāṃtiyannu haraḍuttalū*) (spreading lustre). कृष्णव्यथिः—दहिसिद कंटकादिगळिगॆ कृष्णरूपवाद विकारवन्नुंटुमाडुत्तलू (*kṛṣṇavyathiḥ—dahisida kaṃṭakādigaḷigè kṛṣṇarūpavāda vikāravannuṃṭumāḍuttalū*) (causing a black change in the thorns and the like that he burns (the entry begins before a line break)). भूम— अत्यधिकवागि (*bhūma— atyadhikavāgi*) (exceedingly). अस्वयन्न—(वृक्षगळ रसवन्नु) आस्वादनॆमाडुवंतॆयू (*asvayanna—(vṛkṣagaḷa rasavannu) āsvādanèmāḍuvaṃtèyū*) (as if tasting (the juices of the trees)). अतसानि—तरुगुल्मादि गळन्नु नीरसवागि माडुवंतॆयू (*atasāni—tarugulmādi gaḷannu nīrasavāgi māḍuvaṃtèyū*) (as if making the bushes and the like juiceless (the word is divided by a line break)). उष्णन्—दहिसुत्तलू (*uṣṇan—dahisuttalū*) (burning). एति—संचरिसुत्तानॆ. (*eti—saṃcarisuttānè.*) (he ranges).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Agni who pervades the various regions and spreads in many ways, who pervades the wide earth and spreads around: that Agni ranges by himself and freely, like an animal wandering at will, without restraint, spreading lustre, causing a black change and distress in the thorns and the like that he burns, and burning as if tasting the juices of the trees exceedingly and making the bushes and the like juiceless.

*(The supplied text ends here, at the end of the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 7 on p. 484; the printed English follows in the next window.)*

### Printed p. 485

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. २५. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 485 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 25. ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 485*).*

*(Continuation of Ṛk 7 of Sūkta 4 of Maṇḍala 2: its printed English and Special Topics follow the Bhāvārtha of the previous page.)*

**Printed English translation**

He who is in many places ; who spreads over the whole earth, like an animal without a herdsman, that goes according to its own will, Agni, the bright-shining, consuming the dry-bushes, by whom the pain of blackness (is inflicted on the trees), entirely drinks up (their moisture).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 7)**

When Agni pervades the forest and burns it, व्यस्थात् विविधं विश्वं व्याप्ोति (*vyasthāt vividhaṃ viśvaṃ vyāpoti*) (as printed): he pervades the whole forest in many ways, leaving not a bit; and उर्विं अभिदक्षत्—विस्त्रतां पृथिवीं सर्वां अभिमुख्येन प्रवर्धमानो भवति । (*urviṃ abhidakṣat—vistratāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ abhimukhyena pravardhamāno bhavati |*) (a line-end hyphen inside it is joined): it is described that he not only pervades all the trees and herbs in the forest, but spreads over the wide forest land so that no one else has any chance to enter it. In regard to this Agni's spreading and ranging of his own accord in the forests, the comparison with an animal is stated: पशुर्न स्वयुः अगोपाः एति—जातः पशुः यथा स्वच्छंदेन चरति तथा स्वयमेव गच्छ् निर्यामकवर्जितो गच्छति । (*paśurna svayuḥ agopāḥ eti—jātaḥ paśuḥ yathā svacchaṃdena carati tathā svayameva gacch niryāmakavarjito gacchati |*) (as printed). It is explained that as an animal born and growing in the forest (such as an elephant) is not subject to anyone else and lives by moving as it wishes, so Agni, born in the forest, grows by his own free behaviour without coming under the control of those who keep him in order.

Here the comparison with an animal suits Agni very well. Animals such as tigers, lions and wild buffaloes, born and grown in the forest and subject to no one, range about, moving wherever they like. In the same way the forest fire, born in the forest itself (from the friction of trees), invades and burns the whole of the wide forest, and no one can stop it: this is the main purport.

कृष्णव्यथिः भूम अस्वदयन्न आतसानि उष्णन् (*kṛṣṇavyathiḥ bhūma asvadayanna ātasāni uṣṇan*)—कृष्णवर्णं प्राप्ताः दग्धाः वृथाकराः कंटकादयो येन (*kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ prāptāḥ dagdhāḥ vṛthākarāḥ kaṃṭakādayo yena*) (as printed): burning all the thorns and the like and making them black so that those who see them feel sorrow; वृक्षगर्ता रर्सा आस्वादयतीव (*vṛkṣagartā rarsā āsvādayatīva*) (as printed): sucking and consuming all the essential juices in the trees, like one who tastes them; संततानि नीरसानि वा तरुगुल्मादीनि दहन्नेति (*saṃtatāni nīrasāni vā tarugulmādīni dahanneti*): burning all the densely grown, juiceless (dried) trees and bushes, Agni pervades the forest and goes ever forward: thus it is described. Here, when Agni burns green trees, the juice in the trees dries up from Agni's heat and the tree is also burnt; its comparison to tasting the juice is also natural and full of meaning.

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> नू ते॒ पूर्व॒स्याव॑सो॒ अधी॑तौ तृ॒तीये॑ वि॒दथे॒ मन्म॑ शंसि ।
> अ॒स्मे अ॑ग्ने सं॒यद्वी॑रं बृ॒हंतं॑ क्षु॒मंतं॒ वाजं॑ स्वप॒त्यं र॒यिं दाः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> नु । ते । पूर्वस्य । अवसः । अधिइत् । तृतीये । विदथे । मन्म । शंसि ।
> अस्मे इति । अग्ने । संयत्वीरं । बृहंतं । क्षुमंतं । वाजं । सुअपत्यं ।
> रयिं । दाः ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने ते तव संबंधिनः पूर्वस्य पूर्वं यागसमये कृतस्यावसोऽभि-
> मततर्पणस्याधीतौ स्मरणे सति तत्सृत्या नु अद्यापि तृतीये विदथे यागे तृतीय-
> सवने । यद्वा प्रातरनुवाकसंबंधिनामाग्नेयोषस्याश्विनानां मध्येऽन्यतमे
> तृतीये क्रत् मौन्मननीयं स्तोत्रं शंसि । आशंसि । शस्यतेऽस्माभिः । हे अग्ने त्वं
> चास्मे अस्मभ्यं संयद्वीरं संयतो वीरा यस्मिन् तादृशं बृहंतं महांतं
> क्षुमंतं शब्दवंतं कीर्तिमंतं वाजमुक्तलक्षणमन्नं स्वपत्यं रयिं च दाः । देहि ॥

*Gist:* Recalling past praises, we recite a hymn at the third pressing; Agni is asked to give us heroic, great, famous food, good offspring and wealth.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). ते—निनगॆ संबंधिसिदुदू (*te—ninagè saṃbaṃdhisidudū*) (belonging to you). पूर्वस्य—हिंदिन सवनद कालदल्लि पठिसिदुदू (*pūrvasya—hiṃdina savanada kāladalli paṭhisidudū*) (recited at the time of the earlier pressing). अवसः—निनगॆ तृप्तियन्नुंटुमाडिदुदू आद (*avasaḥ—ninagè tṛptiyannuṃṭumāḍidudū āda*) (which gave you satisfaction). अधीतौ—स्तुतियन्नु अनुसरिसि (*adhītau—stutiyannu anusarisi*) (following the praise). नु—ईगलू कूड (*nu—īgalū kūḍa*) (even now). तृतीये विदथे—तृतीय सवनद कालदल्लि (*tṛtīye vidathe—tṛtīya savanada kāladalli*) (at the time of the third pressing). मन्म—मननीयवाद स्तुतियु (*manma—mananīyavāda stutiyu*) (a hymn worthy of reflection). शंसि—पठिसल्पडुत्तदॆ (*śaṃsi—paṭhisalpaḍuttadè*) (is recited). अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). अस्मे—नमगॆ (*asme—namagè*) (to us). संयद्वीरं—वीर रिंद कूडिदुदू (*saṃyadvīraṃ—vīra riṃda kūḍidudū*) (accompanied by heroes (the word is divided by a line break)). बृहंतं—महत्तादुदू (*bṛhaṃtaṃ—mahattādudū*) (great). क्षुमंतं—कीर्तियन्नु हरडतक्कद्दू आद (*kṣumaṃtaṃ—kīrtiyannu haraḍatakkaddū āda*) (spreading fame). वाजं—अन्नवन्नू (*vājaṃ—annavannū*) (food). स्वपत्यं—श्रेष्ठवाद संततियन्नू (*svapatyaṃ—śreṣṭhavāda saṃtatiyannū*) (excellent offspring). रयिं—धनवन्नु (*rayiṃ—dhanavannu*) (wealth). दाः—कॊडु (*dāḥ—kòḍu*) (give).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, following the praise which belongs to you, which was recited for you at the time of the earlier pressing and which gave you satisfaction, even now a hymn worthy of reflection is recited at the time of the third pressing (the sentence continues on the next page)

### Printed p. 487

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ. ५. व. २५. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 487 (*[a. 2. a. 5. va. 25. ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 487*).*

...O Agni, give us food that is accompanied by heroes, great and spreading fame, excellent offspring and wealth. (The print has a misprint for the word "recited" in the first part of the Bhāvārtha.)

**Printed English translation**

Verily your praise has been recited (by us) at the third (daily) sacrifice, as it was in the repetition of your first propitiation : give us, Agni, ample and notorious food, posterity, riches, such as may be the support of numerous dependants.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 8)**

Addressing Agni: remembering the praises and the like pleasing to Agni that the sacrificers and priests have performed from the time the sacrifice began until now, तृतीये विदथे (*tṛtīye vidathe*)—at the third pressing; or यद्वा प्रातरनुवाकसंबंधिनां आग्नेयोषस्याश्विनानां मध्यॆ तृतीयक्रत् (*yadvā prātaranuvākasaṃbaṃdhināṃ āgneyoṣasyāśvinānāṃ madhyè tṛtīyakrat*) (as printed), at the time of performing sacrifices: among the three kinds of mantras connected with the morning anuvāka recited in the morning, अग्नेयक्रतु, उषस्य कत्तु आश्विनिक्रतु (*agneyakratu, uṣasya kattu āśvinikratu*) (as printed), the hymns and the like recited in the third, a different rite, are recited by us. The wish is expressed that Agni may listen to these hymns. From this it is described that the sacrificers pray: संयद्वीरं (*saṃyadvīraṃ*), sons who subdue heroes, बृहंतं क्षुमंतं वाजं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ kṣumaṃtaṃ vājaṃ*), abundant food, fame and wealth, may Agni grant.

### Printed p. 488

*Running head (as supplied): [488 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. अ. १. सू. ४] (*[488 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. 4]*).*

*(Continuation of Ṛk 9 of Sūkta 4 of Maṇḍala 2: its bhāṣya follows the Pada of the previous page.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वया रक्षकेण वन्वंतश्चांदसं भजंतो गृत्समदा ऋषयः । आत्मनि
> परोक्ष्येण वचनं । यथा गुहा गुहायां वर्तमानानुपरान् उपरमणसाध-
> नान् उपरि उत्कृष्टे वर्तमानान्ता धनविशेषानभिस्युः । अभिभवेयुः । स्वाधीनान्
> कुर्युः । यद्वा गूढानुपरान् उपरेऽधिकत्वेन वर्तमानान्मापानभिस्युः । अभिभ-
> वेयुः । तथा कुर्वित्यर्थः । कीदृशाः । सुवीरासः । शोभनपुत्राद्युपेताः । अभि.
> मातिसहः । वैरिणां पापादीनां सोढारः । किंच सूरिभ्यो मेधाविभ्यो यज-
> मानेभ्यो गृणते ॥ व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । शब्दयद्भ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः । यद्वा सूरिभ्यो
> यजमानेभ्यो गृणते स्तोत्रे च स्मत् सुमत् अतिप्रभूतं तत् तादृशं प्रसिद्धं
> वयोऽन्नं धाः । धेहि ॥

*Gist:* May the Gṛtsamadas, praising Agni, with his help win hidden treasures and become heroic and enemy-subduing; Agni is asked to give food to praisers.

*(The bhāṣya contains short grammatical remarks on the change of number and on the Vedic usage; they are transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने—ऎलै अग्निये (*agne—èlai agniye*) (O Agni). वन्वंतः—निन्नन्नु स्तुतिसि भजिसुव (*vanvaṃtaḥ—ninnannu stutisi bhajisuva*) (those who praise and serve you). गृत्समदासः—गृत्समद ऋषिगळु (*gṛtsamadāsaḥ—gṛtsamada ṛṣigaḷu*) (the Gṛtsamada seers). त्वया—रक्षकनाद निन्न सहायदिंद (*tvayā—rakṣakanāda ninna sahāyadiṃda*) (with the help of you, the protector). यथा—याव रीतियल्लि (*yathā—yāva rītiyalli*) (in which manner). गुहा—गुहॆयल्लि गूढवागिरतक्क (*guhā—guhèyalli gūḍhavāgiratakka*) (hidden in a cave). उपरान्—उत्कृष्टवाद धनगळन्नु (*uparān—utkṛṣṭavāda dhanagaḷannu*) (the excellent treasures). अभि स्युः—हॊंदुवरो अदरंतॆयू (मत्तु) (*abhi syuḥ—hòṃduvaro adaraṃtèyū (mattu)*) (they obtain, so (and)). सुवीरासः—श्रेष्ठराद वीरपुत्ररिरुवंतॆयू (*suvīrāsaḥ—śreṣṭharāda vīraputrariruvaṃtèyū*) (as having excellent heroic sons). अभिमातिसहः—शत्रुगळन्नु सदॆबडियुव शक्तिवंतरागिरुवंतॆयू माडु (*abhimātisahaḥ—śatrugaḷannu sadèbaḍiyuva śaktivaṃtarāgiruvaṃtèyū māḍu*) (as able to crush enemies, make (us) so). सूरिभ्यः—यज्ञकर्तरिगागि (*sūribhyaḥ—yajñakartarigāgi*) (for the sacrificers). गृणते—स्तुतियन्नु पठिसतक्क स्तोतृगळिगॆ (*gṛṇate—stutiyannu paṭhisatakka stotṛgaḷigè*) (for the praisers who recite praise). स्मत्—अतिप्रभूतवादुदू (*smat—atiprabhūtavādudū*) (abundant). तत्—प्रसिद्धवादुदू आद (*tat—prasiddhavādudū āda*) (well-known). वयः— अन्नवन्नु (*vayaḥ— annavannu*) (food). धाः—कॊडु. (*dhāḥ—kòḍu.*) (give).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, make the Gṛtsamada seers who praise and serve you, with the help of you, the protector, obtain excellent treasures hidden in a cave, and be endowed with excellent heroic sons and able to crush their enemies. Give to the praisers, who recite hymns for the sacrificers, abundant and well-known food. (The print has a misprint for the first word, "O".)

**Printed English translation**

By you (Agni), may the Gritsamadas, repeating your praise, become masters of the precious secret (treasures); so that they may be possessed of excellent dependants, and be able to resist (their) enemies, and do you give to (your) pious worshippers, and to him who glorifies (you), such (abundant) food.

### Printed p. 489

*Running head (as supplied): [आ २. आ ५. व. २६. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 489 (*[ā 2. ā 5. va. 26. ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 489*).*

*[As supplied, the label line of the Special Topics reads विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*); standard label inserted.]*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 9)**

वन्वंतः (*vanvaṃtaḥ*)—छांदसं भजंतो गृत्समदा ऋषयः (*chāṃdasaṃ bhajaṃto gṛtsamadā ṛṣayaḥ*): it is explained that these are the seers, Gṛtsamada and others, his descendants or relatives, who have become worthy of Agni's grace and pursue the study of the Veda. Here the seer of the mantra, Gṛtsamada himself, speaks with reference to himself, his own people and the people of his line.

यथा गुहा उपर्ना अभि स्युः (*yathā guhā uparnā abhi syuḥ*)—गुहायां वर्धमान्ना उपरि वर्तमान्ना वा धनविशेषान् स्वाधीन्ना कुर्युः । यद्वा गूढान् अधिकत्वेन वर्तमान्ना पापा अभिभवेयुः तथा कुरु । (*guhāyāṃ vardhamānnā upari vartamānnā vā dhanaviśeṣān svādhīnnā kuryuḥ | yadvā gūḍhān adhikatvena vartamānnā pāpā abhibhaveyuḥ tathā kuru |*) (as printed, with several garbled forms): addressing Agni, one kind of prayer is explained, that the wealth which is hidden away in caves (in a lonely or secret place) or which lies on the surface of the earth may come under the control of us, the seers, who live by the study of the Veda alone, through his grace. The second kind: the prayer for Agni's grace is expressed that we may have the strength by which the hidden and abundant sins that we have committed secretly, so that no one knows, may be destroyed.

सूरिभ्यः गृणते (*sūribhyaḥ gṛṇate*)—मेधाविभ्यः यजमानेभ्यः यद्वा सूरिभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः (*medhāvibhyaḥ yajamānebhyaḥ yadvā sūribhyaḥ stotṛbhyaḥ*): Yāska has read the word for "wise" among the names of praise (नि. ३-१९ (*ni. 3-19*)). Here two kinds of meaning are given for it, "for the priests who recite praise" or "for the wise sacrificers", and Agni is prayed to give abundant sons, wealth, food and the like.

#### Sūkta 5 (Maṇḍala 2)

ऐदनॆय सूक्तवु. (*aidanèya sūktavu.*) ("the fifth sūkta").

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (introduction)

> होताजनिष्टेत्यष्टर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं सोमाहुतेरार्षमाग्नेयमानु-
> ष्टुभं। होताष्टावानुष्टुभमित्यनुत्यनुक्रांतं॥ प्रातरनुवाकाशिनशस्त्रयोराग्नेये
> क्रतावस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रितं च । अग्नायो होताजनिष्ट । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥ चतु-
> र्विंशेऽहन्यपीदमेवाज्यं । चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्टेत्याज्यं । आ. ७-२ । इति ॥ अभि-
> प्लविके द्वितीयेऽहनीदमेवाज्यं । द्वितीयस्य चतुर्विंशेनाज्यं । आ. ७-६ ।
> इत्यतिदिष्टत्वात् ॥

*Gist:* The fifth sūkta has eight ṛks, seer Somāhuti, deity Agni, Anuṣṭubh metre; used in the morning litany and Āśvina śastra, and in the twenty-four-day rite.

### Printed p. 490

*Running head (as supplied): [490 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २. अ. १. सू. ५] (*[490 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū. 5]*).*

**Anuvāda (Kannada)** of Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 5 of Maṇḍala 2. This sūkta beginning होताजनिष्ट (*hotājaniṣṭa*) is the fifth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Somāhuti is the seer of this sūkta; Agni is the deity; the metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said होताष्टावानुष्टुभं (*hotāṣṭāvānuṣṭubhaṃ*). That this sūkta is used for the ṛks connected with the Āgneya rite at the time of reciting the morning anuvāka and the Āśvina śastra mantras is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अग्नायो होताजनिष्ट (*agnāyo hotājaniṣṭa*) (आ. ४-१३ (*ā. 4-13*)); and that in a special sacrifice performed over twenty-four days this sūkta is used for the ājya-hotra on the twenty-fourth day is explained by the sūtra चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्टेत्याज्यं (*caturviṃśe hotājaniṣṭetyājyaṃ*) (आ. ७-२ (*ā. 7-2*)), and that this sūkta should be recited for the ājya-hotra on the second day of the Abhiplava sacrifice by the sūtra द्वितीयस्य चतुर्विंशेनाज्यं (*dvitīyasya caturviṃśenājyaṃ*) (आ. ७-६ (*ā. 7-6*)).

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> होता होमनिष्पादकश्चेतनश्चतयितास्मदनुष्ठितस्य पिता पालकोऽस्मद्यज्ञस्य
> ईदृशोग्निरजनिष्ट । उत्पन्नः । किमर्थं । पितृभ्यः पालकेभ्यो यजमानेभ्यः ॥
> षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी ॥ तेषामूतये रक्षणाय च । वयं च वाजिनो हविर्लक्षणान्न-
> वंतः संतः प्रयक्षं प्रकर्षण पूज्यं जेन्यं जीतव्यं यमं यमयितव्यं वसु
> धनं शकेम । शक्ता भूयास्म लब्धुमिति शेषः । यद्वा वाजिनोऽन्नस्य यमं
> यमनं कर्तुं शकेम । प्रयक्षं जेन्यं वसु धनमित्युपमानं । उक्तलक्षणं धनमिव ।
> तद्यथावरोद्दुं शक्नुमस्तद्वत् ॥

*Gist:* Agni, hotṛ, instigator and protector of our rite, is born to protect the sacrificers; with food offered may we win worshipful, conquerable, controllable wealth.

*[In the supplied text a word of the bhāṣya for the sixth case was printed with Devanagari letters for its conjuncts inside the Kannada text; it is rewritten letter for letter as Kannada, as noted in the Kannada text. The bhāṣya contains short grammatical remarks; they are transcribed in the block and not explained.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

होता—होमसंपादकनू (*hotā—homasaṃpādakanū*) (the accomplisher of homa). चेतनः—(नम्म अनुष्ठानगळिगॆ) चैतन्यवन्नुंटुमाडु ववनू (*cetanaḥ—(namma anuṣṭhānagaḷigè) caitanyavannuṃṭumāḍu vavanū*) (one who animates (our rites) (the word is divided by a line break)). पिता—नम्म यज्ञद पालकनू आद अग्नियु (*pitā—namma yajñada pālakanū āda agniyu*) (the protector of our sacrifice, Agni). पितृभ्यः—यज्ञकर्तर (*pitṛbhyaḥ—yajñakartara*) (of the sacrificers). ऊतये— रक्षणॆगागि (*ūtaye— rakṣaṇègāgi*) (for the protection). अजनिष्ट—उत्पन्ननागिद्दानॆ (*ajaniṣṭa—utpannanāgiddānè*) (he has been born). (वयं—नावू सह) (*(vayaṃ—nāvū saha)*) ((we also)). वाजिनः—हविस्सिन रूपद अन्नवंतरागि (*vājinaḥ—havissina rūpada annavaṃtarāgi*) (possessing food in the form of oblation). प्रयक्षं—अतिशयवागि पूज्यवादुदू (*prayakṣaṃ—atiśayavāgi pūjyavādudū*) (exceedingly worshipful). जेन्यं—जेतव्यवादुदू (*jenyaṃ—jetavyavādudū*) (to be won). यमं— नम्म नियमदल्लिरतक्कद्दू आद (*yamaṃ— namma niyamadalliratakkaddū āda*) (within our control). वसु—धनवन्नु (*vasu—dhanavannu*) (wealth). शकेम—हॊंदुवंतागलि. (*śakema—hòṃduvaṃtāgali.*) (may we obtain).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Agni, the accomplisher of homa, the giver of vitality to us, the protector of our sacrifice, has been born for the protection of the sacrificers. May we also, possessing food in the form of oblation, worship Agni and obtain wealth that is exceedingly worshipful and within our control.

**Printed English translation**

An invoker (of the gods), our instructor and protector, has heen [sic] born for the preservation of our patrons ; may we, possessed of (sacrificial) food be able to acquire worshipful, conquerable, and manageable riches.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1)**

चेतनः— चेतॆयिता अस्मदनुष्ठितस्य । (*cetanaḥ— cetèyitā asmadanuṣṭhitasya |*) (as printed): one who is the impeller of the sacrificial rites and the like that we perform or are performing; that is, one who gives us the power and capacity to accomplish them.

पिता (*pitā*): Sāyaṇa has explained that this word, formed from the root meaning "to protect", means "protector". Yāska, having cited the ṛk (cited in the next lines) ... (the sentence continues on the next page)

### Printed p. 492

*Running head (as supplied): [492 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २. अ.१ . सू.५] (*[492 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2. a.1 . sū.5]*).*

दौर्मे पिता जनिता नाभिरत्र बंधुर्मे माता पृथिवी महीयं । (*daurme pitā janitā nābhiratra baṃdhurme mātā pṛthivī mahīyaṃ |*)
उत्तानयोश्चन्वो ३ र्योनिरंतरत्रा पिता दुहितुर्गर्भमाधात् ॥ (*uttānayoścanvo 3 ryoniraṃtaratrā pitā duhiturgarbhamādhāt ‖*)

(म. सं. १-१६४-३३ (*ma. saṃ. 1-164-33*)) (as printed; the first abbreviation is a misprint) (rendered loosely: heaven is my father, the begetter; here is the navel, the bond; my kinsman is my mother, this great earth; of the two upturned bowls the womb is in between; there the father placed the embryo of the daughter), has said of the word पिता (*pitā*) there: पाता ना पालयिता ना (*pātā nā pālayitā nā*) (as printed), "protector or preserver" or "guardian" (नि. ४-२१ (*ni. 4-21*)); and, having cited the ṛk

उदीरतामवर उत्परास उन्मध्यमाः पितरः सोम्यासः । (*udīratāmavara utparāsa unmadhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ |*)
असुं य ईयुरवृका ऋतज्ञास्ते नोऽवन्नु पितरो हवेषु ॥ (*asuṃ ya īyuravṛkā ṛtajñāste no 'vannu pitaro haveṣu ‖*)

(ऋ, सं. १०-१५-१ (*ṛ, saṃ. 10-15-1*)) (rendered loosely: may the lower, the higher and the middle Fathers, the Soma-drinkers, rise; may those unharmed, truth-knowing Fathers who have attained life protect us in the invocations), he has given the meaning "Pitṛ deities" for the word पितरः (*pitaraḥ*) in it (नि. ११-१८ (*ni. 11-18*)). Sāyaṇa has explained both words पिता (*pitā*) and पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*) in the present ṛk with the meaning "protector", applying "protector" to Agni and "the protecting sacrificers" to the sacrificers. Although the meaning "protector" given by Sāyaṇa for the word पिता (*pitā*) suits Agni, there is no objection to giving for पितृभ्यः (*pitṛbhyaḥ*) the meaning "for (the protection of) the Pitṛ deities" rather than "for the sacrificers". The scholar Wilson (the name in Latin letters in the Kannada text) has approved the meaning "Pitṛ deities" itself.

वाजिनः—हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतः । (*vājinaḥ—havirlakṣaṇānnavaṃtaḥ |*) The word वाजः (*vājaḥ*) is read among the twenty-eight names of food (नि. ३-९ (*ni. 3-9*)) (the print has a misspelt word for "read"); वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*) means those accompanied by food, or those who have the food in the form of oblation prepared to offer to Agni.

जेन्यं वसु (*jenyaṃ vasu*)—वसु (*vasu*) means wealth. This wealth should be worthy of being won by us; that is, it should be such that, subduing the enemies, we win their wealth and bring it under our control. Agni is prayed that we may be able to obtain such wealth.

In this ṛk and in the following ṛks Agni is addressed and praised as the priests who take part in the sacrifice: the hotṛ, the netṛ, the praśāstṛ, the neṣṭṛ, the adhvaryu and the rest. In the present ṛk, praising Agni as होता (*hotā*) (one who invokes the gods at the sacrifice) or होमनिष्पादकः (*homaniṣpādakaḥ*) (one who accomplishes the homa), it is described that Agni, of such greatness, has been born (for our sacrifice, in the fire-sticks).

#### Ṛk 2

*[One reading of the Saṃhitā is marked with a query, as it differs from the Pada.]*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ यस्मि॑न्त॒प्त र॒श्मय॑स्त॒ता य॒ज्ञस्य॑ ने॒तरि॑ ।
> म॒नु॒ष्वद्दैव्य॑मष्ट॒मं पोता॒ विश्वं॒ तदि॑न्वति ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । यस्मिन् । सप्त । रश्मयः । तताः । यज्ञस्य । नेतरि ।
> मनुष्वत् । दैव्यं । अष्टमं । पोता । विश्वं । तत् । इन्वति ॥ २ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> यज्ञस्य नेतरि यागस्य निर्वाहके यस्मिन्नग्नौ सप्त रश्मयः सप्तसंख्याका रश्मि-
> वद्वाप्ता होत्रका आतताः । स्वस्वकर्मभिः सर्वतो व्याप्ता भवंति । स पोता
> पावको देवानां प्रोत्राख्य ऋत्विग्रूपो वाग्निर्मनुष्वत् मनुष्यपोतृवत्
> दैव्यं । देवो यज्ञः । तत्संबंध्यष्टममष्टर्त्विक्संबंधि तद्विश्वं कर्तव्यजातं सप्त
> होत्रकैः सह स्वयमष्टमः सन् इन्वति । व्याप्नोति । यद्वा तदित्यस्य लिंगव्यत्ययः। स
> पोतेति संबंधः । सप्तहोत्रकैः सहाष्टमो भूत्वा तद्विद्यज्ञं निर्वहतीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* In Agni, the leader of the sacrifice, the seven hotṛ-rays are spread; as the divine potṛ he, as eighth, accomplishes the whole rite.

*(The bhāṣya contains a short grammatical remark on the change of gender; it is transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यज्ञस्य नेतरि—यज्ञक्कॆ नेतृवाद (निर्वाहकनाद) (*yajñasya netari—yajñakkè netṛvāda (nirvāhakanāda)*) (in the leader (manager) of the sacrifice). यस्मिन्—याव अग्नियल्लि (*yasmin—yāva agniyalli*) (in which Agni). सप्त रश्मयः—(सप्तरश्मिरूपदल्लिरुव) सप्तसंख्याकराद होतृगळू (*sapta raśmayaḥ—(saptaraśmirūpadalliruva) saptasaṃkhyākarāda hotṛgaḷū*) (the seven hotṛs in the form of the seven rays). आ तताः—तम्म तम्म कर्तव्यगळॊडनॆ सर्वत्र व्यापिसिद्दारॆयो अंतह (*ā tatāḥ—tamma tamma kartavyagaḷòḍanè sarvatra vyāpisiddārèyo aṃtaha*) (have spread everywhere with their respective duties, such). पोता—(देवतॆगळिगॆ) पोतृवॆंब ऋत्विक्काद अग्नियु (*potā—(devatègaḷigè) potṛvèṃba ṛtvikkāda agniyu*) (Agni, the priest called potṛ (for the gods)). मनुष्वत्—मानव ऋक्कुगळल्लि ऒब्बनाद पोतृविनंतॆ (*manuṣvat—mānava ṛkkugaḷalli òbbanāda potṛvinaṃtè*) (like the potṛ, one of the human priests). दैव्यं—देवतात्मवाद यज्ञदल्लि (*daivyaṃ—devatātmavāda yajñadalli*) (in the divine sacrifice). अष्टमं—(उळिद एळु ऋत्विक्कुगळॊडनॆ) सेरि ऎंटनॆय ऋत्विक्कागि (*aṣṭamaṃ—(uḷida eḷu ṛtvikkugaḷòḍanè) seri èṃṭanèya ṛtvikkāgi*) (joining the other seven priests as the eighth priest). तत् विश्वं— समस्तवाद कर्तव्यवन्नु (*tat viśvaṃ— samastavāda kartavyavannu*) (the whole duty). इन्वति—व्यापिसुत्तानॆ. (निर्वहिसुत्तानॆ) (*invati—vyāpisuttānè. (nirvahisuttānè)*) (he pervades (he accomplishes)).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

In Agni, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the seven hotṛs, in the form of seven rays, are spread everywhere with their respective duties. That Agni, the divine potṛ, accomplishes the whole duty of the sacrifice, like a human potṛ.

### Printed p. 494

*Running head (as supplied): [494 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २ अ. १. सू. ५] (*[494 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2 a. 1. sū. 5]*).*

*(Continuation of Ṛk 2 of Sūkta 5 of Maṇḍala 2: its printed English and Special Topics follow the Bhāvārtha of the previous page.)*

**Printed English translation**

In whom, as conductor of the sacrifice, the seven rays are manifested and who, as a human Potri, officiates in the eighth place to perfect every divine (rite).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 2)**

नेतरि—यागस्य निर्वाहके यस्मिन्नग्नौ । (*netari—yāgasya nirvāhake yasminnagnau |*) The commentator's meaning is "in the Agni who accomplishes the sacrifice". In this ṛk it is said that Agni performs the duty of the priests called the netṛ and the potṛ.

सप्त रश्मयस्तता—सप्तसंख्याका रश्मिवद्वाप्ता होत्रका आ तताः । स्वस्वकर्मभिः सर्वतो व्याप्ता भवंति । (*sapta raśmayastatā—saptasaṃkhyākā raśmivadvāptā hotrakā ā tatāḥ | svasvakarmabhiḥ sarvato vyāptā bhavaṃti |*) The meaning is that the seven hotṛs, who are like seven rays or like the seven flames of Agni, gather around Agni and engage in their respective sacrificial duties. Who the seven hotṛs are here: as the commentator said earlier, four hotṛs of the hotṛ group and three priests of the Brahmā group, seven in all, engage in the homa rite: such is the purport. Yāska, in the explanation of the ṛk

दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि व्रते राजाना मित्रावरुणा निवाससि । (*dakṣasya vādite janmani vrate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā nivāsasi |*)
अतूर्तपंथाः पुरुरथो आर्यमा सप्तहोता विषुरूपेषु जन्मसु ॥ (*atūrtapaṃthāḥ pururatho āryamā saptahotā viṣurūpeṣu janmasu ‖*)

(म. सं. १०-६४-५ (*ma. saṃ. 10-64-5*)) (as printed; the first abbreviation is a misprint; the verse names Aryaman as the one with seven hotṛs), has explained the word for "seven hotṛs" as the seven rays of Agni:

सप्तहोता सप्तास्मै रश्मयो रसानभिसन्नामयंति । सप्तैनमृषयः स्तुवंतीति वा । (*saptahotā saptāsmai raśmayo rasānabhisannāmayaṃti | saptainamṛṣayaḥ stuvaṃtīti vā |*)

(नि. ११-२३ (*ni. 11-23*)) (a line-end hyphen inside it is joined) (rendered loosely: "Saptahotṛ": his seven rays bring to him the saps; or the seven seers praise him). That is, he has explained that Agni has the name "of seven hotṛs" because Agni's rays (flames) are seven, or because the seven seers praise this Agni. In the present ṛk the purport is the seven hotṛs, like seven rays, or the seven priests.

मनुष्यत् दैव्यं अष्टमं पोता विश्वं तत् इन्वति (*manuṣyat daivyaṃ aṣṭamaṃ potā viśvaṃ tat invati*) (as printed): in this sentence of the second half the meaning is explained that Agni, with the seven priests mentioned above, becomes the eighth priest, the potṛ, in the sacrifice performed by men and himself helps to accomplish the sacrificial rite.

*[A stray ornament line of the supplied text, in a script other than Kannada, is kept as an italic note in the Kannada text.]*

*(The bhāṣya contains short grammatical remarks; they are transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

वा—अथवा (*vā—athavā*) (or). ईं अनु—ई यज्ञवन्नु उद्देशिसि (*īṃ anu—ī yajñavannu uddeśisi*) (with reference to this sacrifice). यत्—याव हविस्सुगळन्नु (*yat—yāva havissugaḷannu*) (which oblations). दधन्वे—(अध्वर्वादिगळु) अर्पिसुवरो मत्तु (*dadhanve—(adhvarvādigaḷu) arpisuvaro mattu*) ((the adhvaryu and others) offer, and). ब्रह्माणि—याव शस्त्रादियाद मंत्रगळन्नु (*brahmāṇi—yāva śastrādiyāda maṃtragaḷannu*) (which hymns of praise and the like). वोचत्—(होत्रादिगळु) पठिसुवरो (*vocat—(hotrādigaḷu) paṭhisuvaro*) ((the hotṛ and others) recite). तत्—आ ऎल्लवन्नू सह (*tat—ā èllavannū saha*) (all that also). वेरु—अग्नियु तिळिदे इरु त्तानॆ (अपेक्षिसुत्तानॆ ई अग्नियु) (*veru—agniyu tiḷide iru ttānè (apekṣisuttānè ī agniyu)*) (Agni knows (he desires, this Agni) (the word is divided by a line break)). विश्वानि—समस्तवाद (*viśvāni—samastavāda*) (all). काव्या—ऋत्विक्कुगळ कर्मगळन्नु (*kāvyā—ṛtvikkugaḷa karmagaḷannu*) (the acts of the priests). नेमिः—चक्रद हॊरवलयवु (*nemiḥ—cakrada hòravalayavu*) (the rim of a wheel). चक्रं इव—चक्रवन्नु पूर्णवागि व्यापिसुवंतॆ (*cakraṃ iva—cakravannu pūrṇavāgi vyāpisuvaṃtè*) (as if pervading the wheel completely). परि अभवत्- पूर्णवागि व्यापिसिद्दानॆ (*pari abhavat- pūrṇavāgi vyāpisiddānè*) (he has pervaded completely).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Agni knows all the oblations that the adhvaryu and others offer for this sacrifice, and all the hymns that the hotṛ and others recite. As the rim of a wheel completely pervades the wheel, so Agni, desiring them, has pervaded all the rites of the priests.

### Printed p. 496

*Running head (as supplied): [496 सायणभाष्यसहिता [मं. २. अ. १ सू. ५.] (*[496 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [maṃ. 2. a. 1 sū. 5.]*).*

**Printed English translation**

Whatever (offerings the priest) presents, whatever prayers he recites, he, (Agni), knows them all : he comprehends all priestly acts, as the circumference (includes the spokes) of a wheel.

*(The printed English divides "circumference" by a line break and a hyphen, joined here.)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 3)**

In the previous ṛk it was said that Agni, like the hotṛ and other priests, himself engages in the accomplishment of the sacrifice. In this ṛk it is described that Agni himself, being in the respective priests in the respective part, himself accomplishes the work of all the priests.

वा ईं अनु दधन्वे (*vā īṃ anu dadhanve*): Agni himself, knowing all the oblations that the priests such as the adhvaryu offer in the sacrifice, makes the oblation in the form of the adhvaryu, and likewise ब्रह्माणि वोचत् तत् वेरु (*brahmāṇi vocat tat veru*): Agni knows the hymns of praise, the śastras and the like, recited by the priests of the hotṛ group, and recites them himself.

परि विश्वानि काव्या नेमिः चक्रमिव अभवत् (*pari viśvāni kāvyā nemiḥ cakramiva abhavat*): besides, Agni himself does, or is able to do, all the acts that the wise priests perform in the sacrifice. An illustration is given here: as the rim of a wheel (the band round the outer rim, "Tyre" as printed in English) pervades the wheel all round, that is, pervades the whole wheel, so Agni pervades all the rites performed in the sacrifice; that is, he himself takes part in all the sacrificial rites and accomplishes the sacrifice: such is the purport.

### Printed p. 497

*Running head (as supplied): [अ. २. अ ५ व. २६ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 497 (*[a. 2. a 5 va. 26 ] ṛgvedasaṃhitā 497*).*

*(Continuation of Ṛk 4 of Sūkta 5 of Maṇḍala 2: its bhāṣya follows the Pada of the previous page. As supplied, the label line of the bhāṣya reads सायणभ.षं (*sāyaṇabha.ṣaṃ*), inside the quoted block; standard label inserted.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> शुचिः स्वयं शोधकः प्रशास्ता देवानां एतन्नामक ऋत्विक् प्रशासिता वा
> यज्ञविघ्नानां शुचिना क्रतुना शोधकेनाग्निहोत्रादिकर्मणा साकं हि सहैवाजनि ।
> उत्पन्नः । जातमात्र एव शुद्धः सर्वस्य प्रशास्ता च सन्नग्निहोत्रादिनिर्वोढाभवदि-
> त्यर्थः । अस्याग्नेध्रुवा ध्रुवाणि फलपर्यवसायीानि व्रतानि कर्माणि विद्वान् जानन्
> यजमानो वया इव विस्तृताः शाखा इवानुरोहते । क्रमेणानुतिष्ठति ॥

*Gist:* Agni, regulator of the sacrifice, is born with the purifying rites; the wise sacrificer follows his rules in order, as branches spring from a stem.

*(The bhāṣya contains a short grammatical remark; it is transcribed in the block and not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

शुचिः—स्वयं शुद्धिकारकनू (*śuciḥ—svayaṃ śuddhikārakanū*) (pure, himself the purifier). प्रशास्ता—यज्ञद विघ्नगळन्नु नाशमाडुववनू (*praśāstā—yajñada vighnagaḷannu nāśamāḍuvavanū*) (the destroyer of the obstacles of the sacrifice). अथवा प्रशास्त्रनामकनाद ऋत्विक्कू आद अग्नियु (*athavā praśāstranāmakanāda ṛtvikkū āda agniyu*) (or the priest called the praśāstṛ, Agni (the two parts run together in the print)). शुचिना—शुद्धिकारकवाद (*śucinā—śuddhikārakavāda*) (of the purifying). क्रतुना साकं हि—अग्निहोत्रादि कर्मगळॊडनॆये (*kratunā sākaṃ hi—agnihotrādi karmagaḷòḍanèye*) (together with the rite, with agnihotra and the other rites). अजनि—उत्पन्ननादनु (*ajani—utpannanādanu*) (he was born). अस्य—ई अग्निय (*asya—ī agniya*) (of this Agni). ध्रुवा व्रता—फलपरवसायियाद कर्मगळन्नु (*dhruvā vratā—phalaparavasāyiyāda karmagaḷannu*) (the rites that lead to their fruit). विद्वान्—अरितिरुव यजमाननु (*vidvān—aritiruva yajamānanu*) (the sacrificer who knows). वया इव— विस्तृतवाद शाखॆगळंतॆ (*vayā iva— vistṛtavāda śākhègaḷaṃtè*) (like spreading branches). अनु रोहते—अग्निय मादरियन्ननुसरिसि क्रमवागि नॆरवेरिसुत्तानॆ. (*anu rohate—agniya mādariyannanusarisi kramavāgi nèraverisuttānè.*) (he performs in order, following the pattern of Agni).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Agni, himself the purifier and the destroyer of the obstacles of the sacrifice, was born together with the purifying rites such as agnihotra. The sacrificers who know the rites of this original Agni that lead to their fruit perform them following the pattern of Agni, as the branches of a tree spread following the original tree.

**Printed English translation**

The pure regulator (of the sacrifice) is born verily together with the holy act; the wise (worshipper) performs all his, (Agni's), prescribed rites in succession, as the branches spring (from a common stem).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 4)**

In this ṛk Agni is described as performing the work of the praśāstṛ. The प्रशास्ता (*praśāstā*) is one of the sixteen priests. The duty of this priest is to remove the obstacles that may occur in the sacrifice and make the sacrifice proceed completely. Therefore प्रशास्ता प्रशासिता वा यज्ञविघ्नानां शुचिना क्रतुना शोधकेनाग्निहोत्रादिकर्मणा (*praśāstā praśāsitā vā yajñavighnānāṃ śucinā kratunā śodhakenāgnihotrādikarmaṇā*): that is, he purifies the obstacles of the sacrifice by his command or by rites such as agnihotra, in the form of expiation, and makes the sacrifice go on. Therefore he is called the praśāstṛ: one who regulates (that the sacrifice must go on in this way) (the sentence continues on the next page; the stray line "[32] Vol. 14" at the end of the page is kept as a note in the Kannada text)

### Printed p. 498

*Running head (as supplied): [498 सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. २. अ. १. सू ५] (*[498 sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [ maṃ. 2. a. 1. sū 5]*).*

...one who rules, one who commands. It is described here that Agni was born in the form of such a priest.

An illustration is given here for the rites performed in the sacrifice. वया इव अनु रोहते (*vayā iva anu rohate*): as, when a tree grows, branches grow one above another round its trunk, so in the sacrifice, according to a systematic rule, as soon as one rite is done the next rite is performed. The purport is that the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice knows such rites of the nature of Agni's rules and performs them accordingly.

The word for "rite" (the Kannada word with its ending: the rite-word) has been read among the names of rites (नि. ३-२ (*ni. 3-2*)), and for it the meaning "intelligence" is also given in the same place: क्रतुं-कर्म वा प्रज्ञां वा (*kratuṃ-karma vā prajñāṃ vā*) (नि. २-२८ (*ni. 2-28*)); or the word is read among the eleven names of intelligence beginning with केतः (*ketaḥ*) (नि. ३-१३ (*ni. 3-13*)) (the print has a misspelt word for "beginning").

व्रता—वृतानि । (*vratā—vṛtāni |*) Rites, rules. व्रतमिति, कर्मनाम, वृणोतीति सतः (*vratamiti, karmanāma, vṛṇotīti sataḥ*): "vrata" means rite; since this rite (a rite of sin or of merit) always surrounds the doer of the rite, the rite is called vrata. Or:

इदमपीतरत् व्रतमेतस्मादेव निवृत्तिकर्म वारयतीति सतः । अन्नमपि व्रतमुच्यते यदा वृणोति शरीरं ॥ (*idamapītarat vratametasmādeva nivṛttikarma vārayatīti sataḥ | annamapi vratamucyate yadā vṛṇoti śarīraṃ ‖*)

(नि २-१३ (*ni 2-13*)). Besides, the rites of restraint such as yama and niyama are also called vrata; it applies to Vedic rites performed in the presence of Agni or to other rites. Therefore वारयतीति सतः (*vārayatīti sataḥ*): because it keeps away from men, in the rite of restraint, things such as women and the like that cause obstacles, it is called a vrata. And because food, as the support of the body, pervades the body and nourishes it, food too is called vrata: thus he has given the etymology of the word vrata.

> कु॒वित्ति॒सृभ्य॒ आ वरं॒ स्वसा॑रो॒ या इ॒दं य॒युः ॥ ५ ॥
